The people we commonly refer to as the Russian Mennonites came into being as a group in a way quite similar to that of us with an Anabaptist heritage. We sprang from the same areas of Europe, from much of the same teachings of early Anabaptism, and have both experienced many of the same temptations and pitfalls, though at different times and locations.

This article will not focus on the beginnings of the Russian Mennonites apart from a brief overview. The group first entered Russia upon the urgings of the Viceroy Potemkin, who came into authority over the area now known as Ukraine after its annexation by Russia in 1783. The area had been under his partial administration since 1774, and he was eager to populate the land with foreign settlers. The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia. The Mennonites in Danzig, Poland, were first approached with the offer of land, which would have appealed to them because they were routinely denied land ownership as a semi-persecuted people at that time. This offer came in August of 1786, and two brothers from the Danzig church were sent to survey the land and make arrangements for possible immigration.

The first immigration of 462 families began in 1788, and the “Old Colony” was established at Chortitza. They were afforded freedom of religion, exemption from military service, and the right to maintain their own schools and governances.

The Mennonites thrived in their new homeland. Although the first years were hard, partially due to the fact that mostly poorer families and those not in church leadership chose to resettle in Russia, the group soon began to transform the barren plains and steppes into rich agricultural communities. As the churches grew, so did their prosperity.

This period of relative peace lasted for over a century, until the late 1800s, when the Russian government, dissatisfied with the number of foreign settlements inside its borders, began applying pressure to many of the groups it had invited to settle its land some 100 years before. The Mennonites were not the only ones targeted, as many groups from various nations had established themselves in Russia. Steps taken against the Mennonites included pressure to participate in the armed forces as well as pressure to drop the German language that the communities had been using in favor of the Russian language. As these pressures increased, some Mennonites chose to flee the country in the 1870s. The majority, however, by now quite wealthy and affluent in comparison to their Russian peasant neighbors, chose to stay and weather the storm.

Unbeknownst to them, a full-scale revolution that would reshape Russia as a country was just around the corner. In 1917, the Bolsheviks came to power through the October Revolution, an event where the reigning tsar, or emperor, was deposed and exiled, and a new government was set up. A civil war broke out, and much of the fighting raged over the lands occupied by the Mennonites. Here, it is necessary to insert a brief history of the ideology of this new government.

The October Revolution and its subsequent change in government were fueled by a class war. As opposed to Nazi Germany, where a person could be arrested and killed for their race, in Russia, a person could and would be arrested for their class, for example, property ownership was seen as a crime against the people, and so the wealthier class of Russian peasants and farmers, those who most often owned property and employed the lower class of peasants, became an instant target a revolution that claimed to want to distribute all property and resources evenly amongst its citizenry.

By this time, the strong agricultural society of the Mennonites had transformed Ukraine into a breadbasket, its vast fields sown with wheat developed specifically by the Mennonites: Turkey Red Wheat. This hardy crop had made the Mennonite church quite wealthy, and their colonies had grown and flourished into villages of comfort and, at times, extravagance. This must have been a two-fold insult to the still impoverished peasants of Russia. Not only was there a large group of people in their midst that taught, spoke, and did their dealings in a language not of the Motherland, but these people also were wealthy beyond most peasants’ dreams.

It is, therefore, no surprise that when the kulaks, the wealthy class of peasants, came under persecution from the new government, the Mennonites were seen as the enemy of the people. As the civil war raged over Mennonite lands, villages were burnt and decimated, people executed or driven off, and livestock and grain plundered. Eventually, this period of fighting did come to an end, but for those few who survived the destruction, there was no reprieve to be found.

With the label of kulak and being generally defenseless, the Mennonites faced intense persecution. Religious services were rarely allowed, and the agricultural communities that had fed Russia and many others besides were collectivized and put under government control. Many of their churches ceased to exist entirely, although those in the east tended to last longer than the western villages.

Imagine then, to a people accustomed for generations to the favor and benevolence of material possessions and success, that all things material are stripped away. In a historical eye blink, the wealthy become the poor, and the favored become the hated. Even with a strong Christian faith, such a turn of events would shock and confuse.

But further tests were yet ahead for those who endured the first 25 years of the Soviet persecution. With the memory of their easy lives still fresh, the dawn of World War II brought a unique and enticing opportunity: the rise of a government that promoted the well-being of the German race, that valued those groups that could turn an empty prairie into a sprawling farm, that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.

And so, they embraced the invading Germans. We readers, who are blessed with the ability to see the end result of these people’s decisions, can certainly make a good guess at what the end result was of wholesale support for the Nazis, but we must remember the scenarios that these Mennonites found themselves in...it was not one that would have been easy to decipher and decide upon if it were to be judged by man’s knowledge.

And so it was that the descendants of those helpless believers who gave their bodies at the stake and sword aligned themselves with a worldly kingdom that promised to protect and provide for them. In exchange for an eternal heritage, they chose to hope that the might of the German army would win back their earthly heritage and riches, and it was in this might that they trusted, forming bands of men who fought alongside the Germans against their old neighbors.

History did not deviate from its course, and the German army was eventually beaten back to its own borders and then further, and yet further into German lands. Before this retreating army ran those that had looked to it for their deliverance.

The atrocities of the Soviet government against its citizens are well documented in various works, most famously in the Gulag Archipelago, a book written by a Russian officer who was accused of treason. That author, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, painted a terrible picture of the treatment and exile of those who had opposed the USSR. Amongst the imprisoned or executed millions described in his tomes, there lie the remnants of a people who began as we did, experienced the smile of prosperity as we do, and then, treasuring that prosperity, lost it in calamitous fashion. We would do well to consider the paths we choose, as the wise king of the Scriptures instructs us, lest we, too, fall in the pursuit of prosperity. “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).

Die mense wat ons algemeen as die Russiese Menoniete noem, het as ’n groep op ’n manier tot stand gekom wat baie soortgelyk is aan dié van ons met ’n Anabaptistiese erfenis. Ons het uit dieselfde gebiede van Europa ontstaan, uit baie van dieselfde leringe van die vroeë Anabaptisme, en ons het albei baie van dieselfde versoekings en slaggate ervaar, hoewel op verskillende tye en plekke.

Hierdie artikel sal nie op die begin van die Russiese Menoniete fokus nie, behalwe vir ’n kort oorsig. Die groep het eers Rusland binnegekom op versoek van die Visegraaf Potemkin, wat beheer oor die gebied wat nou as Oekraïne bekend staan gekry het ná die anneksasie deur Rusland in 1783. Die area was sedert 1774 onder sy gedeeltelike administrasie, en hy was gretig om die land met buitelandse setlaars te bevolk. Die inwoners van Nieu-Rusland, soos dit destyds genoem is, was meestal nomades en Kozakke, ’n semi-nomadiese groep wat in die steppe van Rusland teenwoordig was. Die Menoniete in Danzig, Pole, is eers genader met die aanbod van grond, wat vir hulle aantreklik sou wees omdat hulle daardie tyd gereeld verhoed is om grond te besit as ’n semi-vervolgde volk. Hierdie aanbod het in Augustus 1786 gekom, en twee broers van die Danzig-kerk is gestuur om die land te ondersoek en reëlings te tref vir moontlike immigrasie.

Die eerste immigrasie van 462 gesinne het in 1788 begin, en die “Oude Kolonie” is by Chortitza gestig. Hulle is vryheid van godsdiens, vrystelling van diens in die weermag, en die reg om hul eie skole en bestuursvorme te behou, toegestaan.

Die Menoniete het in hul nuwe tuisland gedy. Alhoewel die eerste jare moeilik was, deels omdat hoofsaaklik armer gesinne en dié wat nie in kerkleierskap was nie gekies het om na Rusland te herplaas, het die groep gou begin om die verlore vlaktes en steppe in ryk landbougemeenskappe te omskep. Namate die kerke gegroei het, het so ook hul welvaart.

Hierdie tydperk van relatiewe vrede het vir meer as ’n eeu geduur, tot laat 1800’s, toe die Russiese regering, ontevrede met die aantal buitelandse nedersettings binne sy grense, begin druk uitoefen op baie van die groepe wat die land ongeveer 100 jaar vroeër uitgenooi het om daar te kom woon. Die Menoniete was nie die enigstes wat geteiken is nie, aangesien baie groepe van verskeie nasies in Rusland gevestig het. Stappe teen die Menoniete het druk ingesluit om aan te sluit by die gewapende magte sowel as druk om die Duitse taal wat die gemeenskappe gebruik het te Laat vaar ten gunste van die Russiese taal. Namate hierdie druk toegeneem het, het sommige Menoniete in die 1870’s gekies om die land te verlaat. Die meerderheid, egter, wat teen hierdie tyd nogal ryk en welvarend was in vergelyking met hul Russiese boerbuurmanne, het gekies om te bly en die storm uit te staan.

Onbewus aan hulle was ’n volskaalse revolusie wat Rusland as ’n land sou hervorm, net om die hoek. In 1917 het die Bolsjewiste deur die Oktoberrevolusie aan bewind gekom, ’n gebeurtenis waar die heersende tsaar, of keiser, afgegradeer en verban is, en ’n nuwe regering ingestel is. ’n Burgeroorlog het uitgebreek, en baie van die gevegte het oor die lande gebrand waarvoor die Menoniete gewoon het. Hier is dit noodsaaklik om ’n kort geskiedenis van die ideologie van hierdie nuwe regering in te voeg.

Die Oktoberrevolusie en die daaropvolgende verandering in regering is aangedryf deur ’n klasoorlog. Anders as in Nazi-Duitsland, waar ’n persoon gearresteer en vermoor kon word vir hul ras, kon en sou ’n persoon in Rusland gearresteer word vir hul klas; byvoorbeeld eiendomsbesit is as ’n misdaad teen die volk beskou, en so het die rykere klas van Russiese boere en boerbesitters, dié wat dikwels eiendom besit en die laer klas boere in diens gehad het, ’n onmiddellike teiken van ’n revolusie geword wat beweer het dat dit alle eiendom en hulpbronne billik onder sy burgers wil verdeel.

Teen hierdie tyd het die sterk landbousamelewing van die Menoniete Oekraïne in ’n graanproduserende strook omskep, sy uitgestrekte lande ingeplant met koring spesifiek ontwikkel deur die Menoniete: Turkey Red-wes (Turkey Red Wheat). Hierdie taai gewas het die Menonitiese kerk nogal ryk gemaak, en hul kolonieë het gegroei en geblom in dorpe van gerief en soms weelde. Dit moes ’n dubbelslag-insult gewees het vir die nog steeds verarmde boere van Rusland. Nie net was daar ’n groot groep mense in hul midde wat in ’n taal gelei, gepraat en sake gedoen het wat nie die Moederland se taal was nie, maar hierdie mense was ook ryk bo meeste boere se drome uit.

Dit is dus geen verrassing dat toe die kulaks, die welgestelde klas boere, onder vervolging deur die nuwe regering gekom het, die Menoniete as die vyand van die volk gesien is nie. Terwyl die burgeroorlog oor Menonietlande woed, is dorpe afgebrand en verwoes, mense tereggestel of verdryf, en vee en graan geplunder. Uiteindelik het hierdie tydperk van gevegte tot ’n einde gekom, maar vir die weiniges wat die verwoesting oorleef het, was daar geen versagting te vind nie.

Met die etiket van kulak en algemeen ongeskik om hulself te verdedig, het die Menoniete intense vervolging in die gesig gestaar. Godsdienstige dienste is selde toegelaat, en die landbougemeenskappe wat Rusland en baie ander gevoed het, is gekollektiveer en onder staatsbeheer gestel. Baie van hul kerke het heeltemal opgehou bestaan, alhoewel dié in die ooste geneig was om langer te hou as die westelike dorpe.

Stel jou dus voor, aan ’n volk wat generasies lank gewoond was aan die guns en welwillendheid van materiële besittings en sukses, dat alle materiële dinge onttrek word. In ’n historiese oogwink word die rykes die armes, en die aangewesenes die gehates. Selfs met ’n sterk Christelike geloof sou so ’n ommekeer skok en verwarring veroorsaak.

Maar verdere beproewings was nog voorlê vir dié wat die eerste 25 jaar van die Sowjetvervolging deurstaan het. Met die herinnering aan hul maklike lewens nog vars, het die aanbreek van die Tweede Wêreldoorlog ’n unieke en aanloklike geleentheid gebring: die opkoms van ’n regering wat die welsyn van die Duitse ras bevorder het, wat daardie groepe waardeer het wat ’n leë prairie in ’n uitgestrekte plaas kon omskep, wat fel anti-Kommunisties was—vir hierdie geteisterde groep gelowiges moes dit ’n Godgesinde wonder gelyk het om hulle van hulle bloedige ballingskap te bevry.

En so het hulle die invalle Duitsers omhels. Ons lesers, wat die vermoë het om die eindresultaat van hierdie mense se besluite te sien, kan sekerlik ’n goeie raaiskoot maak oor wat die uitkoms was van massiewe ondersteuning vir die Natsionaliste, maar ons moet onthou die scenario’s waarin hierdie Menoniete hulself bevind het... dit was nie ’n situasie wat maklik te dekrypeer en te beslis sou wees as dit volgens menslike kennis beoordeel is nie.

En so het die nageslagte van daardie weerlose gelowiges wat hul liggame aan die stake en swaard gegee het, hulself verbind aan ’n wêreldse koninkryk wat belowe het om hulle te beskerm en vir hulle te voorsien. In ruil vir ’n ewige erfenis het hulle gekies om te hoop dat die mag van die Duitse leër hul aardse erfenis en rykdom sou herwin, en dit was op hierdie mag wat hulle vertrou het, met vorming van groepe mans wat langs die Duitsers geveg het teen hul ou bure.

Die geskiedenis het nie van koers verander nie, en die Duitse leër is uiteindelik teruggedring na sy eie grense en daarna verder, en steeds verder in Duitse gebiede. Voor hierdie terugtrekkende leër het diegene wat na hulle gekyk het vir hul verlossing, gevlug.

Die gruweldade van die Sowjetregering teen sy burgers is goed gedokumenteer in verskeie werke, die bekendste in die Gulag Archipelago, ’n boek geskryf deur ’n Russiese offisier wat van verraad beskuldig is. Daardie skrywer, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, het ’n verskriklike prentjie geskilder van die behandeling en ballingskap van dié wat die USSR teengestaan het. Tussen die gevangenes of tereggestelde miljoene wat in sy boeke beskryf word, lê die oorblyfsels van ’n volk wat begin het soos ons, die glimlag van welvaart ervaar het soos ons, en toe, dié welvaart koesterend, dit op ’n rampagtige wyse verloor het. Ons sou goed daaraan doen om die paaie wat ons kies, te oorweeg, soos die wyse koning van die Skrifte ons gebied, sodat ons nie ook val in die strewe na welvaart nie. “Bedink die gang van jou voete, en laat al jou paaie gevestig word” (Spreuke 4:26).

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.

Es invierno ya; la nieve caída
ha dejado los cielos fríos y claros;
por ramas sin hojas sopla el viento agudo,
y toda la tierra yace muerta y sombría.

Y sin embargo el amor de Dios no se retira;
su vida en el aire cortante respira;
su belleza pinta la aurora encarnada,
y viste cada rama con guirnaldas brillantes.

Y aunque afuera soplen los vientos agudos,
y los cielos estén fríos, y las heladas severas,
el hogar ahora cierra más su círculo,
y más cálida resplandece su luz interior.

Oh Dios, das el frío del invierno,
así como los gozosos rayos del verano,
nos envuelves con calor en tu amor,
y nos sostienes durante los días invernales de la vida.

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

Apa yang kita pikirkan ketika kita memikirkan istilah ‘gereja’? Kita hidup di zaman ketika ada banyak dan beraneka gereja. Jika satu gereja tidak cocok untukmu, ada gereja lain untuk dipilih. Sementara beberapa gereja mendorong umatnya untuk hidup bagi Allah dan orang lain alih-alih bagi diri mereka sendiri, gereja-gereja lain mempromosikan sebuah Injil yang mengatakan banyak uang dan kehidupan yang lebih baik sekarang adalah hasil mengikuti Kristus. Namun, masih ada gereja yang berusaha mengikuti apa yang dikatakan Alkitab—Sola scriptura (semata-mata kitab suci). Secara tradisional, gereja-gereja Anabaptis konservatif di Amerika telah berusaha berfungsi dengan cara demikian. Tetapi apakah itu berubah?

Kita hidup di masa ketika garis-garis dilintasi, kabur, dan membingungkan. Orang-orang tidak yakin apa yang benar dan apa yang tidak. Hari ini, pria dan wanita di seluruh dunia mencari jawaban dan solusi, tetapi ke mana mereka harus mencari?

Aku sedang berbicara dengan seorang pemuda yang bersaksi telah bertobat pada usia muda. Dia menghadiri gereja dengan setia dan dianggap cukup berbakat. Tetapi ada masalah—dia memiliki dosa yang masih tidak bisa dia kendalikan. Saat dia bergumul dengan Allah dan memohon kemenangan, dia mulai mendengar pesan yang berulang dari orang-orang yang mengaku Kristen lain, “Tidak ada yang sempurna!” “Kita semua punya masalah.” “Semua orang telah berbuat dosa!” Akhirnya, pemuda ini menerima dosanya sebagai hal yang normal. Dia membenarkannya karena tampaknya semua orang mengatakan mereka juga punya dosa, bahwa mereka tidak hidup dalam kemenangan penuh. Itu membawa pemuda ini ke tempat kehancuran total.

Apakah kita sedang memberitakan dan menerima sebuah Injil yang dikalahkan—sebuah injil yang tidak menawarkan pengampunan sepenuhnya dan kemenangan sepenuhnya? Banyak pemuda zaman ini bingung. Banyak orang di dunia sekarang tidak mengerti. Siapa pun bisa pergi ke gereja dan mencoba menjadi orang yang lebih baik. Tetapi bagaimana dengan Injil Yesus Kristus yang mahakuasa dan mengubah hidup?

Rasul Paulus berkata bahwa Yesus akan datang kembali untuk “...sebuah gereja yang mulia, tidak bercela atau kusut atau yang semacam itu; tetapi supaya ia kudus dan tidak bercacat” (Ef. 5:27). Dan Yesus sendiri berkata “...Engkaulah Petrus, dan di atas batu karang ini Aku akan mendirikan jemaat-Ku; dan alam maut tidak akan menguasainya” (Mat. 16:18).

Sebelum aku bertobat, aku jelas menjadi budak dosa, tetapi aku menginginkan kemenangan. Aku kecanduan narkoba dan alkohol, tetapi aku tidak menyukainya. Aku ingin bebas. Aku pergi ke konseling dan fasilitas rehabilitasi di seluruh Amerika, tetapi itu tidak berhasil. Aku tidak punya kuasa. Aku bisa berhenti selama beberapa hari atau bahkan beberapa minggu, lalu amarah dan depresi datang, dan aku kembali ke zat-zat itu. Suatu hari, aku berhadapan langsung dengan Sang Pencipta. Tangan Allah yang mahakuasa menggenggamku dan membuka mataku. Aku bertobat dari dosaku dan diberi lembaran baru dan hati yang bersih. Aku tidak pernah kembali lagi. Narkoba, alkohol, dan dua bungkus rokok sehari selesai—selamanya.

Aku hampir tidak percaya apa yang Allah lakukan. Kuasa Allah itu nyata. Aku tidak dapat mengatasinya sendiri, sebagaimana tak seorang pun dari kita dapat, tetapi Allah telah berjanji memberi kita kebebasan dari perhambaan dan hidup baru yang penuh kemenangan jika kita menyerahkan hidup kita kepada-Nya. Kemampuan untuk mengatasi kuasa dosa dan kemudian hidup dalam kemenangan inilah yang dicari dunia. Apakah kita percaya bahwa Allah dapat membebaskan kita bukan hanya dari penyalahgunaan zat tetapi juga dari amarah, keegoisan, kepahitan, keserakahan, dan kesombongan? Firman Allah berkata “Jika kita mengaku dosa kita, Ia adalah setia dan adil sehingga Ia akan mengampuni dosa kita dan menyucikan kita dari segala kejahatan” (1 Yoh. 1:9). Tak seorang pun tertarik pada Injil yang dikalahkan, tak seorang pun kecuali mereka yang hidup dalam kekalahan karena mereka telah memilih perkara dunia ini di atas Allah dan Firman-Nya.

Apakah kita bersedia memberi kesaksian tentang kuasa kebangkitan? Kita perlu memberitakan sebuah injil yang menyelamatkan orang sepenuhnya dari perhambaan dosa—selamanya. Kita harus berani dan yakin dalam iman kita supaya kita dapat memimpin orang kepada Sang Tuan.

Aku sedang memberi kesaksian kepada seorang pria ketika dia berkata dengan suara cukup keras, “Allah tidak nyata!” Mulut anak laki-lakiku yang berusia enam tahun ternganga, dan dia terkejut, “Ayah, dia baru saja berbohong!”

Anakku tidak perlu diyakinkan bahwa Allah itu nyata; dia mempercayainya dengan segenap hatinya. Dunia di luar sana perlu diyakinkan. Mereka perlu melihat sesuatu yang tidak dapat dijelaskan ilmu pengetahuan. Mereka perlu melihat sesuatu yang menentang segala kemungkinan.

Yang itu adalah hati yang benar-benar telah berubah. Petarung kini mengasihi musuh-musuhnya. Orang yang bermasalah dengan amarah kini mengasihi orang lain tanpa syarat. Keluarga yang hancur disembuhkan. Pendosa yang hina diampuni dan hidup dalam perubahan. Harapan, damai, kasih, dan kuasa diberikan dengan cuma-cuma kepada pria dan wanita yang tampaknya tidak punya harapan. “Orang buta menerima penglihatan mereka, orang lumpuh berjalan, orang kusta dibersihkan, orang tuli mendengar, orang mati dibangkitkan, dan orang-orang miskin diberitakan Injil” (Mat. 11:5).

Apakah kamu menjalani hidupmu sehingga dunia dapat melihat pekerjaan Allah itu praktis, efektif, dan nyata setiap hari? Berikut beberapa hal yang Gereja butuhkan di zaman kita untuk sekali lagi menarik orang yang hilang.

Kesiapan untuk menderita

Sejarah menunjukkan bahwa gereja, sepanjang zaman, telah menderita karena Kristus. Itu adalah bagian dari biaya mengikuti Kristus. Alkitab berkata, “Memang, semua orang yang mau hidup saleh di dalam Kristus Yesus akan menderita penganiayaan” (2 Tim. 3:12). Itu sesuatu yang memang terjadi.

Hari ini, banyak orang menginginkan impian Amerika. Orang hidup bermoral baik, menjadi warga negara yang baik, menghasilkan nafkah yang baik, dan pergi ke gereja pada hari Minggu. Tetapi apakah itu yang kita dipanggil untuk lakukan? Injil menyebar seperti api ketika gereja menderita penganiayaan dan melakukannya dengan rela dan gembira. Itu sesuatu yang belum pernah dilihat dunia—sebuah iman yang ditunjukkan orang melalui hidup mereka, dan kematian mereka adalah sesuatu yang layak untuk mati karenanya. Marilah kita tidak takut menderita karena Kristus hari ini.

Penantangan diri

Kemudian kata Yesus kepada murid-murid-Nya, “Jika seseorang ingin datang mengikuti Aku, ia harus menyangkal dirinya sendiri dan memikul salibnya dan mengikut Aku” (Mat. 16:24).

Pernahkah kamu bertanya-tanya mengapa Yesus menginstruksikan kita untuk menyangkal diri? Lagi pula, Dia memberi kita keinginan dan hasrat, jadi mengapa harus kita menyangkalnya? Aku pernah mendengar orang mengatakan bahwa kita perlu menyelaraskan kehendak kita dengan kehendak Allah, tetapi aku tidak menemukan ini dalam Alkitab. Sebaliknya, kita harus cukup menolak kehendak kita sendiri dan menerima kehendak Allah.

Aku ingat hari pertama boot camp ketika aku bergabung dengan Korps Marinir setelah lulus dari sekolah menengah. Hampir seratus pemuda ada di sana. Kami semua punya hasrat dan pemikiran sendiri. Kami punya identitas sendiri. Luar biasa melihat semua keberagaman itu. Akan menjadi bencana jika Amerika Serikat mengirim kami bertempur pada hari pertama itu. Jadi, mereka memiliki rencana untuk memperbaiki masalah ini. Selama tiga bulan berikutnya, mereka mematahkan kami. Secara fisik dan mental, kami belajar bagaimana menyangkal diri dan tunduk kepada komandan kami dan satu sama lain. Dunia sering tercengang oleh disiplin dan persatuan besar yang dikenal dari Marinir.

Saat kita menjadi bagian dari kerajaan Allah, kita tidak dapat efektif jika setiap orang melakukan apa yang mereka mau. Sekelompok orang percaya semua bisa punya niat baik, tetapi jika ada satu orang yang tidak menyangkal dirinya, ia tidak akan pernah bisa tunduk pada tujuan yang lebih besar. Ada perang yang berkecamuk, dan kita tidak bisa bertempur sendiri. Kita harus menyangkal diri, bergabung tenaga dengan saudara-saudari kita, dan berperang untuk kemenangan di rumah kita, gereja kita, dan dalam hidup kita.

Penyerahan

Alkitab memanggil kita untuk menyerahkan diri kita:

  • kepada Allah (Yak. 4:7).
  • [kepada mereka] yang mempunyai pengawasan rohani atas kamu [kita] (Ibr. 13:17).
  • kepada setiap ketentuan manusia demi Tuhan (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • satu kepada yang lain dalam takut akan Allah (Ef. 5:21).

Setelah kita menyangkal diri, barulah kita dapat menyerahkan diri kepada orang lain. Banyak orang kini sangat sulit menyerahkan diri kepada sesama manusia. Beberapa merasa mereka bebas di dalam Kristus; oleh karena itu, mereka bisa berbuat sesuka hati. Ada alasan mengapa kita diperintahkan untuk menyerahkan diri kepada orang lain. Mudah bagi kita untuk menjauh dari doktrin yang sehat ketika kita percaya kita bisa memahami segalanya sendiri.

Ketika kita benar-benar telah menyangkal diri, kita mendapati bahwa menyerahkan diri kepada saudara-saudari justru agak mudah, bahkan merupakan berkat besar. Sebenarnya, itu merupakan kebebasan sejati. Keinginanmu tidak penting lagi, dan kamu mulai bergantung pada saudara-saudaramu. Ketika mendapatkan jalan sendiri tidak penting bagi kita, maka ketika kita tidak mendapatkan jalan kita, kita baik-baik saja dengan itu. Saat kita meletakkan hidup kita untuk satu sama lain, kita menjadi kekuatan yang tidak dimengerti dunia. Dunia tertarik kepada gereja selama berabad-abad, menginginkan apa yang dimilikinya. Tetapi luar biasanya, hari ini tampaknya gereja yang ditarik kepada dunia, menginginkan apa yang dimilikinya.

Ada kuasa dalam penyerahan. Ratusan tahun yang lalu, seorang bernama Alexander Agung menaklukkan hampir seluruh dunia yang dikenal kala itu dengan kekuatan militer dan kecerdikan yang dipadukan dengan diplomasi.

Cerita mengatakan bahwa Alexander dan sekelompok kecil prajurit mendekati sebuah kota yang sangat kuat, dikelilingi tembok. Berdiri di luar tembok, Alexander meninggikan suaranya dan menuntut bertemu raja. Ketika raja datang, Alexander bersikeras agar raja menyerahkan kota dan penduduknya kepada Alexander dan rombongan kecil prajuritnya.

Sang raja tertawa, “Mengapa aku harus menyerah kepadamu? Engkau tak dapat menyakiti kami!” Maka, Alexander menawarkan untuk memberi demonstrasi. Ia memerintahkan anak buahnya berdiri berbaris satu per satu dan mulai berjalan. Ia memerintahkan mereka berjalan lurus menuju tebing yang curam.

Orang-orang kota berkumpul di tembok dan menonton dalam keheningan terkejut ketika, satu per satu, prajurit Alexander berjalan, tanpa ragu, tepat ke tebing dan mati! Setelah sepuluh prajurit mati, Alexander memerintahkan sisanya kembali ke sisinya. Orang-orang kota dan sang raja segera menyerah kepada Alexander Agung. Mereka menyadari bahwa jika beberapa orang benar-benar bersedia melakukan bunuh diri atas perintah pemimpin dinamis ini, maka tidak ada yang dapat menghentikan kemenangan akhirnya.

Ketaatan

Penyerahan dan ketaatan berjalan beriringan. Jika kita bersedia menyerahkan diri kepada sesuatu atau seseorang, kita akan ingin menaati. Menjadi sangat penting untuk menyerahkan diri kepada mereka yang memimpin kita, terutama Allah yang mahakuasa di surga. Jika kita bergumul untuk menyerahkan diri, kita biasanya akan bergumul dengan ketaatan. Tuhan melarang jika kita mulai percaya bahwa kita lebih baik melakukan sesuatu sendirian tanpa saudara-saudara kita.

Cinta

“Dengan demikian semua orang akan tahu, bahwa kamu adalah murid-murid-Ku, yaitu jikalau kamu saling mengasihi” (Yoh. 13:35).

Orang melambai satu sama lain di persimpangan, atau mereka akan membukakan pintu untuk orang tua. Orang-orang umumnya penuh kasih sampai sesuatu tidak berjalan sesuai kehendak mereka. Lalu mereka bisa menjadi sangat sulit. Apakah demikian gereja hari ini menunjukkan kasihnya kepada dunia? Selama segala sesuatunya berjalan mulus, dan tak seorang pun menginjak kaki kita, kita semua rukun dan saling mengasihi. Lalu begitu ada sesuatu yang patut dipertarungkan, kita memasang “sarung tinju”. Bukankah Alkitab mengatakan bahwa “kasih sabar menanggung segala sesuatu, percaya segala sesuatu, mengharapkan segala sesuatu, sabar menanggung segala sesuatu” (1 Kor. 13:7)? Kasih sejati terungkap ketika kita menghadapi kesusahan atau ketika seorang saudara melakukan sesuatu yang menyinggung kita. Itulah kasih yang akan menunjukkan kepada dunia bahwa kita murid-murid Yesus.

Apakah kita mengasihi saudara kita cukup untuk menolong ketika ia sedang membutuhkan? Mungkin ia tanpa sadar menyimpang jauh dari Allah dalam suatu hal. Seberapa besar kita mengasihinya? Sebagian orang menganggap kasih hanya berbicara tentang hal-hal positif satu sama lain, tetapi jika kita sungguh mengasihi saudara kita, kita akan mendatangi dia dengan kasih dan berbicara jujur kepadanya. Lalu jika kita mempraktikkan gaya hidup menyangkal diri dan menyerahkan diri kepada saudara-saudari, seharusnya itu berjalan baik. Tuhan melarang jika kita marah kepada saudara yang datang kepada kita untuk menunjukkan kesalahan kita.

Saat kita memilih untuk menderita bersama umat Allah dan telah menyangkal diri, maka kita menghargai ketika seorang saudara atau saudari berbicara ke dalam hidup kita. Kita tidak akan membiarkan diri kita tersinggung.

Menderita karena dan bersama satu sama lain, ditambah menyangkal diri demi satu sama lain, seringkali membentuk kasih yang teguh antar kita. Jenis kasih ini adalah jenis yang tidak dikenal tetapi sangat diinginkan dunia di sekitar kita. Dunia menjadi semakin egois dan mandiri seiring berlalunya hari. Kita tidak mampu melewatkan kesempatan untuk menunjukkan kepada mereka kuasa Allah melalui kasih kita satu sama lain.

Orang-orang saleh sepanjang zaman telah mendapat kesempatan untuk melayani Sang Raja dan menyebarkan pesan Kerajaan Allah, tetapi mereka telah pergi ke kekekalan. Hari ini giliran kita. Ladang sudah putih untuk dituai. Marilah kita terlibat dan, dengan pertolongan Allah, memelihara gereja yang mulia dari Yesus Kristus bagi anak-anak kita, generasi berikutnya.

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.

“So, what brings you in today?” I asked Ben, a 40-year-old man who was sitting across from me.

“Well,” he answered. “I have a few different symptoms. The biggest one is that I am always tired, but I’ve also been gaining weight, and my knees hurt some in the mornings.”

I mentally began to go through what doctors call a differential diagnosis – things that can cause the cluster of symptoms that a patient has. I usually let the patient explain what symptoms he is experiencing and then ask questions to try to hone in on the specific diagnosis.

Ben went on for a little while longer. Then, he proceeded to pull out a piece of paper. “So, Doctor,” he told me. “I’ve done some research into my diagnosis, and I think these are tests that I need to have done to work things up.”

I looked at the list. It was pretty long and included some things I probably would have ordered anyway, like a blood count and thyroid level, but also some very odd things like a Vitamin B1 level and a DHEA level. He also wanted a CT Scan of his head, chest, and abdomen.

“This is a lot of testing,” I said. “I’m not sure we need to do all of it. Can we talk a little bit more about your symptoms and then try to hone in on what testing would be best to sort it out?”

Ben was not impressed. “I have done my research!” He told me firmly. “These days, with the internet, you can find out things that your doctor wouldn’t tell you about – maybe things he doesn’t even know to test for. The problem is that I need YOU to order these things for me so my insurance will cover them. Otherwise, I wouldn’t even be here.”

With that, we’ll leave Ben and his uncomfortable doctor behind. There have always been patients who brought in articles from magazines telling the reader, “Six things your doctor won’t tell you about your health” and listing testing that should be done. It does seem to have gotten worse.

A lot of patients know more than their doctors. They can search for their symptoms on the web and find out all sorts of things that could cause those symptoms.

Beyond that, artificial intelligence is smart. Chat GPT, an artificial intelligence platform, was able to pass the three parts of the US Medical Licensure Exam.1 It didn’t do terribly well— it only got just above a passing grade, but I suppose that’s good enough that it could open an office across the street from mine and start seeing patients.

In some ways letting patients have access to this level of information is a good thing. Doctors aren’t some sort of high priests who are given special rights to access the Holiest of Holies of medical information. More than that, doctors are anything but perfect, and you have only to read online reviews to see that they don’t listen well, botch procedures, and struggle with difficult diagnoses.

It can be challenging, though, when patients believe that they know more than their doctor. I have always said that if you know more than your doctor, either you need a healthy dose of humility or a new doctor— or maybe both.

Get Wisdom!

Proverbs 4:5-9 says, “Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee. Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding. Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her. She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.”

Proverbs 18:15 speaks of getting knowledge, but it indicates that before we seek knowledge, we should make certain that we have wisdom and understanding.

The author of the book of Proverbs was Solomon. We know that early in his reign he had a dream in which God appeared to him and offered him whatever he desired. In his humility, Solomon asked for an understanding heart, so that he would be able to wisely lead such a great people (I Kings 3:9,10).

When we look at knowledge, it is simply a group of facts— blocks of information that need to be assembled into some sort of coherent pattern. Wisdom and understanding are the tools with which we make sense of the knowledge that we have acquired.

Wisdom lets us judge the accuracy of the sources of “knowledge” as well. It helps us to ask the question, “Is this person trying to sell me something? Do they actually have any scientific studies that indicate that what they say is true?”

These are two questions that I ask when I look at a website. Are there links to products that are being sold to me, and is the advertising clearly separated from the articles? More than that, are there links to studies that support what is being claimed? If there are, how big were those studies? If a study has only 12 people in it, it is not large enough to give accurate information.

Robert Harris made an acronym CARS, that helps sort out whether information on a website is valid. Credibility, past Accuracy, Reasonableness, and Supporting information are all important to look at to see if we should value the information on a website.2

Unfortunately, many people who claim to have the answers to living long and healthy lives are actually trying to sell books, supplements, and a variety of other products. One prominent doctor who promotes better health through the use of supplements (that he sells) has managed to accrue enough money through the process that he stated in a 2017 affidavit that he was worth in excess of 100 million dollars. This doesn’t mean that he has nothing to offer, but it does say that he has some bias towards recommending things he is selling.

The American Medical Association has guidelines for doctors to sell products out of their offices ethically. Those guidelines say that the products should serve a particular urgent need (say, crutches at an Orthopedic office), have scientific validity for their use, and that doctors should offer information about other ways that patients can get the same products elsewhere.3 More than that, doctors should reveal to their patients any financial interest that they have in the product that is being offered to the patient.

Confirmation Bias

Most of us read in order to confirm the things we already believe. I see this when people read the Bible— somehow, people can read the Bible and completely ignore Scriptures that contradict their behaviors in terms of political involvement or modesty of dress but believe that they are following all things of the Scripture.

In the same way, each one of us can find stories and information that reinforce our beliefs about doctors and medicine. If we believe that doctors are simply after money and are unethical and prescribe medicines that are toxic to patients, we can find articles that confirm that. On the other hand, if we look for stories that tear down alternative medicine theories, we can find those articles too.

The important thing is that we approach the question looking for real answers and understanding that science doesn’t know everything.

As an example, we do not have good treatments for people who have Long COVID symptoms. That doesn’t mean that many people who suffered through COVID months later aren’t suffering from things like mental fog and fatigue, but it does mean that there is not a single medication that has done better than sugar pills in studies to get rid of those symptoms.

In the absence of scientifically proven treatment plans, many clinics have developed their own treatment courses, using a mixture of supplements and even hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Are these helpful? I don’t know, but I do know that those marketing them will confidently claim that they have an extremely high success rate in curing people if they are simply willing to follow (and pay for) the treatment plan.

More than that, when people are researching their symptoms, they tend to choose what diagnoses they think are likely based on their underlying personality types. Some people are prone to catastrophize— that is, they immediately believe the worst possible outcome of any given scenario they are presented with. These people will type in their symptoms and will come to the conclusion that they have cancer with only days or weeks to live. As God told Hezekiah, it is time for them to set their house in order.

On the other hand, there are plenty of people who have optimistic personalities. They type in their symptom list and come to the conclusion that they have a mild viral illness and will feel better in a few days.

The whole point of having a medical provider review things is that the practitioner can (hopefully) sort out the likely things from the unlikely ones. They don’t deal with the emotional overlay that patients do, so they can objectively decide how many tests to order and what type of tests to order in order to come up with a diagnosis.

Doctors Can Identify Dangerous Situations

I remember seeing a patient years ago who came in to see me with what she thought was a sinus infection. She was in her 20s and said that she had a pounding sensation in her head and a lot of pressure.

She didn’t really have any drainage or fever and none of the typical symptoms of a sinus infection, but sinusitis seemed like the most likely diagnosis that she could come up with.

I took one look at her and didn’t like what I saw. For one thing, she was extremely pale. For another, her pulse rate was quite fast – 130 beats a minute at rest. When I examined her, I found nothing that indicated that she had a sinus infection.

“Jenny,” I told her. “I need you to go to the hospital and get a stat blood count. I’m afraid you are really anemic— although I don’t know why. Wait at the lab and I will talk to you once I get the results back.”

It was perhaps 20 minutes later that I got an urgent call from the hospital laboratory. “Dr. Waldron,” the voice on the other end said. “We have a critical lab result for you…”

Jenny’s hemoglobin was 4.6 (normal is between 12 and 16), and she ended up getting a transfusion. What she didn’t get was treatment for a sinus infection.

Chest pain is a classic symptom that can point to an underlying heart condition. At the same time, it could simply indicate esophageal reflux (acid in the esophagus) or inflammation in a rib or muscle. I probably see a couple of patients every day who have this symptom.

The majority of them need a simple treatment, but a few of them need to be sent urgently to the hospital for a complete heart evaluation. I don’t know how an online search engine will know which direction to indicate for a person to seek after reviewing their symptoms.

At best, an online resource will refer a user to seek emergency services or their local doctor.

Not All Doctors Are Equal

Roughly 50 percent of doctors finished in the bottom half of their Medical School class. Just because someone didn’t have top marks in Medical School doesn’t mean that they don’t have adequate knowledge to treat an ailment. Perhaps the most important knowledge that a doctor needs is to know when he doesn’t know.

It is still challenging for patients to know whether they are dealing with someone who will help them. When you meet a doctor, you tend to judge them based on their “bedside manner.” Most of us look for someone who exudes confidence and seems to know what they are doing.

Confidence does not equal competence, and there are many doctors (and people in other fields) who have high levels of confidence in themselves but are not really competent to take care of the situation at hand.

Here is where doing some research can help. First, your doctor has online reviews, and those reviews will indicate something about the level of care they provide for patients. Second, if what your healthcare provider tells you seems really odd, it is easy to do a little research on the condition that you are supposedly dealing with and see if the symptoms line up and if the treatment seems reasonable.

It is important to realize that humans are not like vehicles. What I mean by that is that there is no scan tool that healthcare providers can hook up and generate all of the error codes and then fix the things that generate those codes.

Even if healthcare providers are certain of the diagnosis, some patients do not respond to the first or even the second treatment that is available. That doesn’t mean that the diagnosis or the treatment was wrong, but that people are not clones of each other and some respond better to one type of treatment than another.

Maybe someday we will have some type of genetic testing that tells us right off what the perfect medication or treatment plan is for a given illness, but that day seems a long way off.

A final thing to mention is that good doctors will not feel threatened by their patients asking questions or doing research. There are times when a patient will ask me about a new treatment that I am not familiar with, and I need to do my own research.

Those scenarios are not upsetting for me but rather a learning opportunity. “I’m not familiar with that,” I will tell my patient. “Let me do a little research and talk to some specialists that I trust, and I will call you later this week and let you know what I find out.”

Sometimes I investigate and find that the treatment is expensive and seems to provide mixed or little benefit, but sometimes it is an improvement over the past ways of doing things. Doctors need to learn and adjust their style of practicing medicine as we learn new things about diseases and how the human body responds to them.

Humility is Needed

The longer I practice medicine, the less I feel that I know. It isn’t that I have developed dementia, but rather that I realize that there are numerous diseases that we don’t have good treatments for. The human body is amazingly complex. There are 36 trillion cells in the human body, and normally, they all work together perfectly; the problem is figuring out what to do when they don’t.

The Dunning-Kruger Effect is something that affects many fields in which people with limited knowledge and skill significantly overestimate their abilities in that field. Studies have shown that 65 percent of Americans believe that they have above-average IQs.4 Statistically, this isn’t possible. Fifty percent of any group of people will have above-average IQs, and the other 50 percent will be below-average. That’s how the IQ scale is set up.

While this effect is present for doctors, it is also present for patients. “Doing your research” is not the same thing as spending four years in Medical School, another three years in a residency training program, and continuing to stay abreast of developments in medicine through a variety of educational courses. We all would do well to listen better and realize our limitations.

The fact that your mother’s cousin took milkweed extract and felt much better from similar symptoms to yours is interesting. Whether the milkweed extract helped them get over their illness, whether there was a placebo effect, or they were just going to get better anyway, regardless of what they took, is up for debate.

True Wisdom

I have mentioned wisdom already, and I would finish with that. True wisdom is realizing that healing comes from God. Psalms 103:3 says of God, “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.”

Healing doesn’t come from antibiotics or chemotherapy. It doesn’t come from taking the right supplements or even eating a healthy diet. Healing comes because God touches us, right down to the tiniest parts of our cells and immune system, and makes things whole again.

I do believe that sometimes He works through medicine, but other times He works through the effective, fervent prayer of righteous men and women. (James 5:16)

With all of our knowledge, it is easy for us to get puffed up with pride and believe that we need no one else. We live in a world that is teeming with knowledge and a world in which wisdom has taken a back seat.

We must choose the source of our information carefully and realize that we don’t know everything. Maybe the reason why the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom is because it is the first step to us laying aside our pride and realizing that we are a tiny part of Creation. Only then, can we humbly listen and learn and receive healing.

“So, ¿qué te trae hoy?” le pregunté a Ben, un hombre de 40 años que estaba sentado frente a mí.

“Bueno,” respondió. “Tengo varios síntomas diferentes. El más importante es que siempre estoy cansado, pero también he estado ganando peso y me duelen un poco las rodillas por las mañanas.”

mentalmente comencé a repasar lo que los médicos llaman un diagnóstico diferencial: las cosas que pueden causar el conjunto de síntomas que presenta un paciente. Normalmente dejo que el paciente explique qué síntomas experimenta y luego hago preguntas para tratar de afinar el diagnóstico específico.

Ben continuó un rato más. Luego procedió a sacar un papel. “Entonces, doctor,” me dijo. “He investigado sobre mi diagnóstico y creo que estas son las pruebas que necesito que me hagan para averiguarlo.”

Miré la lista. Era bastante larga e incluía algunas cosas que probablemente habría pedido de todos modos, como un hemograma y niveles tiroideos, pero también cosas muy extrañas como un nivel de vitamina B1 y un nivel de DHEA. También quería una tomografía computarizada de la cabeza, el tórax y el abdomen.

“Son muchas pruebas,” dije. “No estoy seguro de que tengamos que hacerlas todas. ¿Podemos hablar un poco más sobre tus síntomas y luego intentar precisar qué pruebas serían las mejores para aclararlo?”

Ben no estaba impresionado. “¡He hecho mi investigación!” me dijo con firmeza. “Hoy en día, con internet, puedes enterarte de cosas que tu médico no te diría, quizá cosas que ni siquiera sabe que hay que analizar. El problema es que necesito QUE TÚ pidas estas pruebas para que mi seguro las cubra. De lo contrario, ni siquiera estaría aquí.”

Con eso, dejaremos atrás a Ben y a su incómodo médico. Siempre ha habido pacientes que traen artículos de revistas que dicen al lector: “Seis cosas que tu médico no te dirá sobre tu salud” y enumeran pruebas que deberían hacerse. Parece que esto ha empeorado.

Muchos pacientes saben más que sus médicos. Pueden buscar sus síntomas en la web y encontrar todo tipo de cosas que podrían causar esos síntomas.

Además, la inteligencia artificial es inteligente. ChatGPT, una plataforma de inteligencia artificial, pudo aprobar las tres partes del Examen de Licencia Médica de EE. UU.1 No lo hizo terriblemente bien: apenas obtuvo algo más que una nota de aprobado, pero supongo que es suficiente como para que pudiera abrir una consulta al otro lado de la calle y empezar a ver pacientes.

En cierto modo, permitir que los pacientes accedan a este nivel de información es algo bueno. Los médicos no son una suerte de sumos sacerdotes que tienen derechos especiales para acceder al Lugar Santísimo de la información médica. Más aún, los médicos están lejos de ser perfectos, y basta con leer reseñas en línea para ver que no escuchan bien, cometen errores en procedimientos y tienen dificultades con diagnósticos complejos.

Sin embargo, puede ser un reto cuando los pacientes creen que saben más que su médico. Siempre he dicho que si sabes más que tu médico, o necesitas una buena dosis de humildad o un nuevo médico, o quizá ambas cosas.

¡Consigue sabiduría!

Proverbios 4:5-9 dice: “Adquiere sabiduría, adquiere inteligencia; no lo olvides ni te apartes de las palabras de mi boca. No la abandones, y ella te guardará; quiérela, y ella te conservará. La sabiduría es lo principal; adquiere, pues, sabiduría; y con todo lo que adquieras, adquiere inteligencia. Exáltala, y ella te ennoblecerá; te hará llevar una corona de honra cuando la abraces. Ella dará a tu cabeza un adorno de gracia; una corona de gloria te entregará.”

Proverbios 18:15 habla de adquirir conocimiento, pero indica que antes de buscar conocimiento, debemos asegurarnos de tener sabiduría e inteligencia.

El autor del libro de Proverbios fue Salomón. Sabemos que al principio de su reinado tuvo un sueño en el que Dios se le apareció y le ofreció lo que deseara. En su humildad, Salomón pidió un corazón entendido, para poder gobernar con sabiduría a tan gran pueblo (1 Reyes 3:9,10).

Cuando miramos el conocimiento, es simplemente un conjunto de hechos: bloques de información que deben ensamblarse en algún tipo de patrón coherente. La sabiduría y la inteligencia son las herramientas con las que damos sentido al conocimiento que hemos adquirido.

La sabiduría también nos permite juzgar la exactitud de las fuentes de “conocimiento”. Nos ayuda a hacernos la pregunta: “¿Esta persona intenta venderme algo? ¿Realmente tiene estudios científicos que indiquen que lo que dice es cierto?”

Estas son dos preguntas que me hago al visitar un sitio web. ¿Hay enlaces a productos que me estén vendiendo, y la publicidad está claramente separada de los artículos? Además, ¿hay enlaces a estudios que respalden lo que se afirma? Si los hay, ¿qué tamaño tuvieron esos estudios? Si un estudio tiene solo 12 personas, no es lo suficientemente grande como para ofrecer información precisa.

Robert Harris creó el acrónimo CARS, que ayuda a distinguir si la información en un sitio web es válida. Credibilidad, Exactitud pasada, Razonabilidad e Información de respaldo son aspectos importantes a revisar para ver si debemos valorar la información de un sitio web.2

Desafortunadamente, muchas personas que afirman tener las respuestas para vivir una vida larga y saludable en realidad intentan vender libros, suplementos y una variedad de otros productos. Un médico prominente que promueve una mejor salud mediante el uso de suplementos (que él vende) llegó a acumular tanto dinero que declaró en una declaración jurada de 2017 que su patrimonio superaba los 100 millones de dólares. Esto no significa que no tenga nada que ofrecer, pero sí indica que tiene cierto sesgo hacia recomendar cosas que vende.

La Asociación Médica Estadounidense tiene directrices para que los médicos vendan productos en sus consultorios de manera ética. Esas directrices dicen que los productos deben cubrir una necesidad urgente particular (por ejemplo, muletas en una consulta de ortopedia), tener validez científica para su uso y que los médicos deben ofrecer información sobre otras formas en que los pacientes pueden obtener los mismos productos en otros lugares.3 Además, los médicos deben revelar a sus pacientes cualquier interés financiero que tengan en el producto que se ofrece al paciente.

Sesgo de confirmación

La mayoría de nosotros leemos para confirmar las cosas que ya creemos. Lo veo cuando la gente lee la Biblia: de algún modo, las personas pueden leer la Biblia e ignorar por completo las Escrituras que contradicen su conducta en temas de participación política o modestia de vestimenta, pero creer que están siguiendo todas las cosas de la Escritura.

Del mismo modo, cada uno de nosotros puede encontrar historias e información que refuercen nuestras creencias sobre los médicos y la medicina. Si creemos que los médicos solo buscan dinero, son poco éticos y prescriben medicamentos tóxicos para los pacientes, podemos encontrar artículos que lo confirmen. Por otro lado, si buscamos historias que desacrediten las teorías de la medicina alternativa, también podemos encontrar esos artículos.

Lo importante es que abordemos la cuestión buscando respuestas reales y comprendiendo que la ciencia no lo sabe todo.

Por ejemplo, no tenemos buenos tratamientos para personas que padecen síntomas de COVID prolongado. Eso no significa que muchas personas que sufrieron COVID meses atrás no padezcan cosas como niebla mental y fatiga, pero sí significa que no existe un medicamento único que haya mostrado en estudios mejores resultados que los placebo para eliminar esos síntomas.

En ausencia de planes de tratamiento científicamente probados, muchas clínicas han desarrollado sus propios cursos de tratamiento, usando una mezcla de suplementos e incluso tratamientos con oxígeno hiperbárico. ¿Son útiles? No lo sé, pero sí sé que quienes los promocionan afirmarán con confianza que tienen una tasa de éxito extremadamente alta para curar a las personas si simplemente están dispuestas a seguir (y pagar) el plan de tratamiento.

Además, cuando las personas investigan sus síntomas, tienden a elegir qué diagnósticos creen probables en función de sus rasgos de personalidad subyacentes. Algunas personas son propensas a catastrofizar: es decir, inmediatamente creen el peor resultado posible de cualquier escenario que se les presente. Estas personas introducen sus síntomas y llegan a la conclusión de que tienen cáncer y solo les quedan días o semanas de vida. Como Dios le dijo a Ezequías, es tiempo de que pongan en orden su casa.

Por otro lado, hay muchas personas con personalidades optimistas. Teclean su lista de síntomas y llegan a la conclusión de que tienen una enfermedad viral leve y se sentirán mejor en unos días.

El objetivo de que un proveedor médico revise el caso es que el profesional pueda (con suerte) separar lo probable de lo improbable. No se enfrentan a la superposición emocional que tienen los pacientes, por lo que pueden decidir objetivamente cuántas pruebas solicitar y qué tipo de pruebas pedir para llegar a un diagnóstico.

Los médicos pueden identificar situaciones peligrosas

Recuerdo que hace años vi a una paciente que vino a verme pensando que tenía una infección sinusal. Tenía unos 20 años y decía que notaba una sensación palpitante en la cabeza y mucha presión.

No tenía realmente secreción ni fiebre y ninguno de los síntomas típicos de una sinusitis, pero la sinusitis parecía el diagnóstico más probable que ella pudo imaginar.

La miré y no me gustó lo que vi. Por una parte, estaba extremadamente pálida. Por otra, su frecuencia de pulso era bastante alta: 130 latidos por minuto en reposo. Cuando la examiné, no encontré nada que indicara que tuviera una infección sinusal.

“Jenny,” le dije. “Necesito que vayas al hospital y te hagan un hemograma urgente. Me temo que estás realmente anémica, aunque no sé por qué. Espera en el laboratorio y te hablaré cuando tenga los resultados.”

Quizá 20 minutos después recibí una llamada urgente del laboratorio del hospital. “Doctor Waldron,” dijo la voz al otro lado. “Tenemos un resultado de laboratorio crítico para usted…”

La hemoglobina de Jenny era 4.6 (lo normal está entre 12 y 16), y terminó recibiendo una transfusión. Lo que no recibió fue tratamiento para una infección sinusal.

El dolor torácico es un síntoma clásico que puede apuntar a una enfermedad cardíaca subyacente. Al mismo tiempo, podría simplemente indicar reflujo esofágico (ácido en el esófago) o inflamación en una costilla o músculo. Probablemente veo un par de pacientes cada día que presentan este síntoma.

La mayoría de ellos necesitan un tratamiento sencillo, pero algunos deben ser enviados con urgencia al hospital para una evaluación cardíaca completa. No sé cómo un motor de búsqueda en línea sabrá qué indicación dar a una persona para que busque ayuda tras revisar sus síntomas.

En el mejor de los casos, un recurso en línea remitirá a un usuario a buscar servicios de emergencia o a su médico local.

No todos los médicos son iguales

Aproximadamente el 50 por ciento de los médicos terminaron en la mitad inferior de su clase en la escuela de Medicina. Que alguien no haya tenido las mejores notas en la facultad no significa que no tenga el conocimiento adecuado para tratar una dolencia. Quizá el conocimiento más importante que necesita un médico es saber cuándo no sabe.

Sigue siendo un desafío para los pacientes saber si están tratando con alguien que los ayudará. Al conocer a un médico, tendemos a juzgarlo por su “manera de tratar al paciente”. La mayoría buscamos a alguien que irradie confianza y parezca saber lo que hace.

Confianza no equivale a competencia, y hay muchos médicos (y personas en otros campos) que tienen un alto nivel de confianza en sí mismos pero que no son realmente competentes para atender la situación en cuestión.

Aquí es donde algo de investigación puede ayudar. Primero, tu médico tiene reseñas en línea, y esas reseñas indicarán algo sobre el nivel de atención que brinda a los pacientes. Segundo, si lo que tu proveedor de salud te dice parece realmente extraño, es fácil investigar un poco la condición que supuestamente tienes y ver si los síntomas concuerdan y si el tratamiento parece razonable.

Es importante darse cuenta de que los humanos no son como vehículos. Con esto quiero decir que no existe una herramienta de escaneo que los proveedores de salud puedan conectar para generar todos los códigos de error y luego arreglar las cosas que generan esos códigos.

Incluso si los proveedores de salud están seguros del diagnóstico, algunos pacientes no responden al primer o incluso al segundo tratamiento disponible. Eso no significa que el diagnóstico o el tratamiento fueran incorrectos, sino que las personas no son copias idénticas y algunas responden mejor a un tipo de tratamiento que a otro.

Tal vez algún día tengamos algún tipo de prueba genética que nos diga de inmediato cuál es el medicamento o plan de tratamiento perfecto para una enfermedad dada, pero ese día parece estar muy lejos.

Una última cosa a mencionar es que los buenos médicos no se sentirán amenazados porque sus pacientes hagan preguntas o investiguen. Hay ocasiones en que un paciente me pregunta por un tratamiento nuevo del que no estoy familiarizado y yo necesito hacer mi propia investigación.

Esos escenarios no me molestan sino que son una oportunidad de aprendizaje. “No estoy familiarizado con eso,” le digo al paciente. “Déjame investigar un poco y hablar con algunos especialistas en los que confío, y te llamaré más tarde esta semana para contarte lo que averigüe.”

A veces investigo y encuentro que el tratamiento es caro y parece ofrecer beneficios mixtos o pequeños, pero otras veces es una mejora respecto a las formas anteriores de hacer las cosas. Los médicos necesitan aprender y ajustar su estilo de practicar la medicina a medida que aprendemos cosas nuevas sobre las enfermedades y cómo responde el cuerpo humano a ellas.

Se necesita humildad

Cuanto más tiempo ejerzo la medicina, menos siento que sé. No es que haya desarrollado demencia, sino que me doy cuenta de que hay numerosas enfermedades para las que no tenemos buenos tratamientos. El cuerpo humano es asombrosamente complejo. Hay 36 billones de células en el cuerpo humano, y normalmente todas trabajan juntas a la perfección; el problema es descubrir qué hacer cuando no lo hacen.

El efecto Dunning-Kruger es algo que afecta a muchos campos en los que personas con conocimientos y habilidades limitadas sobreestiman significativamente sus capacidades en ese campo. Estudios han mostrado que el 65 por ciento de los estadounidenses cree tener un coeficiente intelectual por encima del promedio.4 Estadísticamente, esto no es posible. El cincuenta por ciento de cualquier grupo tendrá un CI por encima del promedio y el otro 50 por ciento estará por debajo del promedio. Así es como está calibrada la escala de CI.

Si bien este efecto está presente entre los médicos, también está presente entre los pacientes. “Hacer tu investigación” no es lo mismo que pasar cuatro años en la facultad de Medicina, otros tres años en un programa de residencia y continuar manteniéndose al día en los avances de la medicina a través de una variedad de cursos educativos. A todos nos vendría bien escuchar mejor y darnos cuenta de nuestras limitaciones.

El hecho de que el primo de tu madre tomara extracto de dedalera y se sintiera mucho mejor por síntomas similares a los tuyos es interesante. Si el extracto de dedalera les ayudó a recuperarse, si hubo un efecto placebo o si simplemente iban a mejorar de todos modos, independientemente de lo que tomaran, es algo discutible.

La verdadera sabiduría

Ya he mencionado la sabiduría, y terminaría con eso. La verdadera sabiduría es reconocer que la sanidad viene de Dios. Salmos 103:3 dice de Dios: “El que perdona todas tus iniquidades; el que sana todas tus dolencias.”

La sanidad no proviene de antibióticos ni de quimioterapia. No proviene de tomar los suplementos correctos ni siquiera de llevar una dieta sana. La sanidad viene porque Dios nos toca, hasta las partes más diminutas de nuestras células y del sistema inmunitario, y hace que las cosas vuelvan a ser enteras.

Creo que a veces Él obra por medio de la medicina, pero otras veces obra por medio de la oración eficaz y ferviente de hombres y mujeres justos. (Santiago 5:16)

Con todo nuestro conocimiento, es fácil inflarnos de orgullo y creer que no necesitamos a nadie más. Vivimos en un mundo rebosante de conocimiento y en un mundo en el que la sabiduría ha pasado a un segundo plano.

Debemos elegir la fuente de nuestra información con cuidado y darnos cuenta de que no lo sabemos todo. Quizá la razón por la que el temor de Jehová es el principio de la sabiduría es porque es el primer paso para dejar a un lado nuestro orgullo y darnos cuenta de que somos una pequeña parte de la Creación. Solo entonces podemos escuchar humildemente, aprender y recibir sanidad.
