What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

A cosa pensiamo quando pensiamo al termine «chiesa»? Viviamo in un tempo in cui ci sono chiese molteplici e varie. Se una chiesa non ti va bene, ce ne sono altre tra cui scegliere. Mentre alcune chiese esortano il loro popolo a vivere per Dio e per gli altri invece che per se stessi, altre promuovono un vangelo che afferma che molti soldi e una vita migliore ora sono il risultato del seguire Cristo. Tuttavia, ci sono ancora chiese che cercano di seguire ciò che dice la Bibbia—Sola scriptura (sola Scrittura). Tradizionalmente, le chiese anabattiste conservatrici in America hanno cercato di funzionare in questo modo. Ma sta cambiando?

Viviamo in un tempo in cui le linee vengono attraversate, sfumate e confuse. La gente non è sicura di ciò che è vero e di ciò che non lo è. Oggi, uomini e donne nel mondo cercano risposte e soluzioni, ma dove dovrebbero cercare?

Stavo parlando con un giovane che testimoniava di essere stato convertito in giovane età. Frequentava la chiesa fedelmente ed era considerato piuttosto dotato. Ma c’era un problema—aveva un peccato che non riusciva ancora a controllare. Mentre lottava con Dio e supplicava per la vittoria, cominciò a sentire un messaggio ricorrente da altri cristiani professanti: “Nessuno è perfetto!” “Tutti abbiamo problemi.” “Tutti hanno peccato!” Alla fine, questo giovane accettò il suo peccato come normale. Lo giustificò perché sembrava che tutti dicessero di avere peccati anch’essi, che non vivevano nella completa vittoria. Questo portò quel giovane in un luogo di rovina completa.

Stiamo predicando e accettando un Vangelo sconfitto—un vangelo che non offre perdono completo e vittoria completa? Molti giovani di oggi sono confusi. Molte persone nel mondo di oggi non capiscono. Chiunque può andare in chiesa e cercare di essere una persona migliore. Ma che dire del vangelo onnipotente che cambia la vita di Gesù Cristo?

L’apostolo Paolo dice che Gesù sta per tornare per «. . . una chiesa gloriosa, che non abbia macchia né rughe, né alcuna cosa simile; ma che sia santa e irreprensibile» (Eph. 5:27). E lo stesso Gesù disse «. . . Tu sei Pietro, e su questa pietra edificherò la mia chiesa; e le porte dell'inferno non prevarranno contro di essa» (Matt. 16:18).

Prima di essere convertito, ero certamente schiavo del peccato, ma volevo la vittoria. Ero dipendente da droghe e alcol, ma non mi piaceva. Volevo essere libero. Sono andato a consulenze e strutture di riabilitazione in tutta l’America, ma non ha funzionato. Non avevo potere. Potevo smettere per alcuni giorni o anche settimane, poi la rabbia e la depressione prendevano il sopravvento, e tornavo alle sostanze. Un giorno, mi trovai faccia a faccia col Creatore. La mano dell'Iddio onnipotente mi afferrò e mi aprì gli occhi. Mi pentii dei miei peccati e mi fu data una tabula rasa e un cuore nuovo. Non tornai mai indietro. Droghe, alcol e due pacchetti di sigarette al giorno finirono—per sempre.

Non potevo credere a quello che Dio stava facendo. Il potere di Dio era reale. Non potevo sconfiggerlo da solo, come nessuno di noi può, ma Dio ci ha promesso libertà dalla schiavitù e una nuova vita di vita vittoriosa se sottomettiamo le nostre vite a lui. Questa capacità di vincere il potere del peccato e poi camminare nella vittoria è ciò che il mondo sta cercando. Crediamo che Dio possa liberarci non solo dalla dipendenza da sostanze ma anche dalla rabbia, dall’egoismo, dall’amarezza, dall’avidità e dall’orgoglio? La Parola di Dio dice: «Se confessiamo i nostri peccati, egli è fedele e giusto da perdonarci i peccati e purificarci da ogni iniquità» (1 John 1:9). Nessuno è interessato a un Vangelo sconfitto, nessuno tranne coloro che vivono nella sconfitta perché hanno scelto le cose di questo mondo invece di Dio e della Sua Parola.

Siamo disposti a testimoniare il potere della risurrezione? Dobbiamo proclamare un vangelo che salvi completamente le persone dalla schiavitù del peccato—per sempre. Dobbiamo essere audaci e fiduciosi nella nostra fede così da poter condurre le persone al Maestro.

Stavo testimoniando a un uomo quando egli disse a voce abbastanza alta: “Dio non è reale!” La bocca del mio figlio di sei anni si spalancò, ed esclamò, “Papà, ha appena detto una bugia!”

Mio figlio non ha bisogno di essere convinto che Dio è reale; ci crede con tutto il cuore. Il mondo là fuori ha bisogno di essere convinto. Hanno bisogno di vedere qualcosa che la scienza non può spiegare. Hanno bisogno di vedere qualcosa che sfida ogni probabilità.

Quella cosa è un cuore che è stato veramente cambiato. Il combattente ora ama i suoi nemici. La persona con un problema di rabbia ora ama gli altri incondizionatamente. Famiglie spezzate vengono guarite. Miserabili peccatori sono perdonati e vivono una vita trasformata. Speranza, pace, amore e potere sono donati gratuitamente a uomini e donne che apparentemente non hanno speranza. «I ciechi riacquistano la vista, e gli zoppi camminano, i lebbrosi sono purificati, e i sordi odono, i morti sono risuscitati, e ai poveri è predicato il vangelo» (Matt. 11:5).

Stai vivendo la tua vita affinché il mondo possa vedere l’opera di Dio pratica, efficace e reale ogni giorno? Ecco alcune cose di cui la Chiesa ha bisogno nel nostro tempo per attrarre nuovamente i perduti.

Una disponibilità a soffrire

La storia mostrerebbe che la chiesa, attraverso i secoli, ha sofferto per Cristo. Era parte del costo del seguire Cristo. La Bibbia dice: «Sì, e tutti quelli che vogliono vivere piamente in Cristo Gesù saranno perseguitati» (2 Tim. 3:12). Era qualcosa che accadeva naturalmente.

Oggi, molte persone vogliono il sogno americano. La gente vive una buona vita morale, è brava cittadina, guadagna bene e va in chiesa la domenica. Ma è questo ciò a cui siamo chiamati? Il vangelo si diffuse come incendio quando la chiesa subì persecuzione e lo fece volontariamente e gioiosamente. Era qualcosa che il mondo non aveva mai visto—una fede che la gente mostrava con la propria vita, e la loro morte era qualcosa per cui valeva la pena morire. Non temiamo di soffrire per Cristo oggi.

Negazione di sé

Allora Gesù disse ai suoi discepoli: «Se qualcuno vuole venire dopo di me, rinneghi se stesso, prenda la sua croce e mi segua» (Matt. 16:24).

Ti sei mai chiesto perché Gesù ci istruisce a rinnegarci? Dopotutto, Egli ci ha dato desideri e passioni, quindi perché dobbiamo rinnegarli? Ho sentito persone dire che dobbiamo allineare la nostra volontà con quella di Dio, ma non trovo questo nella Bibbia. Piuttosto, dovremmo semplicemente rinnegare la nostra volontà e accettare la volontà di Dio.

Ricordo il primo giorno di addestramento quando mi arruolai nei Marine Corps dopo il diploma di scuola superiore. Eravamo vicino a cento giovani uomini lì. Ognuno di noi aveva i propri desideri e pensieri. Avevamo la nostra identità. Era sorprendente vedere tutta quella diversità. Sarebbe stato un disastro se gli Stati Uniti d'America ci avessero mandato in battaglia quel primo giorno. Così, avevano un piano per risolvere questo problema. Nei successivi tre mesi, ci hanno spezzati. Fisicamente e mentalmente, abbiamo imparato a rinnegarci e a sottometterci ai nostri comandanti e gli uni agli altri. Il mondo è spesso stupito dalla grande disciplina e unità per cui i Marines sono conosciuti.

Quando entriamo a far parte del regno di Dio, non possiamo essere efficaci se ciascuno di noi fa ciò che vuole. Un corpo di credenti può avere tutte buone intenzioni, ma se anche una sola persona non si è rinnegata, non sarà mai in grado di sottomettersi alla causa più grande. C’è una guerra in corso, e non possiamo combatterla da soli. Dobbiamo rinnegarci, unirci alle forze dei nostri fratelli e combattere per la vittoria nelle nostre case, chiese e vite.

Sottomissione

La Bibbia ci chiama a sottometterci:

  • a Dio (Jas. 4:7).
  • [a coloro] che hanno la [guida spirituale] su di voi [noi] (Heb. 13:17).
  • ad ogni ordinanza dell'uomo per amor del Signore (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • l'uno all'altro nel timore di Dio (Eph. 5:21).

Una volta che ci rinneghiamo, allora e solo allora, possiamo sottometterci agli altri. Molte persone oggi hanno grande difficoltà a sottomettersi al loro prossimo. Alcuni sentono di essere liberi in Cristo; perciò, possono fare come gli pare. C’è una ragione per cui ci è comandato di sottometterci agli altri. È facile per noi allontanarci dalla sana dottrina quando crediamo di poter capire tutto da soli.

Quando ci siamo veramente rinnegati, scopriamo che è piuttosto facile, e persino una grande benedizione, sottometterci alla fratellanza. In effetti, è vera libertà. Ciò che vuoi non importa, e cominci a dipendere dai tuoi fratelli e sorelle. Quando ottenere ciò che vogliamo non è importante per noi, allora quando non lo otteniamo, stiamo bene lo stesso. Mentre ci doniamo l'un l'altro, diventiamo una forza che il mondo non capisce. Il mondo è stato attratto dalla chiesa per secoli, desiderando ciò che essa aveva. Ma sorprendentemente, oggi sembra che la chiesa sia attratta dal mondo, desiderando ciò che esso ha.

C’è potere nella sottomissione. Centinaia di anni fa, un uomo di nome Alessandro Magno conquistò quasi tutto il mondo allora conosciuto usando forza militare e astuzia mescolate con diplomazia.

Si racconta che Alessandro e una piccola compagnia di soldati si avvicinarono a una città fortificata e murata. Stando fuori dalle mura, Alessandro alzò la voce e chiese di vedere il re. Quando il re arrivò, Alessandro insistette che il re si arrendesse la città e i suoi abitanti a lui e alla sua piccola schiera di soldati.

Il re rise: «Perché dovrei arrendermi a te? Non puoi farci del male!» Così, Alessandro offrì al re una dimostrazione. Ordinò ai suoi uomini di mettersi in fila e cominciare a marciare. Li fece marciare dritti verso una parete a picco.

La gente della città si radunò sulla mura e osservò in silenzio scioccato mentre, uno dopo l'altro, i soldati di Alessandro marciavano, senza esitazione, proprio giù dalla scogliera verso la morte! Dopo che dieci soldati morirono, Alessandro ordinò al resto degli uomini di tornare al suo fianco. La gente della città e il re si arresero immediatamente ad Alessandro Magno. Si resero conto che se pochi uomini erano davvero disposti a commettere suicidio al comando di quel leader dinamico, allora nulla avrebbe potuto fermare la sua vittoria eventuale.

Obbedienza

Sottomissione e obbedienza vanno di pari passo. Se siamo disposti a sottometterci a qualcosa o a qualcuno, vorrremo obbedirgli. Diventa molto importante sottomettersi a coloro che stanno sopra di noi, specialmente all'Iddio onnipotente in Cielo. Se lottiamo per sottometterci, di solito lotteremo con l'obbedienza. Dio ce ne scampi se cominciamo a credere che sia meglio fare le cose da soli senza i nostri fratelli.

Amore

«Da questo conosceranno tutti che siete miei discepoli: se avrete amore gli uni per gli altri» (John 13:35).

Le persone si salutano con la mano a un incrocio, o aprono la porta a una persona anziana. Le persone sono generalmente amabili finché qualcosa non va per il loro verso. Poi possono diventare molto difficili. È questo il modo in cui la chiesa oggi mostra il suo amore al mondo? Finché tutto procede senza intoppi, e nessuno calpesta i nostri piedi, andiamo tutti d'accordo e ci amiamo. Poi non appena c'è qualcosa per cui vale la pena lottare, mettiamo i «guantoni da boxe». Non dice la Bibbia che «la carità (amore) tutto copre, tutto crede, tutto spera, tutto sopporta» (1 Cor. 13:7)? Il vero amore si rivela quando affrontiamo l'avversità o quando un fratello fa qualcosa per offenderci. Quell'amore è ciò che mostrerà al mondo che siamo discepoli di Gesù.

Amiamo abbastanza il nostro fratello da aiutarlo quando è nel bisogno? Forse sta inconsapevolmente allontanandosi da Dio in un certo ambito. Quanto lo amiamo? Alcune persone pensano che l'amore significhi parlare solo di cose positive tra di noi, ma se amiamo veramente il nostro fratello, andremo da lui con amore e gli parleremo onestamente. Allora se pratichiamo uno stile di vita di rinnegamento di noi stessi e sottomissione ai fratelli, dovrebbe andare bene. Dio ce ne scampi se ci arrabbiamo con un fratello che viene da noi per mostrarci il nostro errore.

Quando abbiamo scelto di soffrire con il popolo di Dio e ci siamo rinnegati, apprezziamo quando un fratello o una sorella interviene nelle nostre vite. Non permetteremo di essere offesi facilmente.

Soffrire per e con gli altri, oltre a rinnegarci per gli altri, spesso forma un amore solido l'uno per l'altro. Questo tipo di amore è quello che il mondo intorno a noi non conosce ma desidera fortemente. Il mondo diventa sempre più egoista e indipendente con il passare dei giorni. Non possiamo permetterci di perdere le nostre opportunità di mostrare loro il potere di Dio con il nostro amore reciproco.

Persone pii attraverso i secoli hanno avuto la loro opportunità di servire il Re e diffondere il messaggio del Regno di Dio, ma sono passate all'eternità. Oggi tocca a noi. I campi sono già bianchi per la mietitura. Impegniamoci e, con l'aiuto di Dio, preserviamo la gloriosa chiesa di Gesù Cristo per i nostri figli, la prossima generazione.

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

Wat denken we wanneer we de term ‘kerk’ noemen? We leven in een tijd waarin er veel uiteenlopende kerken zijn. Als de ene kerk je niet bevalt, zijn er anderen om uit te kiezen. Terwijl sommige kerken hun mensen aansporen om voor God te leven en niet voor zichzelf, verkondigen andere kerken een evangelie dat veel geld en een beter leven nú als het resultaat van Christus volgen aanbiedt. Er zijn echter nog steeds kerken die proberen te volgen wat de Bijbel zegt—Sola scriptura (alleen de Schrift). Traditioneel hebben de conservatieve anabaptistische kerken in Amerika geprobeerd op deze manier te functioneren. Maar verandert dat?

We leven in een tijd waarin grenzen worden overschreden, vervaagd en verward. Mensen weten niet zeker wat waar is en wat niet. Vandaag zoeken mannen en vrouwen over de hele wereld naar antwoorden en oplossingen, maar waar moeten zij zoeken?

Ik sprak met een jonge man die getuigde op jonge leeftijd tot bekering te zijn gekomen. Hij ging trouw naar de kerk en werd als behoorlijk begaafd beschouwd. Maar er was een probleem—hij had een zonde die hij nog steeds niet onder controle kon krijgen. Terwijl hij worstelde met God en smeekte om overwinning, begon hij een terugkerende boodschap van andere bekennende christenen te horen: “Niemand is perfect!” “We hebben allemaal problemen.” “Iedereen heeft gezondigd!” Uiteindelijk accepteerde deze jongeman zijn zonde als normaal. Hij rechtvaardigde het omdat het leek alsof iedereen ook zei dat hij zondigde, dat men niet in volledige overwinning leefde. Het bracht deze jongeman tot een plaats van totale ondergang.

Prediken en accepteren wij een verslagen evangelie—een evangelie dat geen volledige vergeving en volledige overwinning biedt? Veel jongeren van vandaag zijn verward. Veel mensen in de wereld van vandaag begrijpen het niet. Iedereen kan naar de kerk gaan en proberen een beter mens te zijn. Maar hoe zit het met het almachtige, levensveranderende evangelie van Jezus Christus?

De apostel Paulus zegt dat Jezus terugkomt voor “...een verheerlijkt lichaam, zonder vlek of rimpel of iets dergelijks; maar dat het heilig en onbesmet mag zijn” (Ef. 5:27). En Jezus Zelf zei: “...Dat gij zijt Petrus, en op deze rots zal ik mijn kerk bouwen; en de poorten van de hel zullen haar niet overwinnen” (Matt. 16:18).

Voordat ik bekeerd werd, was ik zeker een slaaf van de zonde, maar ik verlangde naar overwinning. Ik was verslaafd aan drugs en alcohol, maar ik hield er niet van. Ik wilde vrij zijn. Ik ging naar counseling- en afkickcentra door heel Amerika, maar het werkte niet. Ik had geen kracht. Ik kon een paar dagen of zelfs weken stoppen, dan kwamen woede en depressie opzetten en keerde ik terug naar de middelen. Op een dag kwam ik oog in oog met de Schepper te staan. De hand van de almachtige God greep mij vast en opende mijn ogen. Ik bekeerde mij van mijn zonden en kreeg een schone lei en een schoon hart. Ik ben nooit teruggegaan. Drugs, alcohol en twee pakken sigaretten per dag waren voorbij—voor eeuwig.

Ik kon nauwelijks geloven wat God deed. De kracht van God was echt. Ik kon het niet alleen overwinnen, zoals niemand van ons dat kan, maar God heeft ons vrijheid van slavernij en een nieuw leven van overwinnend leven beloofd als we ons leven aan Hem overgeven. Dit vermogen om de macht van de zonde te overwinnen en daarna in overwinning te wandelen is waar de wereld naar zoekt. Geloven wij dat God ons niet alleen van middelenmisbruik kan bevrijden, maar ook van woede, egoïsme, bitterheid, hebzucht en trots? Gods Woord zegt: “Indien wij onze zonden belijden, Hij is getrouw en rechtvaardig om ons de zonden te vergeven en ons te reinigen van alle ongerechtigheid” (1 Joh. 1:9). Niemand is geïnteresseerd in een verslagen evangelie, niemand behalve degenen die in overwinning leven omdat zij de dingen van deze wereld boven God en Zijn Woord hebben gekozen.

Zullen wij getuigen van de kracht van de opstanding? We moeten een evangelie prediken dat mensen volledig redt uit de slavernij van de zonde—voor altijd. We moeten moedig en vol vertrouwen in ons geloof zijn zodat we mensen naar de Meester kunnen leiden.

Ik was een man aan het getuigen toen hij vrij hardop zei: “God is niet echt!” De mond van mijn zesjarige zoon viel open en hij hapte: “Papa, hij vertelde net een leugen!”

Mijn zoon hoeft niet overtuigd te worden dat God echt is; hij gelooft het met heel zijn hart. De wereld daarbuiten moet overtuigd worden. Ze moeten iets zien dat de wetenschap niet kan verklaren. Ze moeten iets zien dat alle kansen tart.

Dat iets is een hart dat werkelijk veranderd is. De vechtersbaas houdt nu van zijn vijanden. Degene met een woedeprobleem houdt nu onvoorwaardelijk van anderen. Gebroken gezinnen worden geheeld. Ellendige zondaars worden vergeven en leven een getransformeerd leven. Hoop, vrede, liefde en kracht worden vrijelijk gegeven aan mannen en vrouwen die schijnbaar geen hoop hebben. “De blinden ontvangen hun gezicht, en de kreupelen wandelen, de melaatsen worden gereinigd, en de doven horen, de doden worden opgewekt, en aan de armen wordt het evangelie gepredikt” (Matt. 11:5).

Leef jij je leven zodat de wereld het werk van God praktisch, effectief en elke dag echt kan zien? Hier zijn een paar dingen die de Kerk in onze tijd nodig heeft om opnieuw de verlorenen aan te trekken.

Een bereidheid te lijden

De geschiedenis toont aan dat de kerk, door de eeuwen heen, heeft geleden omwille van Christus. Het maakte deel uit van de prijs van het volgen van Christus. De Bijbel zegt: “Ja, en allen die godzalig willen leven in Christus Jezus zullen vervolging lijden” (2 Tim. 3:12). Het was iets dat gewoon gebeurde.

Vandaag willen veel mensen de Amerikaanse droom. Mensen leiden een goed moreel leven, zijn goede burgers, verdienen goed de kost en gaan op zondag naar de kerk. Maar is dat waar wij toe geroepen zijn? Het evangelie verspreidde zich als een lopend vuurtje toen de kerk vervolging onderging en dat vrijwillig en vreugdevol deed. Het was iets wat de wereld nog nooit had gezien—een geloof dat mensen lieten zien door hun leven, en hun dood was iets waard om voor te sterven. Laten we vandaag niet bang zijn om voor Christus te lijden.

Zelfverloochening

Toen zei Jezus tot zijn discipelen: “Indien iemand achter Mij aan wil komen, die verleeke zichzelven, en neme zijn kruis op, en volge Mij” (Matt. 16:24).

Heb je je ooit afgevraagd waarom Jezus ons opdraagt onszelf te verloochenen? Hij gaf ons immers verlangens en passies, dus waarom moeten we die verloochenen? Ik heb mensen horen zeggen dat we onze wil op één lijn moeten brengen met Gods wil, maar dat vind ik niet in de Bijbel. In plaats daarvan zouden we gewoon onze wil moeten verloochenen en Gods wil aanvaarden.

Ik herinner me de eerste dag van de kazerne toen ik me bij het Marine Corps voegde na mijn eindexamen van de middelbare school. Bijna honderd jonge mannen waren daar. We hadden allemaal onze eigen verlangens en gedachten. We hadden onze eigen identiteit. Het was verbazingwekkend om al die diversiteit te zien. Het zou een ramp zijn geweest als de Verenigde Staten van Amerika ons die eerste dag ten strijde hadden gestuurd. Dus hadden ze een plan opgesteld om dit probleem op te lossen. In de volgende drie maanden braken zij ons. Fysiek en mentaal leerden we hoe we onszelf moesten verloochenen en ons moesten onderwerpen aan onze commandanten en aan elkaar. De wereld is vaak verbaasd over de grote discipline en eenheid waarvoor de mariniers bekend staan.

Wanneer we onderdeel worden van het Koninkrijk van God, kunnen we niet effectief zijn als ieder doet wat hij wil. Een lichaam van gelovigen kan allemaal goede bedoelingen hebben, maar als één persoon zichzelf niet heeft verloochen, zal die nooit kunnen onderwerpen aan het grotere doel. Er woedt een oorlog, en we kunnen die niet alleen voeren. We moeten onszelf verloochenen, de krachten bundelen met onze broeders en zusters, en vechten voor overwinning in onze huizen, kerken en levens.

Onderwerping

De Bijbel roept ons op ons te onderwerpen:

  • aan God (Jak. 4:7).
  • [aan hen] die het [geestelijke] gezag over u [ons] hebben (Hebr. 13:17).
  • aan alle instellingen van de mens omwille van de Heere (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • aan elkander in de vreze Gods (Ef. 5:21).

Zodra wij onszelf verloochenen, dan en alleen dan kunnen wij ons aan anderen onderwerpen. Veel mensen hebben tegenwoordig grote moeite zich aan hun medemens te onderwerpen. Sommigen voelen zich vrij in Christus; daarom kunnen zij doen wat hen goeddunkt. Er is een reden waarom ons wordt opgedragen ons aan anderen te onderwerpen. Het is gemakkelijk voor ons om af te dwalen van gezonde leer als we geloven dat we alles zelf kunnen uitvinden.

Wanneer we ons werkelijk hebben verloochen, ontdekken we dat het tamelijk gemakkelijk is, en zelfs een grote zegen, om ons aan de broederschap te onderwerpen. In feite is het ware vrijheid. Wat jij wilt doet er niet toe, en je begint afhankelijk te worden van je broeders en zusters. Wanneer het krijgen van je zin niet meer belangrijk voor ons is, dan, als we onze zin niet krijgen, is dat voor ons prima. Terwijl we ons leven voor elkaar neerleggen, worden we een kracht die de wereld niet begrijpt. De wereld werd eeuwenlang aangetrokken tot de kerk en verlangde wat zij had. Maar verbazingwekkend genoeg lijkt het vandaag alsof de kerk naar de wereld wordt getrokken en verlangt wat die heeft.

Er is kracht in onderwerping. Honderden jaren geleden veroverde een man genaamd Alexander de Grote bijna de gehele toen bekende wereld met militaire kracht en slimheid, afgewisseld met diplomatie.

Het verhaal gaat dat Alexander en een klein gezelschap soldaten een sterk versterkte, ommuurde stad naderden. Buiten de muren staande, verhief Alexander zijn stem en eiste de koning te zien. Toen de koning arriveerde, stond Alexander erop dat de koning de stad en haar inwoners aan Alexander en zijn kleine groep strijders zou overgeven.

De koning lachte: “Waarom zou ik mij aan u overgeven? U kunt ons niets aandoen!” Dus bood Alexander de koning een demonstratie aan. Hij beval zijn mannen in een file op te stellen en te beginnen te marcheren. Hij liet hen recht op een loodrechte klif afmarcheren.

De stadsbewoners verzamelden zich op de muur en keken in geschokte stilte toe hoe, één voor één, Alexanders soldaten zonder aarzelen recht van de klif af marcheerden naar hun dood! Nadat tien soldaten waren gestorven, beval Alexander de rest terug te keren naar zijn zijde. De stadsbewoners en de koning gaven zich onmiddellijk over aan Alexander de Grote. Zij realiseerden zich dat als een paar mannen werkelijk bereid waren zelfmoord te plegen op bevel van deze dynamische leider, dan niets zijn uiteindelijke overwinning kon stoppen.

Onafhankelijkheid

Onderwerping en gehoorzaamheid gaan hand in hand. Als wij bereid zijn ons aan iets of iemand te onderwerpen, zullen wij het ook willen gehoorzamen. Het wordt heel belangrijk om ons te onderwerpen aan degenen die over ons staan, vooral de almachtige God in de hemel. Als we moeite hebben ons te onderwerpen, zullen we meestal ook moeite hebben met gehoorzaamheid. God verhoede dat we gaan geloven dat we beter af zijn alles alleen te doen zonder onze broeders.

Liefde

“Hieraan zullen allen weten dat gij mijn discipelen zijt, indien gij liefde onder elkander hebt” (Joh. 13:35).

Mensen zwaaien naar elkaar bij een kruispunt, of ze houden een deur open voor een oudere persoon. Mensen zijn over het algemeen lief totdat iets niet hun zin gaat. Dan kunnen ze erg moeilijk worden. Is dat de manier waarop de kerk vandaag haar liefde aan de wereld toont? Zolang alles soepel loopt en niemand op onze tenen trapt, komen we allemaal goed overeen en houden we van elkaar. Zodra er echter iets is om over te vechten, trekken we de “bokshandschoenen” aan. Zegt de Bijbel niet dat “de liefde alle dingen bedekt, alle dingen gelooft, alle dingen hoopt, alle dingen verdraagt” (1 Kor. 13:7)? Ware liefde blijkt wanneer we tegenslag ondervinden of wanneer een broeder iets doet dat ons kwetst. Dat is de liefde die de wereld zal laten zien dat wij discipelen van Jezus zijn.

Houden wij genoeg van onze broeder om te helpen wanneer hij in nood is? Misschien dwaalt hij onwetend van God af op een bepaald gebied. Hoeveel houden wij van hem? Sommige mensen denken dat liefde alleen maar gaat over positieve dingen met elkaar bespreken, maar als we werkelijk van onze broeder houden, zullen we in liefde naar hem toegaan en eerlijk met hem spreken. En als wij een levensstijl praktiseren van onszelf verloochenen en ons onderwerpen aan de broeders, zal het goed verlopen. God verhoede dat we ons ergeren aan een broeder die naar ons komt om ons op onze dwaling te wijzen.

Wanneer we ervoor gekozen hebben te lijden met het volk van God en onszelf te verloochenen, dan stellen we het op prijs wanneer een broer of zuster in ons leven spreekt. We zullen ons niet laten kwetsen.

Lijden voor en met elkaar, plus onszelf verloochenen voor elkaar, vormt vaak een vaste liefde voor elkaar. Dit soort liefde is het soort dat de wereld om ons heen niet kent maar sterk verlangt. De wereld wordt naarmate de dagen verstrijken steeds egoïstischer en onafhankelijker. We kunnen het ons niet veroorloven onze kansen te missen om hen de kracht van God te tonen door onze liefde voor elkaar.

Godvrezende mensen door de eeuwen heen hebben hun kans gehad de Koning te dienen en de boodschap van het Koninkrijk van God te verspreiden, maar zij zijn opgeroepen naar de eeuwigheid. Vandaag is het onze beurt. De akkers zijn wit tot de oogst. Laten we ons inzetten en, met Gods hulp, de heerlijke kerk van Jezus Christus bewaren voor onze kinderen, de volgende generatie.

What do we think about when we think of the term ‘church’? We live in a day when there are many and varied churches. If one church doesn’t suit you, there are others to choose from. While some churches encourage their people to live for God and others instead of themselves, other churches promote a gospel that says lots of money and a better life now are the results of following Christ. However, there are still churches that try to follow what the Bible says—Sola scriptura (scripture alone). Traditionally, the conservative Anabaptist churches in America have tried to function in this manner. But is that changing?

We live in a day when lines are being crossed, blurred, and confused. People aren’t sure what is true and what is not. Today, men and women around the world are looking for answers and solutions, but where should they look?

I was talking with a young man who testified of being converted at a young age. He attended church faithfully and was considered quite gifted. But there was a problem—he had a sin that he still could not control. As he wrestled with God and pled for victory, he began to hear a recurring message from other professing Christians, “No one is perfect!” “We all have issues.” “Everyone has sinned!” Finally, this young man accepted his sin as normal. He justified it because it seemed that everyone was saying they had sin also, that they were not living in complete victory. It led this young man to a place of complete ruin.

Are we preaching and accepting a defeated Gospel—a gospel that doesn’t offer complete forgiveness and complete victory? Many youth of today are confused. Many people in today’s world don’t understand. Anyone can go to church and try to be a better person. But what about the all-powerful, life-changing gospel of Jesus Christ?

The apostle Paul says that Jesus is coming back for “. . .a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish” (Eph. 5:27). And Jesus Himself said “. . .That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it” (Matt. 16:18).

Before I was converted, I was certainly a slave to sin, but I wanted victory. I was addicted to drugs and alcohol, but I didn’t like it. I wanted to be free. I went to counseling and rehab facilities all over America, but it didn’t work. I had no power. I could quit for a few days or even weeks, then anger and depression would set in, and I would return to the substances. One day, I came face to face with the Creator. The hand of the almighty God got ahold of me and opened my eyes. I repented of my sins and was given a clean slate and a clean heart. I never went back. Drugs, alcohol, and two packs of cigarettes a day were finished—forever.

I could hardly believe what God was doing. The power of God was real. I could not overcome it by myself, as none of us can, but God has promised us freedom from bondage and a new life of victorious living if we submit our lives to him. This ability to overcome the power of sin and then walk in victory is what the world is looking for. Do we believe that God can free us not only from substance abuse but also from anger, selfishness, bitterness, greed, and pride? God’s Word says “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9). No one is interested in a defeated Gospel, no one except those who are living in defeat because they have chosen the things of this world over God and His Word.

Are we willing to testify of the power of the resurrection? We need to proclaim a gospel that completely saves people from the bondage of sin—forever. We must be bold and confident in our faith so we can lead people to the Master.

I was witnessing to a man when he said in a rather loud voice, “God is not real!” My six-year-old son’s mouth fell open, and he gasped, “Daddy, he just told a lie!”

My son doesn’t need to be convinced that God is real; he believes it with all his heart. The world out there does need to be convinced. They need to see something that science cannot explain. They need to see something that defies all odds.

That something is a heart that has been truly changed. The fighter now loves his enemies. The person with an anger problem now loves others unconditionally. Broken families are healed. Wretched sinners are forgiven and living a transformed life. Hope, peace, love, and power are freely given to men and women who seemingly have no hope. “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them ” (Matt. 11:5).

Are you living your life so the world can see the work of God being practical, effective, and real every day? Here are a few things the Church needs in our day to once again draw in the lost.

A willingness to suffer

History would show that the church, all through the ages, has suffered for Christ. It was part of the cost of following Christ. The Bible says, “Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution” (2 Tim. 3:12). It was something that just happened.

Today, many people want the American dream. Folks live a good moral life, are good citizens, make a good living, and go to church on Sundays. But is that what we are called to? The gospel spread like wildfire when the church suffered persecution and did so willingly and joyfully. It was something the world had never seen—a faith that people showed by their life, and their death was something worth dying for. Let’s not be afraid to suffer for Christ today.

Denial of self

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Matt. 16:24).

Have you ever wondered why Jesus instructs us to deny ourselves? After all, He gave us desires and passions, so why must we deny them? I have heard people say that we need to align our will with God’s, but I do not find this in the Bible. Rather, we should simply deny our will and accept God’s will.

I remember the first day of boot camp when I joined the Marine Corps after graduating from high school. Close to one hundred young men were there. We all had our own desires and thoughts. We had our own identity. It was amazing to see all the diversity. It would have been a disaster if the United States of America had sent us off to battle that first day. So, they had a plan set in place to fix this problem. Over the next three months, they broke us. Physically and mentally, we learned how to deny ourselves and submit to our commanders and each other. The world is often amazed by the great discipline and unity for which the Marines are known.

When we become a part of the kingdom of God, we cannot be effective if we each do what we want. A body of believers can all have good intentions, but if any one person has not denied themselves, they will never be able to submit to the greater cause. There is a war raging, and we cannot fight it alone. We must deny ourselves, join forces with our brethren, and fight for victory in our homes, churches, and lives.

Submission

The Bible calls us to submit ourselves:

  • to God (Jas. 4:7).
  • [to those] that have the [spiritual] rule over you [us] (Heb. 13:17).
  • to every ordinance of man for the Lord’s sake (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • one to another in the fear of God (Eph. 5:21).

Once we deny ourselves, then and only then, can we submit to others. Many people today have great difficulty in submitting to their fellow man. Some feel they are free in Christ; therefore, they can do as they please. There is a reason why we are instructed to submit to others. It is easy for us to drift away from sound doctrine when we believe we can figure everything out on our own.

When we have truly denied ourselves, we find that it is rather easy, and even a great blessing, to submit to the brotherhood. In fact, it is true freedom. What you want doesn’t matter, and you begin to depend on your brothers and sisters. When getting our own way isn’t important to us, then when we don’t get our way, we are fine with it. As we lay down our lives for each other, we become a force that the world doesn’t understand. The world was drawn to the church for centuries, wanting what it had. But amazingly, today, it seems the church is being drawn to the world, wanting what it has.

There is power in submission. Hundreds of years ago, a man named Alexander the Great conquered almost all of the then-known world using military strength and cleverness mixed with diplomacy.

The story is told that Alexander and a small company of soldiers approached a strongly fortified, walled city. Standing outside the walls, Alexander raised his voice and demanded to see the king. When the king arrived, Alexander insisted that the king surrender the city and its inhabitants to Alexander and his little band of fighting men.

The king laughed, “Why should I surrender to you? You can’t do us any harm!” So, Alexander offered to give the king a demonstration. He ordered his men to line up single file and start marching. He marched them straight toward a sheer cliff.

The townspeople gathered on the wall and watched in shocked silence as, one by one, Alexander’s soldiers marched, without hesitation, right off the cliff to their deaths! After ten soldiers died, Alexander ordered the rest of the men to return to his side. The townspeople and the king immediately surrendered to Alexander the Great. They realized that if a few men were actually willing to commit suicide at the command of this dynamic leader, then nothing could stop his eventual victory.

Obedience

Submission and obedience go hand in hand. If we are willing to submit to something or someone, we will want to obey it. It becomes very important to submit to those who are over us, especially the almighty God in Heaven. If we struggle to submit, we will usually struggle with obedience. God forbid if we begin to believe that we are better off doing things alone without our brothers.

Love

“By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another” (John 13:35).

People wave to each other at an intersection, or they will open the door for an elderly person. People are generally loving people until something doesn’t go their way. Then they can become very difficult. Is that the way the church today is showing its love to the world? As long as everything is going smoothly, and no one steps on our toes, we all get along and we love each other. Then as soon as there is something worth fighting over, we put the “boxing gloves” on. Doesn’t the Bible say that “charity (love) beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things” (1 Cor. 13:7)? True love is revealed when we face adversity or when a brother does something to offend us. That is the love that will show the world we are disciples of Jesus.

Do we love our brother enough to help when he is in need? Maybe he is unknowingly straying away from God in a certain area. How much do we love him? Some people think that love is only talking about positive things with each other, but if we truly love our brother, we will go to him in love and speak honestly with him. Then if we are practicing a lifestyle of denying ourselves and submitting to the brethren, it should go well. God forbid if we get angry with a brother who comes to us to show us our error.

When we have chosen to suffer with the people of God and have denied ourselves, then we appreciate when a brother or sister speaks into our lives. We will not allow ourselves to become offended.

Suffering for and with each other, plus denying ourselves for each other, often forms a solid love for one another. This type of love is the kind that the world around us does not know but desires greatly. The world is getting more selfish and independent as the days pass. We can’t afford to miss our opportunities to show them the power of God with our love for one another.

Godly people throughout the ages have had their opportunity to serve the King and spread the message of the Kingdom of God, but they have moved on to eternity. Today it is our turn. The fields are white unto harvest. Let’s plug in and, with God’s help, preserve the glorious church of Jesus Christ for our children, the next generation.

Woran denken wir, wenn wir den Begriff „Kirche“ hören? Wir leben in einer Zeit, in der es viele verschiedene Kirchen gibt. Passt eine Kirche nicht zu dir, kannst du dir eine andere aussuchen. Während einige Kirchen ihr Volk ermutigen, für Gott zu leben und nicht für sich selbst, predigen andere Gemeinden ein Evangelium, das behauptet, dass viel Geld und ein besseres Leben jetzt die Folge des Nachfolgens Christi seien. Es gibt jedoch nach wie vor Kirchen, die versuchen, dem zu folgen, was die Bibel sagt—Sola scriptura (allein die Schrift). Traditionell haben die konservativen Täufergemeinden in Amerika versucht, auf diese Weise zu funktionieren. Aber ändert sich das?

Wir leben in einer Zeit, in der Grenzen überschritten, verwischt und verwirrt werden. Die Menschen sind sich nicht sicher, was wahr ist und was nicht. Heute suchen Männer und Frauen auf der ganzen Welt nach Antworten und Lösungen, aber wo sollen sie suchen?

Ich sprach mit einem jungen Mann, der bezeugte, schon in jungen Jahren bekehrt worden zu sein. Er besuchte die Kirche treu und galt als ziemlich begabt. Aber es gab ein Problem—er hatte eine Sünde, die er noch immer nicht unter Kontrolle bringen konnte. Während er mit Gott rang und um Sieg flehte, begann er wiederholt die Botschaft anderer sich bekennender Christen zu hören: „Niemand ist perfekt!“ „Wir alle haben Probleme.“ „Jeder hat gesündigt!“ Schließlich akzeptierte dieser junge Mann seine Sünde als normal. Er rechtfertigte sie, weil es schien, als würden alle sagen, dass auch sie Sünde hätten, dass sie nicht in vollständigem Sieg lebten. Es führte diesen jungen Mann an einen Ort völliger Ruine.

Predigen und akzeptieren wir ein besiegtes Evangelium—ein Evangelium, das keine völlige Vergebung und keinen völligen Sieg anbietet? Viele Jugendliche heute sind verwirrt. Viele Menschen in der heutigen Welt verstehen nicht. Jeder kann in die Kirche gehen und versuchen, ein besserer Mensch zu sein. Aber was ist mit dem allmächtigen, lebensverändernden Evangelium von Jesus Christus?

Der Apostel Paulus sagt, dass Jesus zurückkommt für „. . .eine herrliche Gemeinde, ohne Flecken oder Runzeln oder etwas dergleichen; sondern dass sie heilig und untadelig sei“ (Eph. 5:27). Und Jesus selbst sagte „. . .Du bist Petrus, und auf diesen Felsen werde ich meine Kirche bauen; und die Pforten der Hölle sollen sie nicht überwältigen“ (Matt. 16:18).

Bevor ich bekehrt wurde, war ich sicher ein Sklave der Sünde, aber ich wollte Sieg. Ich war drogen- und alkoholabhängig, aber es gefiel mir nicht. Ich wollte frei sein. Ich ging zu Beratungen und Reha-Einrichtungen in ganz Amerika, aber es funktionierte nicht. Ich hatte keine Kraft. Ich konnte ein paar Tage oder sogar Wochen aufhören, dann stellten sich Wut und Depression ein, und ich kehrte zu den Substanzen zurück. Eines Tages stand ich dem Schöpfer von Angesicht zu Angesicht gegenüber. Die Hand des allmächtigen Gottes faßte mich und öffnete mir die Augen. Ich bereute meine Sünden und bekam eine saubere Tafel und ein reines Herz. Ich ging nie zurück. Drogen, Alkohol und zwei Schachteln Zigaretten am Tag waren vorbei—für immer.

Ich konnte kaum glauben, was Gott tat. Die Kraft Gottes war real. Ich konnte sie nicht allein überwinden, so wie keiner von uns es kann, aber Gott hat uns Freiheit von Knechtschaft und ein neues Leben des siegreichen Wandels verheißen, wenn wir unser Leben ihm unterstellen. Diese Fähigkeit, die Macht der Sünde zu überwinden und dann im Sieg zu wandeln, ist das, wonach die Welt sucht. Glauben wir, dass Gott uns nicht nur von Substanzmissbrauch befreien kann, sondern auch von Wut, Selbstsucht, Bitterkeit, Gier und Stolz? Gottes Wort sagt: „Wenn wir unsere Sünden bekennen, so ist er treu und gerecht, dass er uns die Sünden vergibt und uns reinigt von aller Ungerechtigkeit“ (1 John 1:9). Niemand ist an einem besiegten Evangelium interessiert, niemand—außer denen, die in Niederlage leben, weil sie die Dinge dieser Welt über Gott und sein Wort gestellt haben.

Sind wir bereit, von der Kraft der Auferstehung zu zeugen? Wir müssen ein Evangelium verkündigen, das Menschen völlig von der Knechtschaft der Sünde rettet—für immer. Wir müssen mutig und zuversichtlich in unserem Glauben sein, damit wir Menschen zum Meister führen können.

Ich bezeugte einem Mann, als er ziemlich laut sagte: „Gott ist nicht real!“ Der Mund meines sechsjährigen Sohnes stand offen, und er schnappte: „Daddy, er hat gerade gelogen!“

Mein Sohn muss nicht davon überzeugt werden, dass Gott real ist; er glaubt es von ganzem Herzen. Die Welt da draußen muss überzeugt werden. Sie müssen etwas sehen, das die Wissenschaft nicht erklären kann. Sie müssen etwas sehen, das allen Erwartungen widerspricht.

Dieses Etwas ist ein Herz, das wirklich verwandelt worden ist. Der Kämpfer liebt jetzt seine Feinde. Der Mensch mit Wutproblemen liebt jetzt bedingungslos andere. Zerbrochene Familien werden geheilt. Armselige Sünder werden vergeben und leben ein verwandtes Leben. Hoffnung, Frieden, Liebe und Kraft werden Männern und Frauen frei gegeben, die scheinbar keine Hoffnung haben. „Die Blinden sehen, die Lahmen gehen, die Aussätzigen werden gereinigt, die Tauben hören, die Toten werden auferweckt, und den Armen wird das Evangelium gepredigt“ (Matt. 11:5).

Lebst du dein Leben so, dass die Welt die praktische, wirksame und reale Arbeit Gottes jeden Tag sehen kann? Hier sind ein paar Dinge, die die Kirche in unserer Zeit braucht, um wieder die Verlorenen anzuziehen.

Die Bereitschaft zu leiden

Die Geschichte zeigt, dass die Kirche durch alle Zeiten hindurch um Christi willen gelitten hat. Es war Teil der Kosten, Christus nachzufolgen. Die Bibel sagt: „Ja, und alle, die fromm leben wollen in Christus Jesus, werden Verfolgung erleiden“ (2 Tim. 3:12). Es war etwas, das einfach geschah.

Heute wollen viele Menschen den amerikanischen Traum. Die Leute führen ein gutes moralisches Leben, sind gute Bürger, verdienen gut und gehen sonntags in die Kirche. Aber dazu sind wir berufen? Das Evangelium verbreitete sich wie ein Lauffeuer, als die Kirche Verfolgung erlitt und dies bereitwillig und freudig tat. Es war etwas, das die Welt noch nie gesehen hatte—ein Glaube, den die Menschen durch ihr Leben zeigten, und ihr Tod war etwas, wofür es sich zu sterben lohnte. Fürchten wir uns nicht davor, heute für Christus zu leiden.

Selbstverleugnung

Da sprach Jesus zu seinen Jüngern: „Wenn jemand mir nachkommen will, der verleugne sich selbst und nehme sein Kreuz auf sich und folge mir nach“ (Matt. 16:24).

Hast du dich jemals gefragt, warum Jesus uns anweist, uns selbst zu verleugnen? Schließlich hat er uns Begierden und Leidenschaften gegeben, warum sollen wir sie dann verleugnen? Ich habe Leute sagen hören, dass wir unseren Willen mit Gottes Willen in Einklang bringen müssen, aber das finde ich nicht in der Bibel. Vielmehr sollten wir einfach unseren Willen verleugnen und Gottes Willen annehmen.

Ich erinnere mich an den ersten Tag im Bootcamp, als ich nach dem Highschool-Abschluss dem Marine Corps beitrat. Es waren fast einhundert junge Männer dort. Wir hatten alle unsere eigenen Wünsche und Gedanken. Wir hatten unsere eigene Identität. Es war erstaunlich, all diese Verschiedenheit zu sehen. Es wäre eine Katastrophe gewesen, wenn die Vereinigten Staaten von Amerika uns an diesem ersten Tag in den Kampf hätten schicken können. Also hatten sie einen Plan, um dieses Problem zu lösen. Im Verlauf der nächsten drei Monate brachen sie uns. Körperlich und geistig lernten wir, uns selbst zu verleugnen und uns unseren Kommandeuren und einander zu unterstellen. Die Welt ist oft erstaunt über die große Disziplin und Einheit, für die die Marines bekannt sind.

Wenn wir Teil des Reiches Gottes werden, können wir nicht wirksam sein, wenn jeder tut, was er will. Eine Gemeinschaft von Gläubigen kann alle gute Absichten haben, aber wenn auch nur eine Person sich nicht selbst verleugnet hat, wird sie sich niemals dem größeren Ziel unterordnen können. Es tobt ein Krieg, und wir können ihn nicht allein kämpfen. Wir müssen uns selbst verleugnen, uns mit unseren Brüdern zusammenschließen und für den Sieg in unseren Häusern, Kirchen und Leben kämpfen.

Unterordnung

Die Bibel ruft uns zur Unterordnung auf:

  • gegenüber Gott (Jas. 4:7).
  • [gegenüber denen], die die [geistliche] Leitung über euch [uns] haben (Heb. 13:17).
  • gegenüber jeder menschlichen Anordnung um des Herrn willen (1 Pet. 2:13).
  • einer dem anderen in der Furcht Gottes (Eph. 5:21).

Wenn wir uns selbst verleugnet haben, dann und nur dann können wir uns anderen unterordnen. Viele Menschen haben heute große Schwierigkeiten, sich ihrem Mitmenschen zu unterstellen. Einige fühlen sich in Christus frei; daher können sie tun, was sie wollen. Es gibt einen Grund, warum wir angewiesen werden, uns anderen zu unterordnen. Es ist leicht für uns, von gesunder Lehre abzuweichen, wenn wir glauben, alles allein herausfinden zu können.

Wenn wir uns wirklich selbst verleugnet haben, stellen wir fest, dass es ziemlich einfach und sogar ein großer Segen ist, sich der Bruderschaft zu unterordnen. Tatsächlich ist es wahre Freiheit. Was du willst, spielt keine Rolle mehr, und du beginnst, dich auf deine Brüder und Schwestern zu verlassen. Wenn es uns nicht wichtig ist, unseren eigenen Willen durchzusetzen, dann sind wir auch dann zufrieden, wenn es nicht nach unserem Willen geht. Indem wir unser Leben füreinander hingeben, werden wir zu einer Kraft, die die Welt nicht versteht. Die Welt wurde über Jahrhunderte von der Kirche angezogen und begehrte, was sie hatte. Aber erstaunlicherweise scheint heute die Kirche zur Welt hingezogen zu werden und begehrt, was sie hat.

In der Unterordnung liegt Macht. Vor Hunderten von Jahren eroberte ein Mann namens Alexander der Große nahezu die damals bekannte Welt durch militärische Stärke und Klugheit, gemischt mit Diplomatie.

Es wird erzählt, dass Alexander und eine kleine Gruppe Soldaten sich einer stark befestigten, von Mauern umgebenen Stadt näherten. Vor den Mauern stehend erhob Alexander seine Stimme und verlangte, den König zu sehen. Als der König erschien, bestand Alexander darauf, dass der König die Stadt und ihre Bewohner an Alexander und seine kleine Schar kämpfender Männer übergibt.

Der König lachte: „Warum sollte ich mich dir ergeben? Du kannst uns keinen Schaden zufügen!“ Daraufhin bot Alexander dem König eine Demonstration an. Er befahl seinen Männern, sich in Einerreihe aufzustellen und zu beginnen zu marschieren. Er marschierte sie geradewegs auf eine steile Klippe zu.

Die Stadtbewohner versammelten sich auf der Mauer und sahen in schockiertem Schweigen zu, wie nacheinander Alexanders Soldaten ohne Zögern direkt von der Klippe in den Tod marschierten! Nachdem zehn Soldaten gestorben waren, befahl Alexander den übrigen Männern, zu seiner Seite zurückzukehren. Die Stadtbewohner und der König ergaben sich sofort Alexander dem Großen. Sie erkannten, dass, wenn einige Männer tatsächlich bereit waren, auf Befehl dieses dynamischen Führers Selbstmord zu begehen, nichts seinen endgültigen Sieg aufhalten konnte.

Gehorsam

Unterordnung und Gehorsam gehen Hand in Hand. Wenn wir bereit sind, uns etwas oder jemandem zu unterordnen, werden wir es auch befolgen wollen. Es wird sehr wichtig, uns denen zu unterordnen, die über uns stehen, besonders dem allmächtigen Gott im Himmel. Wenn wir uns mit Unterordnung schwertun, werden wir gewöhnlich auch mit dem Gehorsam kämpfen. Gott bewahre, dass wir beginnen zu glauben, wir seien besser dran, die Dinge allein ohne unsere Brüder zu tun.

Liebe

„Darauf werden alle erkennen, dass ihr meine Jünger seid, wenn ihr Liebe untereinander habt“ (John 13:35).

Menschen winken einander an einer Kreuzung, oder sie öffnen einer älteren Person die Tür. Menschen sind im Allgemeinen liebevoll, bis etwas nicht nach ihrem Willen geht. Dann können sie sehr schwierig werden. Ist das die Weise, wie die Kirche heute ihre Liebe der Welt zeigt? Solange alles glatt läuft und niemand auf unsere Füße tritt, verstehen wir uns und lieben einander. Sobald es jedoch etwas gibt, wofür es sich zu kämpfen lohnt, ziehen wir die „Boxhandschuhe“ an. Steht nicht in der Bibel, dass „die Liebe alles erträgt, alles glaubt, alles hofft, alles duldet“ (1 Cor. 13:7)? Wahre Liebe zeigt sich, wenn wir Widrigkeiten gegenüberstehen oder wenn ein Bruder uns etwas antut, das uns verletzt. Das ist die Liebe, die der Welt zeigen wird, dass wir Jünger Jesu sind.

Lieben wir unseren Bruder genug, um zu helfen, wenn er in Not ist? Vielleicht entfernt er sich unwissentlich in einem bestimmten Bereich von Gott. Wie sehr lieben wir ihn? Manche Menschen denken, Liebe bedeute nur, positive Dinge miteinander zu besprechen, aber wenn wir unseren Bruder wirklich lieben, gehen wir in Liebe zu ihm und sprechen ehrlich mit ihm. Wenn wir dann einen Lebensstil der Selbstverleugnung und Unterordnung gegenüber den Brüdern praktizieren, sollte es gut gehen. Gott bewahre, wenn wir zornig werden auf einen Bruder, der zu uns kommt, um uns unseren Irrtum zu zeigen.

Wenn wir uns entschieden haben, mit dem Volk Gottes zu leiden und uns selbst zu verleugnen, dann schätzen wir es, wenn ein Bruder oder eine Schwester in unser Leben spricht. Wir werden uns nicht leicht verletzen lassen.

Leiden für und miteinander, dazu die Selbstverleugnung füreinander, bildet oft eine feste Liebe zueinander. Diese Art von Liebe ist die, die die Welt um uns nicht kennt, aber sehr begehrt. Die Welt wird mit jedem Tag egoistischer und unabhängiger. Wir können es uns nicht leisten, unsere Gelegenheiten zu verpassen, ihnen die Kraft Gottes durch unsere Liebe zueinander zu zeigen.

Gottesfürchtige Menschen durch die Zeiten hatten ihre Gelegenheit, dem König zu dienen und die Botschaft des Reiches Gottes zu verbreiten, aber sie sind in die Ewigkeit gegangen. Heute sind wir an der Reihe. Die Felder sind weiß zur Ernte. Packen wir mit an und bewahren mit Gottes Hilfe die herrliche Kirche Jesu Christi für unsere Kinder, die nächste Generation.

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.

Nå er det vinter; den falne snø
har latt himmelen kaldt og klar bli se;
gjennom bladløse greiner blåser den skarpe vind,
og all jord ligger død og sørgmodig hen.

Og likevel er ikke Guds kjærlighet borte;
hans liv i den klare luft ånder frem;
hans skjønnhet maler morgengryets røde porte,
og kler hver kvist med glitrende krans og lem.

Og selv om ute den skarpe vinden går,
og himmelen er kald, og frostene bite hardt,
trekker hjemmet sin sirkel nærmere nås,
og varmere gløder lyset innvendig og sart.

O Gud, du gir vinterens kulde også,
likeså som sommerens glade stråler gi;
du varmer oss i din kjærlighet og låser,
og vokter oss gjennom livets vintersti.
