O que pensamos quando pensamos no termo “igreja”? Vivemos numa época em que há muitas e variadas igrejas. Se uma igreja não lhe agrada, há outras para escolher. Enquanto algumas igrejas incentivam seu povo a viver para Deus e para os outros em vez de si mesmos, outras promovem um evangelho que diz que muito dinheiro e uma vida melhor agora são o resultado de seguir Cristo. No entanto, ainda existem igrejas que tentam seguir o que a Bíblia diz—Sola scriptura (somente as Escrituras). Tradicionalmente, as igrejas anabatistas conservadoras na América tentaram funcionar dessa maneira. Mas isso está mudando?

Vivemos em um tempo em que linhas estão sendo cruzadas, embaçadas e confundidas. As pessoas não têm certeza do que é verdadeiro e do que não é. Hoje, homens e mulheres ao redor do mundo procuram respostas e soluções, mas onde devem procurar?

Eu estava conversando com um jovem que testemunhou ter sido convertido quando era pequeno. Ele frequentava a igreja fielmente e era considerado bastante dotado. Mas havia um problema—ele tinha um pecado que ainda não conseguia controlar. Enquanto ele wrestlava com Deus e suplicava por vitória, começou a ouvir uma mensagem recorrente de outros cristãos professos: “Ninguém é perfeito!” “Todos nós temos problemas.” “Todo mundo pecou!” Finalmente, esse jovem aceitou seu pecado como normal. Ele o justificou porque parecia que todos também diziam ter pecado, que não viviam em completa vitória. Isso levou esse jovem a um lugar de ruína completa.

Estamos pregando e aceitando um evangelho derrotado—um evangelho que não oferece perdão completo e vitória completa? Muitos jovens hoje estão confusos. Muitas pessoas no mundo de hoje não entendem. Qualquer um pode ir à igreja e tentar ser uma pessoa melhor. Mas e o evangelho onipotente e transformador de vida de Jesus Cristo?

O apóstolo Paulo diz que Jesus está voltando por “. . .uma igreja gloriosa, que não tenha mancha, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante; antes que seja santa e irrepreensível” (Efés. 5:27). E o próprio Jesus disse “. . .Que tu és Pedro, e sobre esta pedra edificarei a minha igreja; e as portas do inferno não prevalecerão contra ela” (Mat. 16:18).

Antes de ser convertido, eu certamente era escravo do pecado, mas eu queria vitória. Eu era viciado em drogas e álcool, mas não gostava disso. Eu queria ficar livre. Fui a conselhos e centros de reabilitação por toda a América, mas não funcionou. Eu não tinha poder. Eu podia parar por alguns dias ou até semanas, então a ira e a depressão surgiam, e eu voltava às substâncias. Um dia, eu me encontrei face a face com o Criador. A mão do Deus todo-poderoso me agarrou e abriu meus olhos. Arrependi-me dos meus pecados e me foi dado um novo começo e um coração limpo. Eu nunca voltei atrás. Drogas, álcool e dois maços de cigarros por dia acabaram—para sempre.

Mal podia acreditar no que Deus estava fazendo. O poder de Deus era real. Eu não podia vencê-lo sozinho, assim como nenhum de nós pode, mas Deus nos prometeu liberdade da escravidão e uma nova vida de vitória se submetermos nossas vidas a ele. Essa habilidade de vencer o poder do pecado e então andar em vitória é o que o mundo está procurando. Acreditamos que Deus pode nos libertar não apenas do abuso de substâncias, mas também da ira, do egoísmo, da amargura, da ganância e do orgulho? A Palavra de Deus diz “Se confessarmos os nossos pecados, ele é fiel e justo para nos perdoar os pecados e nos purificar de toda injustiça” (1 João 1:9). Ninguém está interessado em um evangelho derrotado, ninguém exceto aqueles que vivem na derrota porque escolheram as coisas deste mundo acima de Deus e da Sua Palavra.

Estamos dispostos a testemunhar o poder da ressurreição? Precisamos proclamar um evangelho que salve completamente as pessoas da escravidão do pecado—para sempre. Devemos ser ousados e confiantes em nossa fé para que possamos conduzir as pessoas ao Mestre.

Eu estava testemunhando a um homem quando ele disse em voz bastante alta: “Deus não é real!” A boca do meu filho de seis anos ficou aberta, e ele ofegou: “Papai, ele acabou de falar uma mentira!”

Meu filho não precisa ser convencido de que Deus é real; ele crê com todo o coração. O mundo lá fora precisa ser convencido. Precisa ver algo que a ciência não pode explicar. Precisa ver algo que desafie todas as probabilidades.

Esse algo é um coração que foi verdadeiramente mudado. O lutador agora ama seus inimigos. A pessoa com problema de raiva agora ama os outros incondicionalmente. Famílias quebradas são curadas. Pecadores miseráveis são perdoados e vivem uma vida transformada. Esperança, paz, amor e poder são dados livremente a homens e mulheres que aparentemente não têm esperança. “Os cegos recebem a vista, e os coxos andam, os leprosos são limpos, e os surdos ouvem, os mortos são ressuscitados, e aos pobres é pregado o evangelho” (Mat. 11:5).

Você está vivendo sua vida para que o mundo veja a obra de Deus sendo prática, eficaz e real todos os dias? Eis algumas coisas que a Igreja precisa em nosso tempo para, mais uma vez, atrair os perdidos.

Disposição para sofrer

A história mostra que a igreja, através das eras, sofreu por Cristo. Era parte do custo de seguir Cristo. A Bíblia diz, “E todos os que querem viver piedosamente em Cristo Jesus padecerão perseguições” (2 Tim. 3:12). Era algo que simplesmente acontecia.

Hoje, muitas pessoas querem o sonho americano. Gente leva uma boa vida moral, são bons cidadãos, ganham bem a vida e vão à igreja aos domingos. Mas será isso a que somos chamados? O evangelho se espalhou como fogo quando a igreja sofreu perseguição e o fez voluntariamente e com alegria. Era algo que o mundo nunca tinha visto—uma fé que as pessoas mostravam pela sua vida, e sua morte era algo pelo qual valia a pena morrer. Não tenhamos medo de sofrer por Cristo hoje.

Negação de si mesmo

Então disse Jesus aos seus discípulos: “Se alguém quer vir após mim, negue-se a si mesmo, e tome a sua cruz, e siga-me” (Mat. 16:24).

Alguma vez você já se perguntou por que Jesus nos instrui a nos negar? Afinal, Ele nos deu desejos e paixões, então por que devemos negá-los? Já ouvi pessoas dizerem que precisamos alinhar nossa vontade com a de Deus, mas eu não encontro isso na Bíblia. Antes, devemos simplesmente negar a nossa vontade e aceitar a vontade de Deus.

Lembro-me do primeiro dia do campo de treinamento quando entrei na Marinha de Fuzileiros depois de me formar no ensino médio. Quase cem jovens estavam lá. Todos nós tínhamos nossos próprios desejos e pensamentos. Tínhamos nossa própria identidade. Era impressionante ver toda a diversidade. Teria sido um desastre se os Estados Unidos da América nos tivessem mandado para a batalha nesse primeiro dia. Então, eles tinham um plano em ação para resolver esse problema. Ao longo dos próximos três meses, nos quebraram. Física e mentalmente, aprendemos a nos negar e a nos submeter aos nossos comandantes e uns aos outros. O mundo muitas vezes fica surpreso com a grande disciplina e unidade pelas quais os fuzileiros são conhecidos.

Quando nos tornamos parte do reino de Deus, não podemos ser eficazes se cada um fizer o que quiser. Um corpo de crentes pode ter todas as boas intenções, mas se qualquer pessoa não se negou, nunca será capaz de se submeter à causa maior. Há uma guerra em andamento, e não podemos lutar sozinhos. Devemos negar a nós mesmos, unir forças com nossos irmãos e lutar pela vitória em nossos lares, igrejas e vidas.

Submissão

A Bíblia nos chama a nos submeter:

  • a Deus (Tg. 4:7).
  • [àqueles] que têm o governo [espiritual] sobre vós [nós] (Heb. 13:17).
  • a toda autoridade humana por amor do Senhor (1 Pd. 2:13).
  • uns aos outros no temor de Deus (Ef. 5:21).

Uma vez que nos negamos, então e somente então, podemos nos submeter aos outros. Muitas pessoas hoje têm grande dificuldade em se submeter ao seu semelhante. Alguns sentem que são livres em Cristo; portanto, podem fazer o que bem entendem. Há uma razão pela qual somos instruídos a nos submeter aos outros. É fácil nos afastarmos da sã doutrina quando acreditamos que podemos resolver tudo por conta própria.

Quando realmente nos negamos, achamos que é relativamente fácil, e até uma grande bênção, submeter-nos à fraternidade. De fato, é verdadeira liberdade. O que você deseja não importa, e você passa a depender de seus irmãos e irmãs. Quando conseguir o nosso próprio caminho deixa de ser importante para nós, então, quando não conseguimos o nosso caminho, ficamos bem com isso. Ao deitarmos nossas vidas uns pelos outros, nos tornamos uma força que o mundo não entende. O mundo foi atraído para a igreja por séculos, desejando o que ela tinha. Mas, surpreendentemente, hoje parece que a igreja está sendo atraída para o mundo, desejando o que ele tem.

Há poder na submissão. Há centenas de anos, um homem chamado Alexandre, o Grande, conquistou quase todo o mundo então conhecido usando força militar e astúcia misturadas com diplomacia.

Conta-se que Alexandre e uma pequena companhia de soldados aproximaram-se de uma cidade fortemente fortificada, murada. Parado fora dos muros, Alexandre levantou a voz e exigiu ver o rei. Quando o rei apareceu, Alexandre insistiu que o rei rendesse a cidade e seus habitantes a Alexandre e sua pequena banda de homens de combate.

O rei riu, “Por que eu deveria me render a você? Você não pode nos fazer mal!” Então, Alexandre ofereceu ao rei uma demonstração. Ordenou que seus homens se alinhassem em fila indiana e começassem a marchar. Ele os fez marchar em direção a um precipício vertical.

Os moradores reuniram-se no muro e assistiram em silêncio chocado enquanto, um por um, os soldados de Alexandre marchavam, sem hesitar, direto para o precipício até morrer! Depois que dez soldados morreram, Alexandre ordenou que o restante voltasse para seu lado. Os moradores e o rei imediatamente se renderam a Alexandre, o Grande. Perceberam que se alguns homens estavam realmente dispostos a cometer suicídio ao comando desse líder dinâmico, então nada poderia deter sua vitória eventual.

Obediência

Submissão e obediência andam de mãos dadas. Se estamos dispostos a nos submeter a algo ou a alguém, quereremos obedecê-lo. Torna-se muito importante submeter-se aos que estão sobre nós, especialmente ao Deus todo-poderoso no Céu. Se tivermos dificuldade em nos submeter, geralmente teremos dificuldade com a obediência. Deus nos livre se começarmos a crer que é melhor fazermos as coisas sozinhos, sem nossos irmãos.

Amor

“Nisto conhecerão todos que sois meus discípulos, que vos haveis amor uns aos outros” (João 13:35).

Pessoas acenam umas para as outras em um cruzamento, ou abrem a porta para um idoso. As pessoas são geralmente amorosas até que algo não saia como querem. Então podem tornar-se muito difíceis. É assim que a igreja hoje mostra seu amor ao mundo? Contanto que tudo esteja andando bem, e ninguém pise em nossos calos, todos nos damos bem e nos amamos. Então, assim que há algo que vale a pena lutar, colocamos as “luvas de boxe”. Não diz a Bíblia que “o amor tudo sofre, tudo crê, tudo espera, tudo suporta” (1 Cor. 13:7)? O amor verdadeiro se revela quando enfrentamos adversidade ou quando um irmão faz algo para nos ofender. Esse é o amor que mostrará ao mundo que somos discípulos de Jesus.

Amamos nosso irmão o suficiente para ajudar quando ele precisa? Talvez ele esteja, sem saber, se desviando de Deus em alguma área. Quanto o amamos? Algumas pessoas pensam que o amor é apenas falar de coisas positivas entre si, mas se realmente amarmos nosso irmão, iremos até ele com amor e falaremos honestamente com ele. Então, se estivermos praticando um estilo de vida de nos negar e de nos submeter à fraternidade, isso deve correr bem. Deus nos livre de nos zangarmos com um irmão que vem nos mostrar nosso erro.

Quando escolhemos sofrer com o povo de Deus e nos negar, então apreciamos quando um irmão ou irmã fala em nossas vidas. Não nos permitiremos ficar ofendidos.

Sofrer por e com os outros, além de nos negarmos por eles, frequentemente forma um amor sólido uns pelos outros. Esse tipo de amor é o que o mundo ao nosso redor não conhece, mas deseja profundamente. O mundo está se tornando mais egoísta e independente com o passar dos dias. Não podemos nos dar ao luxo de perder nossas oportunidades de mostrar-lhes o poder de Deus com nosso amor uns pelos outros.

Pessoas piedosas através das eras tiveram sua oportunidade de servir ao Rei e de espalhar a mensagem do Reino de Deus, mas elas partiram para a eternidade. Hoje é a nossa vez. Os campos estão brancos para a ceifa. Vamos nos engajar e, com a ajuda de Deus, preservar a igreja gloriosa de Jesus Cristo para os nossos filhos, a próxima geração.

City of God, how broad and far
outspread thy walls sublime!
The true thy chartered freemen are
of every age and clime:

One holy church, one army strong,
one steadfast, high intent;
one working band, one harvest-song,
one King omnipotent.

How purely hath thy speech come down
from man's primaeval youth!
How grandly hath thine empire grown
of freedom, love, and truth!

How gleam thy watch-fires through the night
with never-fainting ray!
How rise thy towers, serene and bright,
to meet the dawning day!

In vain the surge's angry shock,
in vain the drifting sands:
unharmed upon the eternal Rock
the eternal city stands.

Cité de Dieu, comme sont vastes et lointaines
tes murailles étendues et sublimes !
Les vrais, tes hommes affranchis, sont
de tout âge et de tout climat :

Une sainte Église, une armée puissante,
une ferme et haute intention ;
une même cohorte laborieuse, un seul chant de moisson,
un seul Roi tout-puissant.

Comme ta parole est descendue purement
de la prime jeunesse de l'homme !
Comme ton empire a grandi avec grandeur
de liberté, d'amour et de vérité !

Comme brillent tes feux de veille à travers la nuit
d'un rayon ne faiblissant jamais !
Comme s'élèvent tes tours, sereines et lumineuses,
pour accueillir le jour naissant !

En vain le choc furieux des flots,
en vain les sables mouvants :
indemne sur le Rocher éternel
la cité éternelle demeure.

And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter (John 10:22).

As the maddening winds howl about him, man turns his collar to the cold and damp. Little praise arises for the season that greets him at his weakest point and seeks to discomfort and discourage him from the zest of life. Winter settles in as a formidable authority and arouses anxiety not so much by the infliction of pain but the removal of the pleasant. As we cross the equinox, “the days get longer, and winter gets stronger”, states the old proverb, and it remains incisively correct.

Winter is the season of profound, persistent cold that drives the frost deeper and thickens the ice on the ponds. Man and beast battle its ferocity, and even the lifeless machinery rebels against winter’s adamant arrival. Chilly drafts penetrate every crack and crevice, forcing their heartless presence into the most private chambers. As the woodpiles shrink, utility bills increase in the struggle to resist winter’s array of armed forces. While a few gay tunes, such as Winter Wonderland, seek to capitalize upon its majestic moments, winter is generally despised by the normal inhabitants of this earth. We grimace under the menacing icy grip that holds us captive and longingly anticipate its eventual release.

Spring may have its equal share of soggy and uncomfortable appointments and ragged days. Northern tradition states that the robins must get snowed on three times before the full arrival of spring. But springtime is never void of the hope and glory of better days ahead. Summer can be unbearable with its burning heat and humidity, but it bears a semblance of blessed fruitfulness on every side, and few will slow their activities to notice its discomforts. The autumn days carry their nostalgic enchantment while the beauty of nature is painted in the most remarkable colors on the foliage of the landscape. The bounties of harvest provide an aura of rejoicing in their sheaves, and man’s heart is still merry with the prospects of maturing life. And then comes . . .

Winter

Our Lord experienced the fullness of it; probably not the fullness of the natural elements that those of us in the northern climates face, but the season of apparent fruitlessness. Some said, “He hath a devil, and is mad; why hear ye him?” (John 10:20). At a time when there was to be a feast of dedication, “it was winter.” There was a massive division among the people. Confusion reigned on every side. Jesus had just healed a blind man, and the Jews cast him out of the temple. Such fruitless and cold stony hearts inhabited the fields that were acclaimed to be “white unto harvest.” The icy grips of sin had hardened the hearts of humanity, and the meadows of religion were littered with barren stalks draped with the remains of empty husks. The beloved disciple wasted no words when he brought us the fact that . . . it was winter.

“Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: thou hast made summer and winter” (Psalm 74:17).

It is easy to believe that God has created summertime. The tunes on a perfect summer day sing to us of the Divine. The beauty revolving about us everywhere speaks of His presence. The cheering birds in every tree, the warmth of the pleasant sunshine, and the amazing prodigy of life draw our hearts to the Giver by a thousand invisible filaments of life. These all testify to the truth that “Thou hast made summer.”

The days of winter are different. “Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?” (John 1:46). We share similar sentiments to those of Nathaniel toward the winter months, for it is not so easy to see the hand of God there. There is a great deal of suffering and rejection that we feel penetrating our inner man. I obviously speak not to the season within nature but to the seasons of life that parallel its existence. We do well to aid our frail faith by some solid affirmation that God has made winter, as well, and that we ought not to doubt His divine purposes in it. What, but a season of chilling despair and discomfort can arouse our apathetic souls to . . .

Appreciation

Absence makes the heart grow fonder. Thus does the advent of winter incite our appreciation for summer. We would be blind if summer were perpetually present. It has been aptly said that our dear ones are only ours when we have lost them. When the winter season finally claims their last breath, we then begin to appreciate them for who they really were. It is not the man with an abundance of uninterrupted health who feels most deeply the value of his well-being. That realization arrives on his doorstep the day his health is shattered. There have been many wealthy men who had previously known the stark bareness of bankruptcy. This indelibly embossed a permanent mark in their character that fitted them for the success that followed in its wake.

So the Christian will often experience a season of winter—a time when all that he had labored over, longed for and loved lies languishing beneath the mounds of sterile hopeless drifts. John the Baptist prophesied boldly while the vision was fresh and the crowds pressed around to hear him preach. But the dark and cold prison cell was difficult for him to appreciate. Yet, God has made winter, and these seasons in our lives are paramount to our spiritual well-being.

Strengthening

In the 1700s, a luthier by the name of Stradivari created violins unequaled in their excellence for beautiful sound. As modern experts puzzled long over their inability to create a similar instrument, most have resolved that the wood of the day had been seasoned by difficult winters, producing a quality that cannot be replicated in our day. All nature strains under the duress of the winter months, and man is not exempt. The short days and deep, brazen chill of the night apply a great demand upon our will. In summer, it is comparatively easy to get out of bed at the appointed hour. The earth is warm, the birds are busy singing, and the light is streaming through the open windows. But in the dark of a frigid winter morning, to fling back the covers and arise in a triumphant air is a challenging proposition. It demands a solid resolution to achieve and makes a failure out of many good intentions.

As we broaden that thought to encompass the soul of man, we reach a truth that cannot be denied. Those who have borne the deep burdens of hard living have an innate strength ingrained in their character that those of a mild environment cannot apprehend. The moral character of Adonijah had eroded, for “his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so?” (1 Kings 1:6). This is the bane of easy living. Those who will insulate themselves on every side from the buffeting of winter will, no doubt, incur a weakening of the will. Those who can conquer their will in the presence of a blatantly cold society are on the highway to success. Summer is languid; but winter makes us resolute. We need to do things even when we don’t feel like doing them. And thus, God has made the winter.

Togetherness

“If two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?” (Ecc. 4:11). There is no need for such togetherness in the summer—and no desire for it either. The crackling stove has a mesmerizing effect upon the household members and most of our winter evening activities center around it. We speak in the same breath, of hearth and home, and it is in winter that the hearth glows and love grows.

There are but shallow relationships among those who have known no hardship. It takes the heavy austerity of winter to perform the genius of love in our hearts. Adversity levels the playing field, while sage and simpleton pull together in the same yoke. Often, as death wraps its cold fingers around a frail body, loved ones rush to the bedside. Past grievances are forgotten in the solemnity of the moment. It was at the gates of winter that “Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age” (Genesis 25:8). It is here that the separating curtains of the long-standing conflict between Isaac and Ishmael abated and a joint effort between the two brothers “buried him in the cave of Machpelah”.

While none of us shall ever hope for the political unrest that would bring persecution and the removal of religious freedom from our land, it is still my belief that our carnal church divisions will cease upon its advent. It takes winter to pull us together, and Christ was the vehicle upon whom it rode in. “It was winter. And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch” (John 10:23). There, before the inauguration of His death, His disciples were all pushing for the head of the line and striving to be the greatest. Now, after the cold harsh removal of the green tree, they were all found to be “with one accord in Solomon’s porch” (Acts 5:12). Such is the ministry of winter that our God has gifted us with.

Sympathy

For some reason, it seems that we must receive a full dosage of maltreatment before the door of our hearts is unlocked to thoughts of the sorrowful plight of others. One can only wonder what the Good Samaritan must have experienced to be so thoroughly moved by the scene of the man in the ditch. Did not the Jews paint a fresh emblem of hatred and disdain before him on the canvas of each new day? For some, the ill-treatment has a tendency to harden the heart. These go through life in reclusive fashion, with bitterness and spite at the helm of their ship. Any acquaintances that remotely fail their discrimination are categorized as suspect, and avoided.

There are others who have endured the cold blast of winter and loathe that any should have to experience the same. These hearts are quickly aroused to pity and carry bias sympathy toward those of similar plight. Even the rich man who met his wintry death and was now in eternal hell was moved to extend mercy to his five brethren who were bound for the same dreadful destination. How much more should our sluggish hearts stir to charity when met with such discomforts as spiritual winter? Can we greet our fellow man with the same stern, icy glare that has smitten us in the face in bygone days? Is there no storehouse of mercy to extend to the wayward soul who is reaping the cold reality of his folly-filled life that he has sown in his youth?

It was winter in the days when our Lord walked in the temple, and surely, the spiritual environment today is no less frigid. “Because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold” (Matthew 24:12). Those of us who choose to despise this barren wilderness can live reclusive at our will. The rest of us shall readily acknowledge that our God hast made . . . winter and allow it to have its perfecting work in our hearts.

En het was te Jeruzalem het feest der Inwijding; het was winter (Johannes 10:22).

Terwijl de razende winden om hem heen gieren, slaat de mens zijn kraag omhoog tegen de kou en de vochtigheid. We prijzen het seizoen dat hem in zijn zwakste toestand begroet en hem probeert te benadelen en te ontmoedigen bij de levenslust, zelden. De winter vestigt zich als een formidabele autoriteit en wekt angst niet zozeer door het veroorzaken van pijn, maar door het wegnemen van het aangename. Als we de equinox passeren, zegt het oude spreekwoord: “de dagen worden langer, en de winter wordt sterker”, en het blijft scherpzinning juist.

Winter is het seizoen van diepe, aanhoudende koude die de vorst dieper drijft en het ijs op de vijvers dikker maakt. Mens en beest worstelen met zijn felheid, en zelfs de levenloze mechaniek verzet zich tegen de adamantijnse komst van de winter. Kille tochtjes dringen door in elke kier en spleet en dringen hun harteloze aanwezigheid binnen in de meest besloten kamers. Terwijl de houtvoorraden krimpen, stijgen de energierekeningen in de strijd om weerstand te bieden aan winters leger van wapens. Hoewel een paar vrolijke deuntjes, zoals Winter Wonderland, trachten te profiteren van zijn majestueuze momenten, wordt de winter over het algemeen veracht door de normale bewoners van deze aarde. We grimmig onder de dreigende ijzige greep die ons gevangen houdt en verlangen naar de uiteindelijke ontbinding daarvan.

De lente kan haar aandeel aan drassige en ongemakkelijke dagen hebben en rafelige momenten. Noordelijke traditie zegt dat de roodborst drie keer met sneeuw bedekt moet worden voordat de lente volledig is aangekomen. Maar de lente is nooit leeg van de hoop en de luister van betere dagen die komen. De zomer kan ondraaglijk zijn met haar verzengende hitte en vochtigheid, maar ze draagt een schijn van gezegende vruchtbaarheid aan alle kanten, en weinigen zullen hun activiteiten vertragen om de ongemakken op te merken. De herfstdagen dragen hun nostalgische betovering terwijl de schoonheid van de natuur in de opmerkelijkste kleuren wordt geschilderd op het loof van het landschap. De overvloed van de oogst schept een sfeer van blijdschap in haar schoven, en het hart van de mens is nog vrolijk bij het vooruitzicht van rijpend leven. En dan komt . . .

Winter

Onze Heer ervoer de volheid daarvan; waarschijnlijk niet de volheid van de natuurlijke elementen die wij in noordelijke klimaten ondervinden, maar het seizoen van schijnbare vruchteloosheid. Sommigen zeiden: “Hij heeft een duivel, en hij is gek; waarom luistert u naar hem?” (Johannes 10:20). Ten tijde van het feest van de inwijding, “het was winter.” Er was een massale verdeeldheid onder het volk. Verwarring heerste aan alle kanten. Jezus had zojuist een blinde man genezen, en de Joden wierpen hem uit de tempel. Dergelijke vruchteloze en koude stenen harten bewoonden de velden die geroemd werden als “wit tot de oogst.” De ijzige grijpen van zonde hadden de harten van de mensheid verhard, en de weiden van religie lagen bezaaid met barre halmen, gedrapeerd met de resten van lege doppen. De geliefde discipel verspeet geen woorden toen hij ons het feit bracht dat . . . het was winter.

“Gij hebt alle grenzen der aarde gezet: Gij hebt zomer en winter gemaakt” (Psalm 74:17).

Het is gemakkelijk te geloven dat God de zomer geschapen heeft. De deuntjes op een perfecte zomerdag zingen ons van het Goddelijke. De schoonheid die overal om ons heen draait, spreekt van Zijn aanwezigheid. De blije vogels in elke boom, de warmte van het aangename zonlicht en het verbazingwekkende wonder van het leven trekken onze harten naar de Gever door duizend onzichtbare levensdraden. Dit alles getuigt van de waarheid dat “Gij hebt de zomer gemaakt”.

De dagen van de winter zijn anders. “Kan uit Nazareth enig goeds komen?” (Johannes 1:46). Wij delen soortgelijke gevoelens met die van Nathanaël ten opzichte van de wintermaanden, want het is niet zo gemakkelijk om Gods hand daar te zien. Er is veel lijden en afwijzing die we voelen binnendringen in onze innerlijke mens. Ik spreek duidelijk niet over het seizoen binnen de natuur, maar over de seizoenen van het leven die parallel lopen aan diens bestaan. We doen er goed aan ons schrale geloof te ondersteunen met enige stevige bevestiging dat God ook de winter heeft gemaakt, en dat wij Zijn goddelijke doeleinden daarin niet moeten betwijfelen. Wat anders dan een seizoen van verstikkende wanhoop en ongemak kan onze apathische zielen opwekken tot . . .

Waardering

Afwezigheid doet het hart groeien in genegenheid. Zo prikkelt de komst van de winter onze waardering voor de zomer. We zouden blind zijn als de zomer zich voortdurend voordeed. Men heeft terecht gezegd dat onze dierbaren pas van ons zijn wanneer we hen verloren hebben. Wanneer het winterseizoen tenslotte hun laatste adem opeist, beginnen we hen te waarderen voor wie ze werkelijk waren. Het is niet de man met een overvloed aan ononderbroken gezondheid die het meest diep voelt wat zijn welzijn waard is. Dat besef komt bij hem aan de deur op de dag dat zijn gezondheid verbrijzeld wordt. Er zijn vele rijke mannen geweest die eerder de schrale naaktheid van faillissement gekend hadden. Dit drukte onuitwisbaar een permanent stempel in hun karakter dat hen geschikt maakte voor het succes dat daarop volgde.

Zo zal de christen vaak een seizoen van winter ervaren—een tijd wanneer alles waarover hij gewerkt heeft, naar verlangd heeft en liefgehad heeft, ligt wegkwijnend onder hopen van steriele hopeloze puinlagen. Johannes de Doper profeteerde moedig terwijl de visioen nog vers was en de menigten zich aandrongen om hem te horen prediken. Maar de donkere en koude gevangeniscel was moeilijk voor hem om te waarderen. Toch heeft God de winter gemaakt, en deze seizoenen in ons leven zijn van het grootste belang voor ons geestelijk welzijn.

Versterking

In de 1700s maakte een vioolbouwer genaamd Stradivari violen die ongeëvenaard waren in hun schitterende klank. Terwijl moderne experts lang puzzelden over hun onvermogen om een soortgelijk instrument te maken, hebben de meesten geconcludeerd dat het hout van die tijd door moeilijke winters gekeerd was, wat een kwaliteit voortbracht die in onze tijd niet gerepliceerd kan worden. De hele natuur lijdt onder de druk van de wintermaanden, en de mens is geen uitzondering. De korte dagen en de diepe, brutale kilte van de nacht leggen een grote eis op onze wil. In de zomer is het betrekkelijk gemakkelijk om op het afgesproken uur uit bed te komen. De aarde is warm, de vogels zingen druk, en het licht stroomt door de open ramen. Maar in de duisternis van een ijskoude wintermorgen is het een uitdaging om de dekens terug te slaan en in een triomfantelijke houding op te staan. Het vereist een vaste vastberadenheid om te slagen en maakt vele goede voornemens tot een mislukking.

Breiden we die gedachte uit tot de ziel van de mens, dan bereiken we een onmiskenbare waarheid. Degenen die de diepe lasten van hard leven hebben gedragen, hebben een aangeboren kracht ingebed in hun karakter die zij van een milder milieu niet kunnen bevatten. Het morele karakter van Adonija was aangetast, want “zijn vader had hem te allen tijden niet ontevreden gemaakt door te zeggen: Waarom hebt gij alzoo gedaan?” (1 Koningen 1:6). Dit is het euvel van gemakkelijk leven. Degenen die zich aan alle kanten isoleren tegen de slagen van de winter zullen ongetwijfeld een verzwakking van de wil oplopen. Degenen die hun wil kunnen overwinnen in het aangezicht van een openlijk koude maatschappij, bevinden zich op de snelweg naar succes. De zomer is traag; maar de winter maakt ons vastberaden. We moeten dingen doen, ook wanneer we er geen zin in hebben. En aldus heeft God de winter gemaakt.

Samenkomst

“Indien twee samen liggen, hebben zij warmte; hoe kan één warm worden?” (Prediker 4:11). Voor dergelijke samenkomst is in de zomer geen noodzaak—en evenmin is er dan verlangen naar. De knapperende kachel heeft een betoverend effect op de gezinsleden en de meeste van onze winteravondactiviteiten draaien eromheen. We spreken met hetzelfde woord over haard en huis, en het is in de winter dat de haard gloedt en de liefde groeit.

Er zijn slechts oppervlakkige relaties onder hen die geen ontbering hebben gekend. Het vergt de zware ascese van de winter om het genie van liefde in ons hart te bewerken. Tegenspoed effent het speelveld, terwijl wijze en eenvoudig gezamenlijk in hetzelfde juk trekken. Vaak, wanneer de dood zijn kille vingers om een zwak lichaam slaat, haasten geliefden zich naar het ziekbed. Oude wrok wordt vergeten in de plechtigheid van het ogenblik. Het was aan de poorten van de winter dat “Abraham de geest gaf, en stierf, oud en voldaan des levens” (Genesis 25:8). Het is hier dat de scheidende gordijnen van het langdurige conflict tussen Isaak en Ismaël wegebden en een gezamenlijke inspanning tussen de twee broeders “hem begroeven in de grot van Machpela”.

Hoewel niemand van ons ooit hoopt op de politieke onrust die vervolging en het wegnemen van godsdienstvrijheid over ons land zou brengen, geloof ik nog steeds dat onze vleselijke kerkelijke verdeeldheden bij de komst daarvan zullen ophouden. Het kost de winter om ons samen te trekken, en Christus was het voertuig waarop het kwam. “Het was winter. En Jezus wandelde in de tempel in de voorhal van Salomo” (Johannes 10:23). Daar, voor de inwijding van Zijn dood, duwden Zijn discipelen allen om het vooraanstehende positie te bemachtigen en streefden ernaar de grootste te zijn. Nu, na de koude harde verwijdering van de groene boom, werden zij allen gevonden “eensgezind in de voorhal van Salomo” (Handelingen 5:12). Aldus is de bediening van de winter die onze God ons geschonken heeft.

Mededogen

Om de een of andere reden lijkt het dat wij een volle dosis mishandeling moeten ontvangen voordat de deur van ons hart ontsloten wordt voor gedachten aan de droevige toestand van anderen. Men kan zich slechts afvragen wat de Barmhartige Samaritaan moet hebben doorgemaakt om zo grondig bewogen te worden door het tafereel van de man in de sloot. Schilderden de Joden niet elke nieuwe dag een vers embleem van haat en minachting voor hem op het doek? Voor sommigen heeft de slechte behandeling de neiging het hart te verharden. Deze gaan door het leven in teruggetrokken wijze, met bitterheid en wrok aan het roer van hun schip. Alle kennissen die enigszins niet aan hun discriminatie beantwoorden, worden als verdacht geëtiketteerd en vermeden.

Er zijn anderen die de koude klap van de winter hebben doorstaan en ereen afkeer van hebben dat iemand hetzelfde zou moeten meemaken. Deze harten worden snel opgewekt tot medelijden en dragen bevooroordeelde sympathie jegens hen die eenzelfde lot delen. Zelfs de rijkdom die zijn winternachtelijke dood ontmoette en nu in de eeuwige hel verkeerde, werd bewogen om barmhartigheid uit te strekken aan zijn vijf broeders die naar hetzelfde vreselijke einde gingen. Hoeveel te meer zouden onze trage harten tot liefdadigheid moeten worden geroerd wanneer zij geconfronteerd worden met zulke ongemakken als geestelijke winter? Kunnen wij onze medemens begroeten met dezelfde strenge, ijzige blik die ons in vervlogen dagen in het gezicht heeft geslagen? Is er geen voorraadkamer van barmhartigheid om uit te strekken naar de dwalende ziel die de kille werkelijkheid oogst van zijn dwaasheidsvol leven dat hij in zijn jeugd gezaaid heeft?

Het was winter in de dagen dat onze Heer in de tempel wandelde, en zeker is de geestelijke omgeving vandaag niet minder ijskoud. “En omdat de ongerechtigheid overvloedig zal worden, zal de liefde van velen verkillen” (Mattheüs 24:12). Wie van ons ervoor kiest dit barre woestijnland te verachten, kan zich naar believen terugtrekken. De rest van ons zal klaarblijkelijk erkennen dat onze God . . . de winter heeft gemaakt en het zijn volmaakte werk in onze harten laten doen.

A Christ-centered Courtship is a series of messages on godly courtship preached by Paul Hershberger. He preached these messages several times at different locations over the last ten years. Recently, we had them transcribed and abridged for reading clarity. After printing all five articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant, we will publish them in a booklet. This is the fourth article of five.

There are five goals for this series:

  1. To turn the hearts of the fathers to their children.
  2. To turn the hearts of the children to their fathers.
  3. That parents would get a burden to lead their children into the perfect will of God for their lives.
  4. That young people would get a burden to seek God, find fulfillment and purpose in walking with God, and mature in their manners and character.
  5. That young men and women would rise up to be godly fathers and mothers with a vision to raise another godly generation.

We discussed Satan’s Snares for male and female in the last issue. Today’s topic is about waiting on God’s timing and plan for marriage.

The Preparation Sleep.

In Genesis 2:21, we read that Adam slept a deep sleep. God did surgery on him, and there was no anesthesiologist there to help with the surgery. Adam just slept a deep sleep.

We’re not talking about a dormant sleep, where we are unaware of our surroundings, but rather a germinating sleep. Germination has two components. The first component is dying and losing our identity. The second component is springing forth a new life. Preparation sleep is a sleep that is willing to die to self and lose its identity and its agenda. And yet, through this dying process, a new life can spring forth. Christians have the blessed opportunity to die to ourselves so that we can have fresh germination coming out of our lives. When we die to ourselves, new life springs forth.

“And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man” (Genesis 2:19–22).

In Genesis 2:20, Adam became aware that there was no helper suitable for him. As all the animals went by, he began to realize his need. Each animal had a male and a female, but he was the only one like him. God’s advice for Adam was, “You need to go to sleep.” And as Adam slept that deep sleep, he was wholly yielded. As Adam slept, God prepared for him a helpmeet. Adam did not interfere with this process. He wasn’t giving advice: “Make her this way or that way. ” This was all God’s doing, and Adam was yielded and in a deep sleep with no plan of his own. Today, this also applies to Eve. In Adam’s day, Eve wasn’t created yet. Today, Eve is alive the same as Adam is. In other words, today, we have males and females. If Eve doesn’t go into this preparation sleep as well, Adam will have difficulty going into a preparation sleep if Eve tries to get his attention. Eve needs to go to sleep in the same way as Adam does.

Young men and women, it is important that you yield your future and marriage to God. If you try to take your future into your own hands, you will likely fail. God has a purpose and plan for each one of you. It is possible that God’s plan for you is not marriage. But God does have a plan for you.

As we consider preparation sleep, let’s look at the life of Jesus when He was young. We want to look at four points from His life and make practical applications.

Jesus was a maturing, godly young man

“And when they had performed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth. This was right after they had been at the temple. And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him. Now, his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the Passover. And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast” (Luke 2:39–42).

In this scripture, Jesus is twelve years old. If you are twelve years old or older, I urge you to sit up and take note. Jesus was twelve, and here’s what it says about Him: “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon Him.” What an example of a maturing, godly young man. He “waxed strong in spirit.” That means the power of the Holy Ghost was strong upon Him. He was “filled with wisdom”—the wisdom of God! “And the grace of God”—the divine influence from God that helps one live a godly life, was upon Him, too.

Jesus began preparing for His life ministry at a young age. Sometimes, we think childhood is a time for playing. I’m not against children playing, but youth must consider what life is about long before adulthood. If you plan to wait until the time for marriage to get serious, you’ve missed a tremendous opportunity. Prepare yourself for marriage so you are ready to be married when that day comes. Then God’s face will shine upon you and bless you, and your life will be fulfilled and fruitful. There’s a preparation that goes on during this sleep.

Jesus sensed the call of God

“And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast. And when they had fulfilled the days, as they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother knew not of it. But they, supposing him to have been in the company, went a day’s journey; and they sought him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance. And when they found him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking him. And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business? And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them” (Luke 2:42-50).

At twelve years old, Jesus was already deeply interested in the Word of God. The calling of God was very clear to Him. When his parents came looking for him, he said, “Why did you look for me? Don’t you know that I need to be about My Father’s business?”

Young men and women, do you sense the calling of God? Is the Spirit of God speaking into your lives, moving, and giving direction? If we live a shallow Christian life, we won’t sense the moving of the Spirit of God. But if we get close to God, the Bible says He’ll draw nigh to us.

Do you understand the Bible, and can you give answers to what you believe? It is important to lay your own foundation. You can’t build on Mom and Dad’s foundation. If you grew up in a godly Christian home, you are blessed. But don’t be lazy; develop your own convictions. Find out for yourself what the Word of God says. Talk to Dad or Mom if you don’t understand something. Lay a foundation so you are ready to be married when the day comes.

Jesus was subject to his parents

“And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart” (Luke 2:51).

The example of Jesus is clear: “I must be about My Father’s business.” But He laid down His will and waited. He went home with his parents and “was subject to them.” He waited for eighteen years. Jesus continued actively pursuing His relationship with His Father in heaven in those eighteen years. He prepared for His ministry while He waited.

Sometimes, we wonder why we have to wait. We can’t see any purpose, and it feels like we’re being held back. But God works in our hearts while we wait and prepare for what’s ahead.

Jesus continued to increase and mature

“And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man” (Luke 2:52). Waiting and “preparation” sleeping didn’t hold Jesus back. As we consider His ministry and all the difficult things He faced, we know he prepared. How could He have such wisdom to have the correct answer to every question or give the right response? He prepared, and He walked with God.

Learning to walk with God

We, too, want to grow in wisdom, stature, and favor with God. To do so, we must learn to walk with God. We learn to walk with God by:

Bible reading

2 Timothy 2:15 says, “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” Constructive daily Bible reading is like constructing a building. It takes time. In the same way, we can’t become a Bible scholar in one year. We don’t read our Bibles just to survive for the day. If we’re reading to survive today, we are not laying bricks in our spiritual building. We need to lay some bricks. If we lay a few bricks every day, after some years, there will be quite a structure if we do it with a plan. Constructive daily Bible reading doesn’t need to be huge but should add up.

Prayer

“I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth” (1 Timothy 2:1–4).

Pray and intercede for other people. Thank God for what He has done for you. If God answered specific prayer requests, thank Him for it. Pray about specific needs in your life. “Lord, what are areas of need in my life? Take one or two of these areas, and seek God for grace to overcome them. If you do this for several years, God will abundantly bless your preparation.

Take time to praise and thank God. “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name” (Hebrews 13:15). Thankfulness coming out of our hearts and lives is important. God inhabits the praises of His people. When we are downcast, one of the best things we can do is sing. Rejoice in the Lord; bless His name.

Learn to hear the voice of God

Learn to discern God’s will and leading. Young people often struggle in this area. But as we learn to walk with God, we keep growing one step at a time. We read our Bibles, study, meditate, and memorize verses. We pray, fast, and seek the Lord. We praise Him and give Him thanks. We intercede for others and ask Him to help us. As we do these spiritual exercises, we begin to know the voice of God. He’ll begin to lead us in ways that we can understand. But we must take a step at a time and keep going. Don’t just aim at survival. Prepare for life.

Die to areas in your life

You need to die to your flesh so you can have that germination come forth into newness of life. Our flesh shrinks back from the idea of dying and says, “That’s not pleasant. I don’t enjoy that.” Our flesh doesn’t enjoy it, but dying to self brings forth new life. We can experience a springing forth in a new life as much as we are willing to die to ourselves.

Developing a Christlike character

Developing a Christlike character can be one of those areas in our lives where we struggle the hardest. But let’s not shrink away from it. We have the grace of God on our side, and he wants to give us inner strength so we can overcome areas of need in our lives.

Consider the fruits of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22–23. This is a good place to start developing a Christlike character. Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance. I still go back and look at that list, asking, “Ok, how am I doing?” If I claim to have the Spirit of God living in my heart, I should have these things coming out of my life. Let’s keep pressing on into the Kingdom.

When developing a Christlike character, let’s ask: What spirit comes from me? Do I have a loud spirit or a quiet spirit? A harsh spirit or a gentle spirit? A critical spirit or a forgiving spirit? A proud spirit or a humble spirit? A selfish spirit or a servant spirit? Unkind or kind? Crude or mannerly? Tough or compassionate? Rude or respectful? Do I need to work on my character?

Yield your life to God’s service

Art thou bound unto a wife? seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? seek not a wife. But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh: but I spare you. But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord. But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband” (1 Cor. 7:2–28, 32–34).

If you are unmarried, it may feel like “God has no purpose for me.” God has a purpose for everyone. In fact, if young people cannot be content and fulfilled in serving the Lord as a single person, they are not ready for married life either. Contentment is caring about the things of the Lord.

It goes with this preparation sleep. If your mind is focused on, “I’ve got to get married!” or “I wonder whom I’ll get married to,” you will be distracted and won’t be able to prepare for God’s plan for your life. These areas in your life need to go to sleep. In God’s timing, He’ll cause it to spring forth in newness of life.

Find fulfillment in serving the Lord, walking with Him, and being content. Find contentment in serving others by starting at home. Also, find contentment and fulfillment in the church.

What kind of partner do I need?

This may seem like a different topic, but this, too, is a part of preparation. Ask yourself: “What kind of partner do I need?” When considering a partner, you need:

  1. One with a vision.
  2. One that is virtuous.
  3. One that has a godly character.
  4. One that is under authority.
  5. One who is in love with Jesus.

This is fairly broad and yet all-encompassing. This is the kind of partner you want.

Parents, talk to your children. Don’t wait till there’s a request from a young man. Or perhaps your son says, “Well, Dad, uh, I really sort of feel drawn to this girl.” Fathers, don’t wait, but prepare for it. Talk about it with your children. And yes, you may ask them to wait. You may want to help them go to sleep. Give them direction on it. This conversation needs to happen when they are a bit older. Maybe around 20 or 21, this conversation could begin.

Parents, pray about this matter. Sometimes, we clearly sense God’s direction for our child in marriage. Other times, we may not be sure and need to ask God for direction. Pray for your children before they seek marriage. We’re not looking for them to just “fall in love” one day.

When am I ready for marriage?

Here are some questions to consider:

  1. Am I mature? Have I learned to walk with God? Am I steady and stable and established in the faith? Or do I have major ups and downs?
  2. Do I have a godly character? How do I treat others? How do I treat my parents and my siblings? How do I treat my coworkers? Am I quiet, gentle, forgiving, humble, a servant, kind, mannerly, compassionate, and respectful?
  3. Am I under authority? This one is important. Have you dealt with your strong nature? Are you willing to be compatible, like Ephesians 5:21 says about “submitting one to another”? Have you learned to honor and respect your father? Are you under authority?
  4. Is Jesus my all in all? Am I married to Christ? Do I find satisfaction in Him?
  5. Am I content with my lot in life? Am I willing to live with less than Mom and Dad have? You cannot start in the same place in life where your parents are today. Do I desire material things, always reaching for more?

Young men

Study Titus 2:6-8

  1. Young men, can you spiritually lead a wife and children? Can you do what Ephesians 5:24-27 says about washing them with the Word and guiding a home spiritually?
  2. Are you able to financially provide? Can you take care of the household? When you marry, it’s not just yourself but your wife and children to provide for.
  3. Are you an overcomer in moral purity? Are you walking in victory?
  4. Are you disciplined to say no to yourself? Are you willing to sacrifice for the good of others? Marriage brings sacrifice. Can you surrender to others?
  5. Are you willing to give up your independence? Are you ready for marriage? Marriage is about two people, not just yourself.

Young women

Study Titus 2:4–5.

  1. Do you have a meek and quiet spirit? A spirit that is restful and content?
  2. Are you able to become someone’s helpmeet? Can you be the rib at his side?
  3. Are you willing to take on his identity, goals, and visions? Are you willing to do that?
  4. Do you enjoy being a keeper at home? Have you learned homemaking skills?
  5. Do you love children? Are your young siblings a bother to you? Will you love your children?

In Summary

In Luke 2:51 Jesus “went down with them [His parents] and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them: but his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.” Even though we can’t see the future, God will bless us when we submit ourselves. At the age of 12, Jesus clearly sensed that call of God. “I must be about my Father’s business.” But He submitted Himself and went home.

Now, it is eighteen years later. “Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased. And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age . . . ” (Luke 3:21–23).

Jesus sensed that clear call from God at age 12. Yet He submitted Himself to His parents, who didn’t understand, and He prepared during the next 18 years. Now heaven opened, and God said, “Thou art My beloved Son, in whom I am well-pleased!” What more could we desire? Nothing else will matter if we get to heaven one day and hear those words.

Jesus prepared over eighteen years for His three years of ministry, but it was the most effective three years of ministry anybody ever has had and will ever have. He prepared!

God has a plan for each one of our lives. Can we yield to His leading and timing? Let’s germinate, dying to ourselves and springing forth into the newness of life. Let’s be in a germinating sleep. We may not understand it all, but let’s prepare, germinate, grow, and increase in the grace of God. My young brother and sister, just take one step at a time, and God will bless your life.

A Christ-centered Courtship adalah serangkaian khotbah tentang pacaran yang saleh yang disampaikan oleh Paul Hershberger. Dia telah menyampaikan khotbah-khotbah ini beberapa kali di berbagai tempat selama sepuluh tahun terakhir. Baru-baru ini, kami menyalinnya dan meringkaskannya untuk kejelasan bacaan. Setelah mencetak kelima artikel dalam The Heartbeat of the Remnant, kami akan menerbitkannya dalam sebuah buklet. Ini adalah artikel keempat dari lima.

Ada lima tujuan untuk seri ini:

  1. Memutar hati para ayah kepada anak-anak mereka.
  2. Memutar hati anak-anak kepada para ayah mereka.
  3. Agar orang tua memiliki beban untuk memimpin anak-anak mereka ke dalam kehendak sempurna Allah bagi hidup mereka.
  4. Agar kaum muda mendapat beban untuk mencari Allah, menemukan pemenuhan dan tujuan dalam berjalan dengan Allah, dan matang dalam tata cara dan karakter mereka.
  5. Agar pemuda dan pemudi bangkit menjadi ayah dan ibu yang saleh dengan visi untuk membesarkan generasi saleh berikutnya.

Kami membahas Jerat-Jerat Iblis bagi laki-laki dan perempuan dalam edisi terakhir. Topik hari ini adalah tentang menunggu waktu dan rencana Allah untuk pernikahan.

The Preparation Sleep.

Dalam Kejadian 2:21, kita membaca bahwa Adam tertidur dalam tidur nyenyak. Allah melakukan operasi padanya, dan tidak ada ahli anestesi yang hadir untuk membantu operasi itu. Adam hanya tertidur nyenyak.

Kita tidak sedang berbicara tentang tidur yang pasif, di mana kita tidak menyadari lingkungan kita, melainkan tidur yang bersifat bertunas. Bertunas memiliki dua komponen. Komponen pertama adalah mati dan kehilangan identitas kita. Komponen kedua adalah memancarkan kehidupan baru. Preparation sleep adalah tidur yang bersedia mati bagi diri sendiri dan kehilangan identitas serta agendanya. Namun, melalui proses kematian ini, kehidupan baru dapat memancarkan diri. Orang Kristen mempunyai kesempatan yang diberkati untuk mati bagi diri kita sendiri sehingga kita dapat mengalami tunas-tunas baru keluar dari hidup kita. Ketika kita mati bagi diri sendiri, kehidupan baru memancarkan diri.

“Dan dari tanah TUHAN Allah membentuk segala binatang di padang dan segala burung di udara, lalu dibawa-Nya kepada manusia untuk melihat bagaimana ia menamakan mereka; dan apapun yang dinamai manusia untuk tiap makhluk yang hidup, itulah namanya. Maka manusia memberi nama kepada segala ternak dan kepada burung-burung udara dan kepada segala binatang di padang; tetapi bagi manusia itu tidak ditemukan penolong yang sepadan baginya. Lalu TUHAN Allah menimpakan tidur yang nyenyak kepada manusia itu, maka ia tidur; diambil-Nyalah salah satu rusuknya lalu ditutup-Nya tempat itu dengan daging. Dan dari rusuk yang diambil TUHAN Allah dari manusia itu dibentuk-Nya seorang perempuan dan dibawa kepada manusia itu.” (Kejadian 2:19–22).

Dalam Kejadian 2:20, Adam menjadi sadar bahwa tidak ada penolong yang sepadan baginya. Saat semua binatang lewat, ia mulai menyadari kebutuhannya. Setiap binatang mempunyai jantan dan betina, tetapi dia adalah satu-satunya yang seperti dirinya. Nasihat Allah bagi Adam adalah, “Engkau perlu tidur.” Dan ketika Adam tertidur dalam tidur nyenyak itu, ia benar-benar menyerahkan diri. Saat Adam tidur, Allah mempersiapkan baginya seorang penolong. Adam tidak mengganggu proses ini. Dia tidak memberi nasihat: “Buat dia seperti ini atau seperti itu.” Semua ini adalah pekerjaan Allah, dan Adam tunduk dan dalam tidur nyenyak tanpa rencana sendiri. Hari ini, hal ini juga berlaku bagi Hawa. Pada zaman Adam, Hawa belum diciptakan. Hari ini, Hawa hidup sama seperti Adam. Dengan kata lain, hari ini kita memiliki laki-laki dan perempuan. Jika Hawa tidak masuk ke dalam preparation sleep seperti itu juga, Adam akan kesulitan memasuki preparation sleep jika Hawa mencoba menarik perhatiannya. Hawa perlu tidur dengan cara yang sama seperti Adam.

Anak-anak muda, penting bagi kalian untuk menyerahkan masa depan dan pernikahan kalian kepada Allah. Jika kalian mencoba mengambil masa depan ke tangan kalian sendiri, kemungkinan besar kalian akan gagal. Allah mempunyai tujuan dan rencana untuk masing-masing dari kalian. Mungkin rencana Allah untukmu bukanlah pernikahan. Tetapi Allah memang mempunyai rencana untukmu.

Saat kita mempertimbangkan preparation sleep, mari kita lihat kehidupan Yesus ketika Ia muda. Kita ingin melihat empat hal dari hidup-Nya dan membuat aplikasi praktis.

Yesus adalah seorang pemuda yang matang dan saleh

“Lalu mereka pulang ke Galilea, ke kota mereka Nazaret. Anak itu bertambah besar dan menjadi kuat, penuh hikmat, dan kasih karunia Allah ada pada-Nya. Orang tua-Nya biasa pergi ke Yerusalem setiap tahun pada hari raya Paskah. Ketika Ia berumur dua belas tahun, mereka pergi ke Yerusalem sesuai dengan kebiasaan hari raya itu.” (Lukas 2:39–42).

Dalam tulisan ini, Yesus berumur dua belas tahun. Jika kamu berumur dua belas tahun atau lebih, saya mendesakmu untuk duduk tegak dan mencatat. Yesus berumur dua belas, dan inilah yang dikatakan tentang-Nya: “Anak itu bertambah besar dan menjadi kuat, penuh hikmat, dan kasih karunia Allah ada pada-Nya.” Betapa teladan seorang pemuda yang matang dan saleh. Ia “menjadi kuat dalam roh.” Itu berarti kuasa Roh Kudus kuat atas-Nya. Ia “dipenuhi hikmat”—hikmat dari Allah! “Dan kasih karunia Allah”—pengaruh ilahi dari Allah yang menolong seseorang hidup saleh—juga ada pada-Nya.

Yesus mulai mempersiapkan pelayanan hidup-Nya sejak usia muda. Kadang-kadang, kita berpikir masa kanak-kanak adalah waktu untuk bermain. Saya bukan menentang anak bermain, tetapi kaum muda harus mempertimbangkan apa arti hidup jauh sebelum dewasa. Jika kalian merencanakan menunggu sampai waktunya pernikahan untuk menjadi serius, kalian telah melewatkan kesempatan luar biasa. Persiapkan dirimu untuk pernikahan agar kamu siap menikah ketika hari itu tiba. Maka wajah Allah akan bersinar kepadamu dan memberkati, dan hidupmu akan dipenuhi dan berbuah. Ada persiapan yang terjadi selama tidur ini.

Yesus merasakan panggilan Allah

“Ketika mereka selesai hari-hari itu mereka pulang, tetapi Anak Yesus tetap tinggal di Yerusalem tanpa diketahui oleh ibu dan bapa-Nya. Mereka menyangka Ia ada dalam rombongan mereka, lalu menempuh perjalanan sehari dan mulai mencari Dia di kalangan sanak saudara dan kenalan mereka. Tetapi mereka tidak menemukan-Nya, lalu kembali ke Yerusalem mencari Dia. Setelah tiga hari mereka menemukan Dia di rumah ibadat, duduk di tengah-tengah para ahli Taurat, mendengar mereka dan mengajukan pertanyaan kepada mereka. Semua orang yang mendengar Dia heran akan pengertian-Nya dan jawaban-jawaban-Nya. Ketika mereka melihat Dia mereka takjub, dan ibu-Nya berkata kepada-Nya: Anak, mengapa Engkau berbuat demikian kepada kami? Sesungguhnya bapa-Mu dan aku sangat mencari Engkau dengan sedih. Jawab-Nya kepada mereka: Mengapa kamu mencari Aku? Tidakkah kamu tahu, bahwa Aku harus berada di dalam perkara Bapa-Ku? Mereka tidak mengerti perkataan yang diucapkan-Nya kepada mereka.” (Lukas 2:42–50).

Pada umur dua belas tahun, Yesus sudah sangat tertarik pada Firman Allah. Panggilan Allah sangat jelas bagi-Nya. Ketika orang tua-Nya datang mencarikan-Nya, Ia berkata, “Mengapa kamu mencari Aku? Tidakkah kamu tahu, bahwa Aku harus berada di dalam perkara Bapa-Ku?”

Anak-anak muda, apakah kalian merasakan panggilan Allah? Apakah Roh Allah berbicara ke dalam hidupmu, bergerak, dan memberi arah? Jika kita hidup sebagai orang Kristen yang dangkal, kita tidak akan merasakan gerakan Roh Allah. Tetapi jika kita mendekat kepada Allah, Alkitab berkata Ia akan mendekat kepada kita.

Apakah kamu memahami Alkitab, dan dapatkah kamu memberikan jawaban tentang apa yang kamu percayai? Penting untuk meletakkan dasar sendiri. Kamu tidak dapat membangun di atas dasar Ayah dan Ibu saja. Jika kamu dibesarkan di rumah Kristen yang saleh, kamu diberkati. Tetapi jangan malas; kembangkan keyakinanmu sendiri. Ketahuilah sendiri apa yang dikatakan Firman Allah. Bicaralah kepada Ayah atau Ibu jika kamu tidak mengerti sesuatu. Letakkan dasar agar kamu siap menikah ketika hari itu tiba.

Yesus taat kepada orang tua-Nya

“Kemudian Ia turun bersama mereka dan pulang ke Nazaret dan taat kepada mereka; namun ibu-Nya menyimpan segala perkataan itu dalam hatinya.” (Lukas 2:51).

Teladan Yesus jelas: “Aku harus berada di dalam perkara Bapa-Ku.” Tetapi Ia menyerahkan kehendak-Nya dan menunggu. Ia pulang ke rumah bersama orang tua-Nya dan “taat kepada mereka.” Ia menunggu selama delapan belas tahun. Yesus terus aktif mengejar hubungan-Nya dengan Bapa-Nya di sorga selama delapan belas tahun itu. Ia mempersiapkan pelayanan-Nya sambil menunggu.

Kadang-kadang kita bertanya-tanya mengapa kita harus menunggu. Kita tidak melihat tujuan apa pun, dan rasanya kita ditahan. Tetapi Allah bekerja di dalam hati kita sementara kita menunggu dan mempersiapkan apa yang ada di depan.

Yesus terus bertambah dan matang

“Dan Yesus bertambah besar dalam hikmat dan tinggi badan dan kasih karunia di hadapan Allah dan manusia” (Lukas 2:52). Menunggu dan “preparation” sleeping tidak menahan Yesus. Ketika kita mempertimbangkan pelayanan-Nya dan semua hal sulit yang Ia hadapi, kita tahu Ia mempersiapkan diri. Bagaimana mungkin Ia memiliki hikmat sedemikian rupa untuk memberikan jawaban yang tepat untuk setiap pertanyaan atau respons yang benar? Ia mempersiapkan diri, dan Ia berjalan dengan Allah.

Belajar berjalan dengan Allah

Kita pun ingin bertumbuh dalam hikmat, tinggi badan, dan kasih karunia di hadapan Allah. Untuk melakukannya, kita harus belajar berjalan dengan Allah. Kita belajar berjalan dengan Allah melalui:

Membaca Alkitab

2 Timotius 2:15 berkata, “Berusahalah supaya engkau layak di hadapan Allah, sebagai seorang pekerja yang tidak perlu malu, yang dapat membagi-bagikan firman kebenaran dengan benar.” Membaca Alkitab setiap hari secara konstruktif itu seperti membangun sebuah bangunan. Itu memerlukan waktu. Demikian juga, kita tidak menjadi seorang sarjana Alkitab dalam satu tahun. Kita tidak membaca Alkitab hanya untuk bertahan hari ini. Jika kita membaca hanya untuk bertahan hari ini, kita tidak sedang meletakkan batu bata di bangunan rohani kita. Kita perlu meletakkan beberapa batu bata. Jika kita meletakkan beberapa batu bata setiap hari, setelah beberapa tahun akan ada suatu struktur jika kita melakukannya dengan rencana. Membaca Alkitab setiap hari secara konstruktif tidak perlu besar tetapi harus terakumulasi.

Doa

“Karena itu aku menasihatkan, supaya yang pertama-tama dilakukan adalah permohonan, doa, permintaan dan syafaat untuk segala orang, untuk raja-raja dan semua yang memegang kuasa, supaya kita dapat menjalani hidup yang tenang dan tenteram dalam segala kesalehan dan kehormatan. Karena ini baik dan berkenan kepada Juruselamat kita, Allah, yang menghendaki supaya semua orang diselamatkan dan sampai kepada pengenalan akan kebenaran.” (1 Timotius 2:1–4).

Berdoa dan bersyafaatlah untuk orang lain. Ucapkan syukur kepada Allah atas apa yang telah Ia lakukan bagimu. Jika Allah menjawab doa-doa tertentu, syukurilah itu. Berdoalah tentang kebutuhan-kebutuhan khusus dalam hidupmu. “Tuhan, apa bidang-bidang kebutuhan dalam hidupku? Ambillah satu atau dua bidang ini, dan carilah kepada Tuhan kasih karunia untuk mengatasinya.” Jika kamu melakukan ini selama beberapa tahun, Allah akan memberkati persiapanmu dengan berkelimpahan.

Luangkan waktu untuk memuji dan mengucap syukur kepada Allah. “Sebab itu marilah kita, oleh Dia, selalu mempersembahkan korban puji-pujian kepada Allah, yakni buah bibir yang mengakui nama-Nya.” (Ibrani 13:15). Rasa syukur yang keluar dari hati dan hidup kita itu penting. Allah diam dalam pujian umat-Nya. Ketika kita tertekan, salah satu hal terbaik yang bisa kita lakukan adalah bernyanyi. Bersukacitalah dalam Tuhan; pujilah nama-Nya.

Belajar mendengar suara Allah

Belajarlah membedakan kehendak dan pimpinan Allah. Anak-anak muda sering bergumul dalam bidang ini. Tetapi ketika kita belajar berjalan dengan Allah, kita terus bertumbuh selangkah demi selangkah. Kita membaca Alkitab, belajar, merenungkan, dan menghafal ayat-ayat. Kita berdoa, berpuasa, dan mencari Tuhan. Kita memuji-Nya dan mengucap syukur kepada-Nya. Kita bersyafaat untuk orang lain dan meminta Dia menolong kita. Ketika kita melakukan latihan-latihan rohani ini, kita mulai mengenal suara Allah. Ia akan mulai memimpin kita dengan cara-cara yang bisa kita pahami. Tetapi kita harus melangkah satu per satu dan terus maju. Jangan hanya bertujuan untuk bertahan hidup. Bersiaplah untuk hidup.

Mati terhadap bidang-bidang dalam hidupmu

Kamu perlu mati terhadap dagingmu agar tunas itu dapat memancarkan diri menjadi kehidupan yang baru. Daging kita mundur dari gagasan mati dan berkata, “Itu tidak menyenangkan. Aku tidak menikmati itu.” Daging kita memang tidak menikmatinya, tetapi mati bagi diri sendiri menghasilkan hidup baru. Kita dapat mengalami keluarnya kehidupan baru sejauh kita bersedia mati bagi diri sendiri.

Mengembangkan karakter yang serupa Kristus

Mengembangkan karakter yang serupa Kristus bisa menjadi salah satu bidang di hidup kita di mana kita paling bergumul. Tetapi jangan mundur dari itu. Kita punya kasih karunia Allah di pihak kita, dan Ia ingin memberi kita kekuatan batin sehingga kita dapat mengatasi bidang-bidang kebutuhan dalam hidup kita.

Pertimbangkan buah-buah Roh dalam Galatia 5:22–23. Ini adalah tempat yang baik untuk memulai mengembangkan karakter yang serupa Kristus. Kasih, sukacita, damai sejahtera, kesabaran, kelemahlembutan, kebaikan, iman, kerendahan hati, dan penguasaan diri. Saya masih kembali melihat daftar itu, bertanya, “Baiklah, bagaimana keadaan saya?” Jika saya mengaku mempunyai Roh Allah tinggal dalam hatiku, saya seharusnya memiliki hal-hal ini keluar dari hidupku. Mari terus maju ke dalam Kerajaan.

Saat mengembangkan karakter yang serupa Kristus, mari bertanya: Roh apa yang keluar dari diriku? Apakah aku memiliki roh yang keras atau roh yang tenang? Roh yang kasar atau lembut? Roh yang menghakimi atau yang mengampuni? Roh yang sombong atau yang rendah hati? Roh yang egois atau yang melayani? Tidak ramah atau ramah? Kasar atau berbudi? Keras atau berbelas kasihan? Kasar atau hormat? Apakah aku perlu bekerja pada karaktermu?

Menyerahkan hidupmu untuk pelayanan Allah

“Adakah engkau terikat kepada seorang perempuan? Jangan mencari kelepasan. Adakah engkau terlepas dari seorang perempuan? Jangan mencari isteri. Tetapi jika engkau kawin, engkau tidak berdosa; dan jika seorang perawan kawin, ia tidak berdosa. Namun demikian orang-orang yang kawin akan mengalami kesusahan dalam dagingnya, dan aku ingin menahan kamu dari itu. Tetapi aku ingin kamu tidak khawatir. Orang yang tidak kawin mengindahkan perkara-perkara yang ada pada Tuhan, bagaimana ia dapat menyenangkan Tuhan. Tetapi orang yang kawin mengindahkan perkara-perkara dunia, bagaimana ia dapat menyenangkan isterinya. Demikian pula terdapat perbezaan antara isteri dan perawan. Perempuan yang belum kawin mengindahkan perkara-perkara Tuhan supaya ia kudus baik di tubuh maupun di roh; tetapi perempuan yang kawin mengindahkan perkara-perkara dunia, bagaimana ia dapat menyenangkan suaminya.” (1 Korintus 7:2–28, 32–34).

Jika kamu belum menikah, mungkin terasa seperti “Allah tidak memiliki tujuan bagiku.” Allah mempunyai tujuan bagi setiap orang. Sebenarnya, jika kaum muda tidak dapat puas dan terisi dalam melayani Tuhan sebagai seorang yang lajang, mereka juga tidak siap untuk hidup berumah tangga. Kepuasan adalah memperhatikan perkara-perkara Tuhan.

Hal ini berhubungan dengan preparation sleep. Jika pikiranmu fokus pada, “Aku harus segera menikah!” atau “Aku bertanya-tanya kepada siapa aku akan menikah,” kamu akan terdistraksi dan tidak dapat mempersiapkan rencana Allah bagi hidupmu. Bidang-bidang dalam hidupmu perlu tidur. Dalam waktunya, Allah akan menyebabkan hal itu memancarkan diri dalam kehidupan yang baru.

Temukan kepuasan dalam melayani Tuhan, berjalan dengan-Nya, dan menjadi puas. Temukan kepuasan dalam melayani orang lain dengan memulai di rumah. Juga, temukan kepuasan dan pemenuhan di dalam gereja.

Pasangan seperti apa yang kubutuhkan?

Ini mungkin tampak topik yang berbeda, tetapi ini juga bagian dari persiapan. Tanyakan pada dirimu sendiri: “Pasangan seperti apa yang kubutuhkan?” Saat mempertimbangkan pasangan, kamu perlu:

  1. Seseorang yang punya visi.
  2. Seseorang yang berbudi pekerti.
  3. Seseorang yang memiliki karakter yang saleh.
  4. Seseorang yang berada di bawah otoritas.
  5. Seseorang yang jatuh cinta kepada Yesus.

Ini cukup luas namun mencakup segalanya. Inilah jenis pasangan yang kamu inginkan.

Orang tua, bicaralah dengan anak-anakmu. Jangan tunggu sampai ada permintaan dari seorang pemuda. Atau mungkin putramu berkata, “Nah, Ayah, eh, aku sungguh agak tertarik pada gadis ini.” Bapak-bapak, jangan menunggu, tetapi bersiaplah untuk itu. Bicarakanlah dengan anak-anakmu. Dan ya, kamu dapat meminta mereka untuk menunggu. Kamu mungkin ingin menolong mereka agar dapat tidur. Beri mereka arahan tentang hal itu. Percakapan ini perlu terjadi ketika mereka agak lebih tua. Mungkin sekitar usia 20 atau 21, percakapan ini bisa dimulai.

Orang tua, berdoalah tentang perkara ini. Kadang-kadang, kita jelas merasakan arahan Tuhan untuk anak kita dalam pernikahan. Kadang lain, kita mungkin tidak yakin dan perlu meminta arahan dari Allah. Berdoalah bagi anak-anakmu sebelum mereka mencari pernikahan. Kita tidak mencari supaya mereka hanya “jatuh cinta” pada suatu hari.

Kapan aku siap menikah?

Berikut beberapa pertanyaan untuk dipertimbangkan:

  1. Apakah aku dewasa? Apakah aku telah belajar berjalan dengan Allah? Apakah aku teguh, stabil, dan mapan dalam iman? Atau apakah aku mengalami pasang surut besar?
  2. Apakah aku mempunyai karakter yang saleh? Bagaimana aku memperlakukan orang lain? Bagaimana aku memperlakukan orang tua dan saudara-saudaraku? Bagaimana aku memperlakukan rekan kerjaku? Apakah aku tenang, lembut, pemaaf, rendah hati, seorang pelayan, baik, berbudi, berbelas kasih, dan penuh hormat?
  3. Apakah aku di bawah otoritas? Yang ini penting. Sudahkah kamu menangani sifat kerasmu? Apakah kamu bersedia kompatibel, seperti yang dikatakan Efesus 5:21 tentang “saling tunduk satu kepada lain”? Apakah kamu telah belajar untuk menghormati dan menghargai ayahmu? Apakah kamu berada di bawah otoritas?
  4. Apakah Yesus adalah segalanya bagiku? Apakah aku telah “menikah” dengan Kristus? Apakah aku menemukan kepuasan dalam Dia?
  5. Apakah aku puas dengan bagian hidupku? Apakah aku bersedia hidup dengan lebih sedikit daripada yang dimiliki Ayah dan Ibu hari ini? Kamu tidak dapat memulai di tempat yang sama dalam hidup di mana orang tuamu berada hari ini. Apakah aku mendambakan barang-barang materi, selalu menginginkan lebih?

Pemuda

Pelajari Titus 2:6-8

  1. Pemuda, dapatkah kamu secara rohani memimpin seorang istri dan anak-anak? Dapatkah kamu melakukan apa yang dikatakan Efesus 5:24–27 tentang memelihara mereka dengan Firman dan menuntun rumah secara rohani?
  2. Apakah kamu mampu menyediakan secara finansial? Dapatkah kamu menanggung kebutuhan rumah tangga? Saat menikah, bukan hanya dirimu sendiri tetapi juga istri dan anak-anak yang harus dipelihara.
  3. Apakah kamu pemenang dalam kesucian moral? Apakah kamu hidup dalam kemenangan?
  4. Apakah kamu disiplin untuk mengatakan tidak pada dirimu sendiri? Apakah kamu bersedia berkorban demi kebaikan orang lain? Pernikahan membawa pengorbanan. Dapatkah kamu menyerahkan diri untuk orang lain?
  5. Apakah kamu bersedia melepaskan kemandirianmu? Apakah kamu siap untuk pernikahan? Pernikahan tentang dua orang, bukan hanya dirimu sendiri.

Pemudi

Pelajari Titus 2:4–5.

  1. Apakah kamu mempunyai roh yang lemah lembut dan tenang? Roh yang tenteram dan puas?
  2. Apakah kamu mampu menjadi penolong bagi seseorang? Dapatkah kamu menjadi rusuk di sisinya?
  3. Apakah kamu bersedia mengambil identitas, tujuan, dan visi suamimu? Apakah kamu bersedia melakukan itu?
  4. Apakah kamu suka menjadi penanggung rumah tangga? Sudahkah kamu mempelajari keterampilan mengurus rumah tangga?
  5. Apakah kamu mencintai anak-anak? Apakah adik-adikmu mengganggumu? Akankah kamu mengasihi anak-anakmu?

Ringkasan

Dalam Lukas 2:51 Yesus “turun bersama mereka [orang tua-Nya] dan pulang ke Nazaret, dan taat kepada mereka: tetapi ibu-Nya menyimpan segala perkataan itu dalam hatinya.” Meskipun kita tidak dapat melihat masa depan, Allah akan memberkati kita ketika kita menyerahkan diri. Pada usia 12, Yesus jelas merasakan panggilan Allah. “Aku harus berada dalam perkara Bapa-Ku.” Tetapi Ia menundukkan diri dan pulang ke rumah.

Sekarang, delapan belas tahun kemudian. “Ketika semua orang dibaptis, terjadilah bahwa Yesus juga dibaptis; dan ketika Ia berdoa, terbukalah langit, dan Roh Kudus turun ke atas-Nya dengan wujud seperti burung merpati, dan datanglah suara dari sorga: Engkaulah Anak-Ku yang Kukasihi; Engkau lah yang berkenan kepada-Ku. Yesus sendiri mula-mula berumur kira-kira tiga puluh tahun . . .” (Lukas 3:21–23).

Yesus merasakan panggilan yang jelas dari Allah pada usia 12. Namun Ia menundukkan diri kepada orang tua-Nya, yang tidak mengerti, dan Ia mempersiapkan diri selama 18 tahun berikutnya. Kini langit terbuka, dan Allah berkata, “Engkaulah Anak-Ku yang Kukasihi, kepada-Mulah Aku berkenan!” Apa lagi yang bisa kita inginkan? Tidak ada yang lain yang akan berarti jika suatu hari kita sampai di sorga dan mendengar perkataan itu.

Yesus mempersiapkan diri selama delapan belas tahun untuk tiga tahun pelayanan-Nya, tetapi itu adalah tiga tahun pelayanan paling efektif yang pernah ada dan yang akan pernah ada. Ia mempersiapkan diri!

Allah mempunyai rencana bagi setiap hidup kita. Dapatkah kita tunduk pada pimpinan dan waktunya? Mari kita bertunas, mati bagi diri sendiri dan memancarkan diri kepada kehidupan yang baru. Marilah kita berada dalam tidur yang bertunas. Kita mungkin tidak memahami semuanya, tetapi marilah kita mempersiapkan diri, bertunas, bertumbuh, dan bertambah dalam kasih karunia Allah. Saudara dan saudari muda, ambillah satu langkah pada suatu waktu, dan Allah akan memberkati hidupmu.

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.
