Hace unos años, me hallaba hundida en un agotamiento físico y emocional, intentando adaptarme a la vida fuera de la aldea africana que habíamos llamado hogar durante ocho años. La depresión y el miedo eran parte habitual de mi vida. A medida que lentamente salía del hoyo en el que me encontraba —un hoyo en el que nunca me di cuenta de que había caído hasta que ya era demasiado tarde para un remedio fácil—, empecé a notar la belleza.

En esos años intensos de ministerio y aprendizaje del idioma en la aldea, dedicar tiempo a la belleza parecía una pérdida de tiempo. Y, sinceramente, vivíamos en una aldea con muy poca belleza que ofrecer; lo único brillante eran las ropas de colores vibrantes que las mujeres llevaban. Las casas de barro, el paisaje plano y el polvo por todas partes eran la vida diaria durante la mayor parte del año. Aunque soy amante de la paz, del silencio y de las cosas hermosas, hice muy poco espacio en mi vida para cualquiera de ello, incluso para las cosas que podría haber hecho en ese entorno.

Ahora vivimos en un lugar más fácil: las Tierras Altas del Sur de Tanzania. Aquí hay aire fresco y sol durante todo el año. Flores... de todo tipo, y una casa encantadora con suelos lisos y paredes recién pintadas. Y es ahora cuando me doy cuenta de lo importante que es la belleza para el alma y lo importante que es notar realmente las cosas bellas en mi vida y crear belleza en cada momento posible.

Ser madre y ama de casa, no importa en qué parte del mundo nos haya colocado Dios, es en sí mismo algo hermoso si realmente lo vemos por lo que es. Es fácil quejarse de las cosas cotidianas y mundanas que conforman mi vida, del polvo constante o del hecho de que estoy encerrada en nuestro recinto semana tras semana. Pero me he sorprendido con gozo. Aquí hay algunas cosas que me gusta hacer para mantener la vida fresca e inspiradora:

Escribir

Me gusta especialmente escribir sobre la bondad y la fidelidad de Dios. La verdadera alegría viene de Él, no de mis circunstancias. He creído eso durante años, pero es solo recientemente que realmente he experimentado esa realidad. Mi atención se afina tan fácilmente en las cosas que desearía que fueran diferentes, pensando que sin la incertidumbre y las dificultades sería feliz. Ahora me doy cuenta de que las dificultades tienen muy poco que ver con la cantidad de gozo que hay en mi corazón. En cambio, podemos permitir que las dificultades nos enseñen qué es la verdadera alegría y de dónde proviene.

Mantener la casa razonablemente limpia y agradable

Intento deshacerme de los extras y reemplazar lo sucio, lo deslucido y lo feo por algo que sea bello y agradable. Deshazte de la cortina mustia y fea en el aula y cámbiala por una amarilla y fresca (sí, incluso si cuesta unos pocos dólares, le recuerdo a mi alma ahorrativa).

Despejar todas las superficies horizontales

Uno de mis objetivos es limpiar todas las superficies planas de mi casa y dejar solo cosas agradables y de buen gusto. Funcionó mucho mejor si mi casa es un lugar reposado y ordenado. Aunque con cinco hijos, reposado y ordenado son términos relativos, estoy aprendiendo que la prisa, el desorden y el ruido de una familia también son hermosos. Eso hace que el suelo limpio sea aún más asombroso y motivo de agradecimiento porque es una experiencia rara.

Hacer algo divertido con mis hijos

Me gusta planear algo divertido para hacer con mis hijos, como un proyecto de ciencias entretenido o una salida. Nuestro favorito son las visitas a los jardines de flores, que se cultivan aquí en la ciudad a lo largo de la carretera como vitrina para dar ideas a otras personas sobre cómo cultivar y cuidar flores. Escondidas en rincones aquí y allá, encuentro todas las flores comunes a las que estaba acostumbrada en Estados Unidos. Es encantador y aún más divertido cuando algunos de los niños comparten mi amor por cultivar cosas.

Servir la comida con gusto

Incluso el arroz y los frijoles pueden servirse en cuencos bonitos en lugar de en las ollas desordenadas en las que se cocinaron. Visita tu mercado local y te sorprenderá lo que puedes encontrar en cristalería y otros platos hermosos que alegran tu mesa.

Hablar con alegría

Habla con alegría—con la encargada de la lavandería, con la ayudante de la casa o con la vecina. No puedo pasar mucho tiempo en el ministerio con personas que no sean mis hijos, pero siempre hay gente que viene por aquí a la que puedo tocar con una sonrisa, con amabilidad o con cualquier ayuda que necesiten. Es fácil enfadarse por el hecho de que la vendedora de verduras no recuerde NO venir por la mañana mientras doy clases, y que su voz en la puerta nos interrumpa otra vez. ¿Y qué tienen que ver los hechos matemáticos, la masa del pan y los suelos sucios con la alegría? ¿Cómo se mezcla el ruido de la vida y las personalidades cascarrabias con lo eterno? Todo está mezclado en mi corazón, a menudo con las realidades polvorientas encima y amenazando con derramarse, pero si cedo a actitudes irritables, eso sí es un verdadero matador de alegría.

Pasar tiempo apreciando la belleza de la naturaleza

Esto reposa mi mente y atrae mi corazón hacia Dios. Aunque nunca he vivido en el Jardín del Edén ni en lugares de igual belleza, siempre hay algo que notar, algo tan pequeño como un parche de hierba verde que lucha por sobrevivir la temporada seca (que es una temporada de prueba para mí aquí en este país). Hace frío (45 grados o menos por la mañana). El crecimiento verde y las lluvias refrescantes han terminado. Todo lo verde está muriendo o hace tiempo que está muerto. Incluso los techos de las casas han perdido su color mientras el polvo cubre cada superficie posible y amenaza con sofocar la inspiración de los humanos también. Incluso la montaña que se ve desde mi ventana de la cocina ha perdido su hermoso mosaico de jardines y campos. Se muestra desnuda y sobria, esperando con la respiración contenida la lluvia—como mi corazón. Pero me he deleitado en un pequeño parche de tierra en nuestro patio trasero que mantengo regado. Hay espatifilos, rosas, hibiscos y otras flores brillantes floreciendo, y suculentas creciendo en encantadores tiestos pequeños. Llevo cubos pesados de agua hasta ese lugar y a veces llevo a los cinco a todos en los autobuses de la ciudad para visitar otro jardín de flores en busca de más flores. Para mí no es una pérdida de tiempo, ya que ese pequeño rincón en mi patio trasero durante esta temporada seca refresca mi corazón una y otra vez.

Practicar la gratitud

Con un esposo muy ocupado, no tengo mucho tiempo con él, y él no tiene mucho tiempo despreocupado con los niños. Sin embargo, me estoy acostumbrando a notar las cosas pequeñas que sí ocurren, como verlo sentado en un tapete con las niñas, simplemente disfrutándolas, cuando miro por la ventana de la cocina. Me quedo de pie y observo, dando gracias a Dios por ese momento. Podría haber pasado desapercibido, especialmente si mi corazón estuviera lleno de ingratitud y mal humor. Notar los pequeños destellos de gozo a lo largo del día hace que mi vida parezca llena de alegría, aunque en realidad mi vida tenga muchas pruebas y desafíos.

La vida aquí en la ciudad es más fácil en muchas maneras, pero hemos sido bombardeados con numerosos desafíos al trabajar con el gobierno, lo cual ha consumido el tiempo y la energía de Tim. Aunque no habíamos vivido en la aldea por más de cuatro años, estábamos haciendo mucho trabajo de apoyo para nuestros compañeros misioneros allí y realizando viajes de regreso a donde todavía sentíamos que era nuestro hogar. Pero a todos nosotros nos han prohibido volver a esa aldea y hemos tenido que trabajar arduamente incluso para obtener los documentos necesarios para simplemente permanecer en el país.

Recientemente, nuestro recinto en la aldea fue tomado por el ejército local, apenas semanas después de que dos familias misioneras tanzanas se mudaran allí. Cuando Tim viajó de regreso para comunicarse y entregar las llaves por respeto a los que nos obligaban a hacer esto, fue insultado con horas de ira irracional y maltrato, junto con muchas demandas. Por supuesto, nuestros corazones se rompieron al ver nuestra casa usada para el entrenamiento del ejército en lugar de para esas preciosas familias misioneras nuevas que dejaban sus hogares en la ciudad para asumir el trabajo allí.

Mi esposo está exhausto, tanto física como emocionalmente, y aun así esta mañana partió de nuevo hacia la aldea para “echar leña sobre el fuego” entregando al oficial del ejército airado un panel solar y un transformador además de las otras cosas que exigía. Es nuestro servicio razonable. Y sí, mi corazón tenía lágrimas mientras lo veía partir desde la ventana. Sé que solo se está exponiendo a más maltrato, y eso me duele. Pero también sé que es solo a través de estas cosas que Dios me enseña la alegría. Al rendir las cosas queridas para mí, me vacío de mis propios deseos. Ya no hay a qué aferrarse ni por qué luchar. Así, queda mucho espacio para que Dios llene mi corazón con lo que Él quiere poner allí—gozo.

Sí, la vida no me ha traído mucha serendipia. Ha habido muchas lágrimas, pero eso ya no es mi enfoque, ya que deliberadamente traigo belleza a cada rendija posible de mi vida y me deleito en la sorpresa del gozo. Mi empeño es permitir que mi hogar y este pequeño espacio en la tierra sean un lugar donde venga el reino de Dios. No puede tratarse únicamente de cosas felices, paz y serendipia, porque eso no me ha sido dado. Tiene que tratarse de algo realmente bueno que ocurra en mi corazón y de cómo eso afecta todo lo que mis manos tocan. Mi corazón puede declarar las obras del Señor al ver cómo Él usa las pruebas en mi vida para edificar mi fe y la fe de otros que observan. De esa manera su reino viene a este pequeño lugar, a esta pequeña rendija de vida, a este espacio vacío de inspiración, salvo por Su asombrosa gracia, que convierte la prueba en gozo.

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.

É inverno agora; a neve caída
deixou os céus friamente límpidos;
por ramos sem folhas, sopra o vento agudo,
e toda a terra jaz morta e sombria.

E ainda o amor de Deus não se retira;
sua vida no ar cortante respira;
sua beleza pinta a aurora carmim,
e veste cada ramo com guirlandas brilhantes.

E embora lá fora soprem ventos agudos,
e os céus sejam frios, e as geadas sejam intensas,
o lar fecha agora mais seu círculo,
e seu lume interior brilha mais quente.

Ó Deus, tu dás o frio do inverno,
assim como os alegres raios do verão,
tu nos envolves calorosamente em teu amor,
e nos conservas através dos dias invernais da vida.

The people we commonly refer to as the Russian Mennonites came into being as a group in a way quite similar to that of us with an Anabaptist heritage. We sprang from the same areas of Europe, from much of the same teachings of early Anabaptism, and have both experienced many of the same temptations and pitfalls, though at different times and locations.

This article will not focus on the beginnings of the Russian Mennonites apart from a brief overview. The group first entered Russia upon the urgings of the Viceroy Potemkin, who came into authority over the area now known as Ukraine after its annexation by Russia in 1783. The area had been under his partial administration since 1774, and he was eager to populate the land with foreign settlers. The residents of New Russia, as it was then called, were mostly nomads and Cossacks, a seminomadic group present in the steppes of Russia. The Mennonites in Danzig, Poland, were first approached with the offer of land, which would have appealed to them because they were routinely denied land ownership as a semi-persecuted people at that time. This offer came in August of 1786, and two brothers from the Danzig church were sent to survey the land and make arrangements for possible immigration.

The first immigration of 462 families began in 1788, and the “Old Colony” was established at Chortitza. They were afforded freedom of religion, exemption from military service, and the right to maintain their own schools and governances.

The Mennonites thrived in their new homeland. Although the first years were hard, partially due to the fact that mostly poorer families and those not in church leadership chose to resettle in Russia, the group soon began to transform the barren plains and steppes into rich agricultural communities. As the churches grew, so did their prosperity.

This period of relative peace lasted for over a century, until the late 1800s, when the Russian government, dissatisfied with the number of foreign settlements inside its borders, began applying pressure to many of the groups it had invited to settle its land some 100 years before. The Mennonites were not the only ones targeted, as many groups from various nations had established themselves in Russia. Steps taken against the Mennonites included pressure to participate in the armed forces as well as pressure to drop the German language that the communities had been using in favor of the Russian language. As these pressures increased, some Mennonites chose to flee the country in the 1870s. The majority, however, by now quite wealthy and affluent in comparison to their Russian peasant neighbors, chose to stay and weather the storm.

Unbeknownst to them, a full-scale revolution that would reshape Russia as a country was just around the corner. In 1917, the Bolsheviks came to power through the October Revolution, an event where the reigning tsar, or emperor, was deposed and exiled, and a new government was set up. A civil war broke out, and much of the fighting raged over the lands occupied by the Mennonites. Here, it is necessary to insert a brief history of the ideology of this new government.

The October Revolution and its subsequent change in government were fueled by a class war. As opposed to Nazi Germany, where a person could be arrested and killed for their race, in Russia, a person could and would be arrested for their class, for example, property ownership was seen as a crime against the people, and so the wealthier class of Russian peasants and farmers, those who most often owned property and employed the lower class of peasants, became an instant target a revolution that claimed to want to distribute all property and resources evenly amongst its citizenry.

By this time, the strong agricultural society of the Mennonites had transformed Ukraine into a breadbasket, its vast fields sown with wheat developed specifically by the Mennonites: Turkey Red Wheat. This hardy crop had made the Mennonite church quite wealthy, and their colonies had grown and flourished into villages of comfort and, at times, extravagance. This must have been a two-fold insult to the still impoverished peasants of Russia. Not only was there a large group of people in their midst that taught, spoke, and did their dealings in a language not of the Motherland, but these people also were wealthy beyond most peasants’ dreams.

It is, therefore, no surprise that when the kulaks, the wealthy class of peasants, came under persecution from the new government, the Mennonites were seen as the enemy of the people. As the civil war raged over Mennonite lands, villages were burnt and decimated, people executed or driven off, and livestock and grain plundered. Eventually, this period of fighting did come to an end, but for those few who survived the destruction, there was no reprieve to be found.

With the label of kulak and being generally defenseless, the Mennonites faced intense persecution. Religious services were rarely allowed, and the agricultural communities that had fed Russia and many others besides were collectivized and put under government control. Many of their churches ceased to exist entirely, although those in the east tended to last longer than the western villages.

Imagine then, to a people accustomed for generations to the favor and benevolence of material possessions and success, that all things material are stripped away. In a historical eye blink, the wealthy become the poor, and the favored become the hated. Even with a strong Christian faith, such a turn of events would shock and confuse.

But further tests were yet ahead for those who endured the first 25 years of the Soviet persecution. With the memory of their easy lives still fresh, the dawn of World War II brought a unique and enticing opportunity: the rise of a government that promoted the well-being of the German race, that valued those groups that could turn an empty prairie into a sprawling farm, that was vehemently anti-Communist- to this beleaguered group of believers, this must have seemed to be a God sent miracle to deliver them from their burdensome exile.

And so, they embraced the invading Germans. We readers, who are blessed with the ability to see the end result of these people’s decisions, can certainly make a good guess at what the end result was of wholesale support for the Nazis, but we must remember the scenarios that these Mennonites found themselves in...it was not one that would have been easy to decipher and decide upon if it were to be judged by man’s knowledge.

And so it was that the descendants of those helpless believers who gave their bodies at the stake and sword aligned themselves with a worldly kingdom that promised to protect and provide for them. In exchange for an eternal heritage, they chose to hope that the might of the German army would win back their earthly heritage and riches, and it was in this might that they trusted, forming bands of men who fought alongside the Germans against their old neighbors.

History did not deviate from its course, and the German army was eventually beaten back to its own borders and then further, and yet further into German lands. Before this retreating army ran those that had looked to it for their deliverance.

The atrocities of the Soviet government against its citizens are well documented in various works, most famously in the Gulag Archipelago, a book written by a Russian officer who was accused of treason. That author, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn, painted a terrible picture of the treatment and exile of those who had opposed the USSR. Amongst the imprisoned or executed millions described in his tomes, there lie the remnants of a people who began as we did, experienced the smile of prosperity as we do, and then, treasuring that prosperity, lost it in calamitous fashion. We would do well to consider the paths we choose, as the wise king of the Scriptures instructs us, lest we, too, fall in the pursuit of prosperity. “Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established” (Proverbs 4:26).

Folkene vi vanligvis omtaler som de russiske mennonittene, oppstod som en gruppe på en måte ganske lik den vi med anabaptistisk arv gjorde. Vi sprang ut fra de samme områdene i Europa, fra mye av de samme læresetningene i tidlig anabaptisme, og har begge opplevd mange av de samme fristelsene og fallgruvene, om enn til ulike tider og på ulike steder.

Denne artikkelen vil ikke fokusere inngående på begynnelsen av de russiske mennonittene utover en kort oversikt. Gruppen kom først inn i Russland etter påtrykk fra visekonge Potemkin, som fikk myndighet over området som i dag kalles Ukraina etter anneksjonen av Russland i 1783. Området hadde vært under hans delvise administrasjon siden 1774, og han var ivrig etter å befolke landet med utenlandske bosettere. Innbyggerne i Novorossija, som det den gang ble kalt, var for det meste nomader og kosakker, en semi-nomadisk gruppe som holdt til i steppene i Russland. Mennonittene i Danzig i Polen ble først kontaktet med tilbud om land, noe som ville appellere til dem fordi de på den tiden rutinemessig ble nektet eiendomsrett som et delvis forfulgt folk. Dette tilbudet kom i august 1786, og to brødre fra Danzig-kirken ble sendt for å rekognosere landet og gjøre ordninger for mulig immigrasjon.

Den første immigrasjonen på 462 familier begynte i 1788, og den «gamle kolonien» ble etablert ved Chortitza. De fikk religionsfrihet, fritak fra militærtjeneste og retten til å opprettholde egne skoler og styresett.

Mennonittene blomstret i sitt nye hjemland. Selv om de første årene var harde, delvis fordi det først og fremst var fattigere familier og de som ikke var i kirkelig lederskap som valgte å slå seg ned i Russland, begynte gruppen snart å forvandle de golde sletter og stepper til rike jordbruksområder. Etter hvert som kirkene vokste, vokste også deres velstand.

Denne perioden med relativ fred varte i over et århundre, helt til slutten av 1800-tallet, da den russiske regjeringen, misfornøyd med antallet utenlandske bosetninger innen sine grenser, begynte å legge press på mange av de gruppene den hadde invitert til å bosette seg der omkring 100 år tidligere. Mennonittene var ikke de eneste som ble mål for dette; mange grupper fra ulike nasjoner hadde etablert seg i Russland. Tiltakene mot mennonittene omfattet press for å delta i de væpnede styrkene samt press for å forkaste det tyske språket som samfunnene hadde brukt til fordel for russisk. Etter hvert som disse påtrykkene økte, valgte noen mennonitter å flykte landet på 1870-tallet. Majoriteten, derimot, som nå var ganske velstående og velstående sammenlignet med sine russiske bonde-naboer, valgte å bli og ri stormen av.

Uvitende for dem, var en fullskala revolusjon som ville omforme Russland som land like rundt hjørnet. I 1917 kom bolsjevikene til makten gjennom oktoberrevolusjonen, en hendelse hvor den regjerende tsaren, eller keiseren, ble avsatt og sendt i eksil, og en ny regjering ble opprettet. En borgerkrig brøt ut, og mye av kampene raste over landene som mennonittene hadde bosatt. Her er det nødvendig å sette inn en kort historie av ideologien til denne nye regjeringen.

Oktoberrevolusjonen og den påfølgende regjeringsforandringen ble drevet av en klassekamp. I motsetning til Nazi-Tyskland, hvor en person kunne bli arrestert og drept på grunn av sin rase, i Russland kunne og ville en person bli arrestert for sin klasse; for eksempel ble eiendomsbesittelse sett på som en forbrytelse mot folket, og dermed ble den rikere bondeklassen—de som oftest eide eiendom og ansatte den lavere bondeklassen—et øyeblikkelig mål i en revolusjon som påsto å ville fordele all eiendom og alle ressurser jevnt blant sine borgere.

På dette tidspunktet hadde det sterke jordbrukssamfunnet blant mennonittene forvandlet Ukraina til et kornmagasin, med vidstrakte åkre sådd med hvete utviklet spesielt av mennonittene: Turkey Red-hvete. Denne hardføre avlingen hadde gjort mennonittkirken ganske rik, og deres kolonier hadde vokst og blomstret til landsbyer av velstand og til tider overdådighet. Dette må ha vært et dobbeltslag mot de fortsatt fattige bøndene i Russland. Ikke bare var det en stor gruppe mennesker blant dem som lærte, talte og gjorde sine saker på et språk som ikke var fedrelandets, men disse menneskene var også rikere enn de fleste bønders villeste drømmer.

Det er derfor ikke overraskende at da kulakkene, den velstående bondeklassen, kom under forfølgelse fra den nye regjeringen, ble mennonittene sett på som folkets fiende. Mens borgerkrigen raste over mennonittiske områder, ble landsbyer brent og ødelagt, folk henrettet eller jaget bort, og husdyr og korn plyndret. Til slutt tok denne perioden med kamper slutt, men for de få som overlevde ødeleggelsen, var det ingen hvile å finne.

Med merkelappen kulakk og generelt uten mulighet til å forsvare seg, sto mennonittene overfor intens forfølgelse. Religionsgudstjenester ble sjelden tillatt, og de jordbrukssamfunnene som hadde født Russland og mange andre ble kollektivisert og satt under statlig kontroll. Mange av deres kirker opphørte helt å eksistere, selv om de i øst pleide å vare lenger enn de vestlige landsbyene.

Tenk deg da, for et folk vant gjennom generasjoner til gunst og velvilje fra materiell eiendom og suksess, at alle materielle goder blir revet bort. I et historisk øyeblikks blunk blir de velstående fattige, og de favoriserte blir hatet. Selv med en sterk kristen tro ville en slik vending i hendelser sjokkere og forvirre.

Men ytterligere prøvelser lå foran dem som holdt ut de første 25 årene av sovjetforfølgelsen. Med minnene om det lette livet fortsatt friske, ga dagen for andre verdenskrig en unik og lokkende mulighet: fremveksten av en regjering som fremmet det tyske folkets velvære, som verdsatte de gruppene som kunne forvandle en tom prærie til en omfattende gård, som var innbitt anti-kommunistisk—for denne tærete gruppen troende måtte dette ha virket som et gudsendt mirakel for å befri dem fra deres tyngende eksil.

Og så omfavnet de de invaderende tyskerne. Vi lesere, som er velsignet med evnen til å se slutten av disse menneskenes valg, kan sikkert gjette godt hva sluttresultatet ble av helhjertet støtte til nazistene, men vi må huske de scenariene disse mennonittene befant seg i... det var ikke et som ville være lett å tyde og ta stilling til hvis det skulle bedømmes etter menneskelig kunnskap.

Og slik var det at etterkommerne av de hjelpeløse troende som gav sine kropper ved stake og sverd, allierte seg med et verdslig rike som lovet å beskytte og forsørge dem. I bytte for et evig arv håpet de at den tyske hærs makt ville vinne tilbake deres jordiske arv og rikdom, og det var i denne makt de stolte, og dannet bander av menn som kjempet side om side med tyskerne mot sine gamle naboer.

Historien avvek ikke fra sitt løp, og den tyske hæren ble etter hvert presset tilbake til sine egne grenser og så videre inn i tysk territorium. Foran denne tilbaketrekkende hæren flyktet de som hadde sett til den for sin befrielse.

Sovjetregjeringens grusomheter mot sine borgere er godt dokumentert i ulike verk, mest berømt i Gulagarkipelet, en bok skrevet av en russisk offiser som ble anklaget for landsforræderi. Den forfatteren, Aleksandr Solzjenitsyn, malte et forferdelig bilde av behandlingen og eksilet av dem som hadde motsatt seg USSR. Blant de fangede eller henrettede millioner som er beskrevet i hans verk, ligger restene av et folk som begynte som vi gjorde, opplevde velstandens smil som vi gjør, og deretter, idet de verdsatte den velstanden, mistet den på en katastrofal måte. Vi ville gjøre klokt i å vurdere de veiene vi velger, som den vise konge i Skriftene instruerer oss, for at ikke også vi faller i jakten på velstand. «Betrakt dine fots vei, og la alle dine stier bli faste» (Ordspørkene 4:26).

“So, what brings you in today?” I asked Ben, a 40-year-old man who was sitting across from me.

“Well,” he answered. “I have a few different symptoms. The biggest one is that I am always tired, but I’ve also been gaining weight, and my knees hurt some in the mornings.”

I mentally began to go through what doctors call a differential diagnosis – things that can cause the cluster of symptoms that a patient has. I usually let the patient explain what symptoms he is experiencing and then ask questions to try to hone in on the specific diagnosis.

Ben went on for a little while longer. Then, he proceeded to pull out a piece of paper. “So, Doctor,” he told me. “I’ve done some research into my diagnosis, and I think these are tests that I need to have done to work things up.”

I looked at the list. It was pretty long and included some things I probably would have ordered anyway, like a blood count and thyroid level, but also some very odd things like a Vitamin B1 level and a DHEA level. He also wanted a CT Scan of his head, chest, and abdomen.

“This is a lot of testing,” I said. “I’m not sure we need to do all of it. Can we talk a little bit more about your symptoms and then try to hone in on what testing would be best to sort it out?”

Ben was not impressed. “I have done my research!” He told me firmly. “These days, with the internet, you can find out things that your doctor wouldn’t tell you about – maybe things he doesn’t even know to test for. The problem is that I need YOU to order these things for me so my insurance will cover them. Otherwise, I wouldn’t even be here.”

With that, we’ll leave Ben and his uncomfortable doctor behind. There have always been patients who brought in articles from magazines telling the reader, “Six things your doctor won’t tell you about your health” and listing testing that should be done. It does seem to have gotten worse.

A lot of patients know more than their doctors. They can search for their symptoms on the web and find out all sorts of things that could cause those symptoms.

Beyond that, artificial intelligence is smart. Chat GPT, an artificial intelligence platform, was able to pass the three parts of the US Medical Licensure Exam.1 It didn’t do terribly well— it only got just above a passing grade, but I suppose that’s good enough that it could open an office across the street from mine and start seeing patients.

In some ways letting patients have access to this level of information is a good thing. Doctors aren’t some sort of high priests who are given special rights to access the Holiest of Holies of medical information. More than that, doctors are anything but perfect, and you have only to read online reviews to see that they don’t listen well, botch procedures, and struggle with difficult diagnoses.

It can be challenging, though, when patients believe that they know more than their doctor. I have always said that if you know more than your doctor, either you need a healthy dose of humility or a new doctor— or maybe both.

Get Wisdom!

Proverbs 4:5-9 says, “Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee. Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding. Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her. She shall give to thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver to thee.”

Proverbs 18:15 speaks of getting knowledge, but it indicates that before we seek knowledge, we should make certain that we have wisdom and understanding.

The author of the book of Proverbs was Solomon. We know that early in his reign he had a dream in which God appeared to him and offered him whatever he desired. In his humility, Solomon asked for an understanding heart, so that he would be able to wisely lead such a great people (I Kings 3:9,10).

When we look at knowledge, it is simply a group of facts— blocks of information that need to be assembled into some sort of coherent pattern. Wisdom and understanding are the tools with which we make sense of the knowledge that we have acquired.

Wisdom lets us judge the accuracy of the sources of “knowledge” as well. It helps us to ask the question, “Is this person trying to sell me something? Do they actually have any scientific studies that indicate that what they say is true?”

These are two questions that I ask when I look at a website. Are there links to products that are being sold to me, and is the advertising clearly separated from the articles? More than that, are there links to studies that support what is being claimed? If there are, how big were those studies? If a study has only 12 people in it, it is not large enough to give accurate information.

Robert Harris made an acronym CARS, that helps sort out whether information on a website is valid. Credibility, past Accuracy, Reasonableness, and Supporting information are all important to look at to see if we should value the information on a website.2

Unfortunately, many people who claim to have the answers to living long and healthy lives are actually trying to sell books, supplements, and a variety of other products. One prominent doctor who promotes better health through the use of supplements (that he sells) has managed to accrue enough money through the process that he stated in a 2017 affidavit that he was worth in excess of 100 million dollars. This doesn’t mean that he has nothing to offer, but it does say that he has some bias towards recommending things he is selling.

The American Medical Association has guidelines for doctors to sell products out of their offices ethically. Those guidelines say that the products should serve a particular urgent need (say, crutches at an Orthopedic office), have scientific validity for their use, and that doctors should offer information about other ways that patients can get the same products elsewhere.3 More than that, doctors should reveal to their patients any financial interest that they have in the product that is being offered to the patient.

Confirmation Bias

Most of us read in order to confirm the things we already believe. I see this when people read the Bible— somehow, people can read the Bible and completely ignore Scriptures that contradict their behaviors in terms of political involvement or modesty of dress but believe that they are following all things of the Scripture.

In the same way, each one of us can find stories and information that reinforce our beliefs about doctors and medicine. If we believe that doctors are simply after money and are unethical and prescribe medicines that are toxic to patients, we can find articles that confirm that. On the other hand, if we look for stories that tear down alternative medicine theories, we can find those articles too.

The important thing is that we approach the question looking for real answers and understanding that science doesn’t know everything.

As an example, we do not have good treatments for people who have Long COVID symptoms. That doesn’t mean that many people who suffered through COVID months later aren’t suffering from things like mental fog and fatigue, but it does mean that there is not a single medication that has done better than sugar pills in studies to get rid of those symptoms.

In the absence of scientifically proven treatment plans, many clinics have developed their own treatment courses, using a mixture of supplements and even hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Are these helpful? I don’t know, but I do know that those marketing them will confidently claim that they have an extremely high success rate in curing people if they are simply willing to follow (and pay for) the treatment plan.

More than that, when people are researching their symptoms, they tend to choose what diagnoses they think are likely based on their underlying personality types. Some people are prone to catastrophize— that is, they immediately believe the worst possible outcome of any given scenario they are presented with. These people will type in their symptoms and will come to the conclusion that they have cancer with only days or weeks to live. As God told Hezekiah, it is time for them to set their house in order.

On the other hand, there are plenty of people who have optimistic personalities. They type in their symptom list and come to the conclusion that they have a mild viral illness and will feel better in a few days.

The whole point of having a medical provider review things is that the practitioner can (hopefully) sort out the likely things from the unlikely ones. They don’t deal with the emotional overlay that patients do, so they can objectively decide how many tests to order and what type of tests to order in order to come up with a diagnosis.

Doctors Can Identify Dangerous Situations

I remember seeing a patient years ago who came in to see me with what she thought was a sinus infection. She was in her 20s and said that she had a pounding sensation in her head and a lot of pressure.

She didn’t really have any drainage or fever and none of the typical symptoms of a sinus infection, but sinusitis seemed like the most likely diagnosis that she could come up with.

I took one look at her and didn’t like what I saw. For one thing, she was extremely pale. For another, her pulse rate was quite fast – 130 beats a minute at rest. When I examined her, I found nothing that indicated that she had a sinus infection.

“Jenny,” I told her. “I need you to go to the hospital and get a stat blood count. I’m afraid you are really anemic— although I don’t know why. Wait at the lab and I will talk to you once I get the results back.”

It was perhaps 20 minutes later that I got an urgent call from the hospital laboratory. “Dr. Waldron,” the voice on the other end said. “We have a critical lab result for you…”

Jenny’s hemoglobin was 4.6 (normal is between 12 and 16), and she ended up getting a transfusion. What she didn’t get was treatment for a sinus infection.

Chest pain is a classic symptom that can point to an underlying heart condition. At the same time, it could simply indicate esophageal reflux (acid in the esophagus) or inflammation in a rib or muscle. I probably see a couple of patients every day who have this symptom.

The majority of them need a simple treatment, but a few of them need to be sent urgently to the hospital for a complete heart evaluation. I don’t know how an online search engine will know which direction to indicate for a person to seek after reviewing their symptoms.

At best, an online resource will refer a user to seek emergency services or their local doctor.

Not All Doctors Are Equal

Roughly 50 percent of doctors finished in the bottom half of their Medical School class. Just because someone didn’t have top marks in Medical School doesn’t mean that they don’t have adequate knowledge to treat an ailment. Perhaps the most important knowledge that a doctor needs is to know when he doesn’t know.

It is still challenging for patients to know whether they are dealing with someone who will help them. When you meet a doctor, you tend to judge them based on their “bedside manner.” Most of us look for someone who exudes confidence and seems to know what they are doing.

Confidence does not equal competence, and there are many doctors (and people in other fields) who have high levels of confidence in themselves but are not really competent to take care of the situation at hand.

Here is where doing some research can help. First, your doctor has online reviews, and those reviews will indicate something about the level of care they provide for patients. Second, if what your healthcare provider tells you seems really odd, it is easy to do a little research on the condition that you are supposedly dealing with and see if the symptoms line up and if the treatment seems reasonable.

It is important to realize that humans are not like vehicles. What I mean by that is that there is no scan tool that healthcare providers can hook up and generate all of the error codes and then fix the things that generate those codes.

Even if healthcare providers are certain of the diagnosis, some patients do not respond to the first or even the second treatment that is available. That doesn’t mean that the diagnosis or the treatment was wrong, but that people are not clones of each other and some respond better to one type of treatment than another.

Maybe someday we will have some type of genetic testing that tells us right off what the perfect medication or treatment plan is for a given illness, but that day seems a long way off.

A final thing to mention is that good doctors will not feel threatened by their patients asking questions or doing research. There are times when a patient will ask me about a new treatment that I am not familiar with, and I need to do my own research.

Those scenarios are not upsetting for me but rather a learning opportunity. “I’m not familiar with that,” I will tell my patient. “Let me do a little research and talk to some specialists that I trust, and I will call you later this week and let you know what I find out.”

Sometimes I investigate and find that the treatment is expensive and seems to provide mixed or little benefit, but sometimes it is an improvement over the past ways of doing things. Doctors need to learn and adjust their style of practicing medicine as we learn new things about diseases and how the human body responds to them.

Humility is Needed

The longer I practice medicine, the less I feel that I know. It isn’t that I have developed dementia, but rather that I realize that there are numerous diseases that we don’t have good treatments for. The human body is amazingly complex. There are 36 trillion cells in the human body, and normally, they all work together perfectly; the problem is figuring out what to do when they don’t.

The Dunning-Kruger Effect is something that affects many fields in which people with limited knowledge and skill significantly overestimate their abilities in that field. Studies have shown that 65 percent of Americans believe that they have above-average IQs.4 Statistically, this isn’t possible. Fifty percent of any group of people will have above-average IQs, and the other 50 percent will be below-average. That’s how the IQ scale is set up.

While this effect is present for doctors, it is also present for patients. “Doing your research” is not the same thing as spending four years in Medical School, another three years in a residency training program, and continuing to stay abreast of developments in medicine through a variety of educational courses. We all would do well to listen better and realize our limitations.

The fact that your mother’s cousin took milkweed extract and felt much better from similar symptoms to yours is interesting. Whether the milkweed extract helped them get over their illness, whether there was a placebo effect, or they were just going to get better anyway, regardless of what they took, is up for debate.

True Wisdom

I have mentioned wisdom already, and I would finish with that. True wisdom is realizing that healing comes from God. Psalms 103:3 says of God, “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases.”

Healing doesn’t come from antibiotics or chemotherapy. It doesn’t come from taking the right supplements or even eating a healthy diet. Healing comes because God touches us, right down to the tiniest parts of our cells and immune system, and makes things whole again.

I do believe that sometimes He works through medicine, but other times He works through the effective, fervent prayer of righteous men and women. (James 5:16)

With all of our knowledge, it is easy for us to get puffed up with pride and believe that we need no one else. We live in a world that is teeming with knowledge and a world in which wisdom has taken a back seat.

We must choose the source of our information carefully and realize that we don’t know everything. Maybe the reason why the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom is because it is the first step to us laying aside our pride and realizing that we are a tiny part of Creation. Only then, can we humbly listen and learn and receive healing.

«Ainsi, qu'est-ce qui vous amène aujourd'hui ?» demandai-je à Ben, un homme de 40 ans qui était assis en face de moi.

«Eh bien, répondit-il. J'ai quelques symptômes différents. Le principal est que je suis toujours fatigué, mais j'ai aussi pris du poids, et mes genoux me font un peu mal le matin.»

J'ai mentalement commencé à passer en revue ce que les médecins appellent un diagnostic différentiel : les éléments qui peuvent provoquer l'ensemble des symptômes présentés par un patient. J'aime généralement laisser le patient expliquer quels symptômes il ressent, puis poser des questions pour essayer de préciser le diagnostic spécifique.

Ben a continué encore un moment. Puis, il a sorti un morceau de papier. «Alors, docteur, m'a-t-il dit. J'ai fait des recherches sur mon diagnostic, et je pense que ce sont les tests qu'il faut me faire pour explorer la situation.»

J'ai regardé la liste. Elle était assez longue et comprenait des éléments que j'aurais probablement prescrits de toute façon, comme une numération formule sanguine et un bilan thyroïdien, mais aussi des choses très inhabituelles comme un taux de vitamine B1 et un taux de DHEA. Il voulait aussi un scanner de la tête, du thorax et de l'abdomen.

«C'est beaucoup d'examens, dis-je. Je ne suis pas sûr que nous ayons besoin de tout cela. Pouvons-nous parler un peu plus de vos symptômes puis essayer de cibler quels examens seraient les mieux adaptés pour y voir plus clair ?»

Ben n'était pas impressionné. «J'ai fait mes recherches !» me dit-il fermement. «De nos jours, avec Internet, on peut découvrir des choses que votre médecin ne vous dirait pas — peut‑être des choses qu'il ne sait même pas tester. Le problème, c'est que j'ai besoin que VOUS demandiez ces examens pour que mon assurance les couvre. Sinon, je ne serais même pas venu.»

Laissez‑nous donc Ben et son médecin mal à l'aise. Il y a toujours eu des patients qui apportaient des articles de magazines disant au lecteur «Six choses que votre médecin ne vous dira pas à propos de votre santé» et énumérant des examens à réaliser. Il semble que cela se soit aggravé.

Beaucoup de patients en savent plus que leurs médecins. Ils peuvent chercher leurs symptômes sur le web et trouver toutes sortes de choses qui pourraient en être la cause.

Au‑delà de cela, l'intelligence artificielle est intelligente. ChatGPT, une plateforme d'intelligence artificielle, a été capable de réussir les trois parties de l'examen de licence médicale des États‑Unis.1 Il n'a pas très bien réussi — il a seulement obtenu une note juste au‑dessus du seuil de réussite, mais je suppose que c'est suffisant pour qu'il ouvre un cabinet en face du mien et commence à recevoir des patients.

D'une certaine manière, donner aux patients l'accès à ce niveau d'information est une bonne chose. Les médecins ne sont pas une sorte de grands prêtres ayant des droits spéciaux d'accès au Très Saint des informations médicales. De plus, les médecins sont loin d'être parfaits, et il suffit de lire des avis en ligne pour voir qu'ils n'écoutent pas bien, gâchent des procédures et peinent avec des diagnostics difficiles.

Cela peut être problématique toutefois lorsque les patients croient qu'ils en savent plus que leur médecin. J'ai toujours dit que si vous en savez plus que votre médecin, soit il vous faut une bonne dose d'humilité, soit un nouveau médecin — ou peut‑être les deux.

Obtenez la sagesse !

Proverbes 4:5-9 dit : «Acquiers la sagesse, acquiers l'intelligence ; n'oublie rien et ne t'écarte pas des paroles de ma bouche. Ne l'abandonne pas, et elle te gardera ; aime‑la, et elle te protégera. La sagesse est la chose principale ; acquiers la sagesse, et avec tout ce que tu acquiers, acquiers l'intelligence. Exalte‑la, et elle t'élèvera ; elle t'apportera l'honneur lorsque tu l'embrasseras. Elle donnera à ta tête un ornement de grâce ; une couronne de gloire elle te remettra.»

Proverbes 18:15 parle de l'acquisition de connaissances, mais il indique qu'avant de rechercher la connaissance, nous devons nous assurer d'avoir la sagesse et l'intelligence.

L'auteur du livre des Proverbes est Salomon. Nous savons qu'au début de son règne il eut un rêve où Dieu lui apparut et lui offrit ce qu'il désirait. Dans son humilité, Salomon demanda un cœur intelligent, afin de pouvoir diriger sagement un si grand peuple (I Rois 3:9,10).

Quand nous regardons la connaissance, ce n'est simplement qu'un ensemble de faits — des blocs d'information qui doivent être assemblés selon un certain schéma cohérent. La sagesse et l'intelligence sont les outils avec lesquels nous donnons du sens à la connaissance que nous avons acquise.

La sagesse nous permet aussi de juger de l'exactitude des sources de la «connaissance». Elle nous aide à poser la question : «Cette personne essaie‑t‑elle de me vendre quelque chose ? A‑t‑elle vraiment des études scientifiques qui indiquent que ce qu'elle affirme est vrai ?»

Ce sont deux questions que je me pose quand j'examine un site web. Y a‑t‑il des liens vers des produits qui me sont vendus, et la publicité est‑elle clairement séparée des articles ? De plus, y a‑t‑il des liens vers des études qui soutiennent ce qui est affirmé ? Si oui, quelle était la taille de ces études ? Si une étude ne comporte que 12 personnes, elle n'est pas assez importante pour fournir une information fiable.

Robert Harris a créé l'acronyme CARS, qui aide à déterminer si l'information d'un site web est valable. Crédibilité, précision passée, raisonnabilité et informations de soutien sont autant d'éléments importants à examiner pour voir si nous devons accorder de la valeur à l'information d'un site.2

Malheureusement, beaucoup de personnes qui prétendent avoir les réponses pour vivre longtemps et en bonne santé essaient en réalité de vendre des livres, des compléments et divers autres produits. Un médecin en vue qui promeut une meilleure santé par l'usage de compléments (qu'il vend) a réussi à accumuler assez d'argent pour déclarer dans une déclaration sous serment en 2017 qu'il valait plus de 100 millions de dollars. Cela ne veut pas dire qu'il n'a rien d'utile à offrir, mais cela indique qu'il a un parti pris en faveur des choses qu'il recommande parce qu'il les vend.

L'Association médicale américaine a des directives pour que les médecins vendent des produits depuis leur cabinet de manière éthique. Ces directives précisent que les produits doivent répondre à un besoin particulier urgent (par exemple, des béquilles dans un cabinet d'orthopédie), avoir une validité scientifique pour leur usage, et que les médecins doivent informer les patients de façons alternatives d'obtenir les mêmes produits ailleurs.3 De plus, les médecins doivent révéler à leurs patients tout intérêt financier qu'ils ont dans le produit proposé au patient.

Biais de confirmation

La plupart d'entre nous lisent pour confirmer ce qu'ils croient déjà. Je le vois quand les gens lisent la Bible — d'une manière ou d'une autre, des personnes peuvent lire les Écritures et complètement ignorer des versets qui contredisent leurs comportements en matière d'engagement politique ou de modestie vestimentaire tout en croyant qu'elles suivent l'ensemble des enseignements de la Bible.

De la même façon, chacun de nous peut trouver des histoires et des informations qui renforcent nos croyances à propos des médecins et de la médecine. Si nous croyons que les médecins ne recherchent que l'argent, sont peu éthiques et prescrivent des médicaments toxiques, nous pouvons trouver des articles qui le confirment. D'un autre côté, si nous cherchons des récits qui démolissent les théories de la médecine alternative, nous pouvons aussi trouver ces articles.

L'important est d'aborder la question en cherchant de véritables réponses et en comprenant que la science ne sait pas tout.

Par exemple, nous n'avons pas de bons traitements pour les personnes qui présentent des symptômes de COVID long. Cela ne signifie pas que beaucoup de personnes ayant souffert de la COVID ne souffrent pas, des mois plus tard, de brouillard mental et de fatigue, mais cela signifie qu'il n'existe pas un médicament unique qui ait fait mieux que des placebo dans des études pour éliminer ces symptômes.

En l'absence de plans thérapeutiques scientifiquement prouvés, de nombreuses cliniques ont développé leurs propres protocoles, utilisant un mélange de compléments et même des traitements par oxygénothérapie hyperbare. Sont‑ils utiles ? Je ne sais pas, mais je sais que ceux qui les commercialisent affirmeront avec assurance qu'ils ont un taux de succès extrêmement élevé pour guérir les gens si ces derniers acceptent simplement de suivre (et de payer pour) le protocole.

De plus, lorsque les gens recherchent leurs symptômes, ils ont tendance à choisir les diagnostics qu'ils jugent probables en fonction de leurs types de personnalité sous‑jacents. Certaines personnes sont enclines à la catastrophisation — c'est‑à‑dire qu'elles croient immédiatement au pire résultat possible de n'importe quel scénario qui leur est présenté. Ces personnes taperont leurs symptômes et en viendront à la conclusion qu'elles ont un cancer et n'ont que quelques jours ou semaines à vivre. Comme Dieu l'a dit à Ézéchias, il est temps pour elles de mettre leur maison en ordre.

D'un autre côté, il y a beaucoup de gens au tempérament optimiste. Ils saisissent leur liste de symptômes et concluent qu'il s'agit d'une petite infection virale et qu'ils se sentiront mieux en quelques jours.

Le but d'avoir un professionnel de santé qui examine les choses est que le praticien puisse (espérons‑le) trier les éléments probables des éléments improbables. Ils ne sont pas soumis à la surcharge émotionnelle des patients, donc ils peuvent décider objectivement du nombre d'examens à prescrire et du type d'examens à demander pour aboutir à un diagnostic.

Les médecins peuvent identifier des situations dangereuses

Je me souviens d'avoir vu, il y a des années, une patiente qui était venue me voir pour ce qu'elle pensait être une sinusite. Elle était dans la vingtaine et disait ressentir des battements violents dans la tête et beaucoup de pression.

Elle n'avait pas vraiment d'écoulement ni de fièvre et aucun des symptômes typiques d'une sinusite, mais la sinusite semblait être le diagnostic le plus probable qu'elle pouvait imaginer.

Je l'ai regardée et je n'ai pas aimé ce que j'ai vu. D'une part, elle était extrêmement pâle. D'autre part, son rythme cardiaque était très rapide — 130 battements par minute au repos. Quand je l'ai examinée, je n'ai rien trouvé qui indique une sinusite.

«Jenny, lui ai‑je dit. Il faut que vous alliez à l'hôpital faire une numération formule sanguine en urgence. J'ai peur que vous soyez vraiment anémique — même si je ne sais pas pourquoi. Attendez au laboratoire et je vous parlerai dès que j'aurai les résultats.»

C'est peut‑être vingt minutes plus tard que j'ai reçu un appel urgent du laboratoire de l'hôpital. «Docteur Waldron, dit la voix à l'autre bout. Nous avons un résultat de laboratoire critique pour vous…»

L'hémoglobine de Jenny était à 4,6 (la normale est entre 12 et 16), et elle a fini par recevoir une transfusion. Ce qu'elle n'a pas reçu, c'est un traitement pour une sinusite.

La douleur thoracique est un symptôme classique qui peut indiquer une affection cardiaque sous‑jacente. En même temps, elle peut simplement indiquer un reflux œsophagien (de l'acide dans l'œsophage) ou une inflammation d'une côte ou d'un muscle. Je vois probablement quelques patients chaque jour qui présentent ce symptôme.

La majorité d'entre eux nécessitent un traitement simple, mais quelques‑uns doivent être envoyés en urgence à l'hôpital pour une évaluation cardiaque complète. Je ne sais pas comment un moteur de recherche en ligne saura dans quelle direction orienter une personne après avoir examiné ses symptômes.

Au mieux, une ressource en ligne dirigera l'utilisateur vers les services d'urgence ou vers son médecin local.

Tous les médecins ne se valent pas

Environ 50 % des médecins ont terminé dans la moitié inférieure de leur promotion en faculté de médecine. Le fait que quelqu'un n'ait pas eu les meilleures notes en faculté ne signifie pas qu'il n'a pas les connaissances adéquates pour traiter une affection. Peut‑être que la connaissance la plus importante qu'un médecin doit avoir est de savoir quand il ne sait pas.

Il reste difficile pour les patients de savoir s'ils ont affaire à quelqu'un qui les aidera. Quand vous rencontrez un médecin, vous avez tendance à le juger d'après son «manière d'être au chevet». La plupart d'entre nous cherchent quelqu'un qui dégage de la confiance et qui semble savoir ce qu'il fait.

La confiance n'est pas synonyme de compétence, et il y a beaucoup de médecins (et de personnes dans d'autres domaines) qui ont un grand niveau de confiance en eux mais ne sont pas vraiment compétents pour gérer la situation.

Voici où faire un peu de recherche peut aider. Premièrement, votre médecin a des avis en ligne, et ces avis indiqueront quelque chose sur le niveau de soin qu'il apporte aux patients. Deuxièmement, si ce que votre professionnel de santé vous dit semble vraiment étrange, il est facile de faire une petite recherche sur l'affection dont il est question et de voir si les symptômes correspondent et si le traitement semble raisonnable.

Il est important de réaliser que les humains ne sont pas comme des véhicules. Ce que je veux dire, c'est qu'il n'existe pas d'outil de diagnostic que les prestataires de soins pourraient brancher pour générer tous les codes d'erreur et réparer ensuite ce qui les provoque.

Même si les prestataires de soins sont certains du diagnostic, certains patients ne répondent pas au premier traitement ni même au deuxième. Cela ne signifie pas que le diagnostic ou le traitement était erroné, mais que les gens ne sont pas des clones les uns des autres et que certains répondent mieux à un type de traitement qu'à un autre.

Peut‑être qu'un jour nous aurons des tests génétiques permettant de dire d'emblée quel est le médicament ou le plan thérapeutique parfait pour une maladie donnée, mais ce jour semble encore lointain.

Une dernière chose à mentionner est que les bons médecins ne se sentiront pas menacés par des patients qui posent des questions ou font des recherches. Il y a des fois qu'un patient me demande au sujet d'un nouveau traitement que je ne connais pas, et je dois faire mes propres recherches.

Ces scénarios ne me dérangent pas ; au contraire, ce sont des occasions d'apprentissage. «Je ne connais pas cela,» dis‑je à mon patient. «Laissez‑moi faire quelques recherches et parler à des spécialistes en qui j'ai confiance, et je vous appellerai plus tard cette semaine pour vous dire ce que j'ai trouvé.»

Parfois j'enquête et je découvre que le traitement est coûteux et semble apporter des bénéfices mitigés ou faibles, mais parfois c'est une amélioration par rapport aux méthodes précédentes. Les médecins doivent apprendre et adapter leur manière de pratiquer la médecine à mesure que nous découvrons de nouvelles choses sur les maladies et la façon dont le corps humain y répond.

L'humilité est nécessaire

Plus je pratique la médecine, moins je me sens savoir. Ce n'est pas que j'ai développé une démence, mais plutôt que je réalise qu'il existe de nombreuses maladies pour lesquelles nous n'avons pas de bons traitements. Le corps humain est incroyablement complexe. Il y a 36 000 milliards de cellules dans le corps humain, et normalement elles travaillent toutes ensemble parfaitement ; le problème est de savoir quoi faire quand elles ne le font pas.

L'effet Dunning‑Kruger est quelque chose qui affecte de nombreux domaines où des personnes aux connaissances et compétences limitées surestiment significativement leurs capacités dans ce domaine. Des études ont montré que 65 % des Américains croient avoir un QI supérieur à la moyenne.4 Statistiquement, cela n'est pas possible. Cinquante pour cent de n'importe quel groupe de personnes aura un QI supérieur à la moyenne, et les 50 % restants seront en dessous de la moyenne. C'est ainsi que l'échelle du QI est établie.

Alors que cet effet est présent chez les médecins, il est aussi présent chez les patients. «Faire vos recherches» n'est pas la même chose que passer quatre ans en faculté de médecine, trois autres années en internat, et continuer à se tenir au courant des développements en médecine à travers divers cours de formation continue. Nous ferions tous bien d'écouter mieux et de réaliser nos limites.

Le fait que le cousin de votre mère ait pris un extrait de laurier‑rose et se soit senti beaucoup mieux pour des symptômes similaires aux vôtres est intéressant. Que l'extrait de laurier‑rose les ait aidés à surmonter leur maladie, qu'il y ait eu un effet placebo, ou qu'ils allaient simplement guérir de toute façon, indépendamment de ce qu'ils ont pris, reste sujet à débat.

La vraie sagesse

J'ai déjà parlé de sagesse, et je voudrais conclure sur ce point. La vraie sagesse consiste à reconnaître que la guérison vient de Dieu. Psaumes 103:3 dit de Dieu : «Qui pardonne toutes tes iniquités ; qui guérit toutes tes maladies.»

La guérison ne vient pas des antibiotiques ou de la chimiothérapie. Elle ne vient pas de la prise des bons compléments ni même d'une alimentation saine. La guérison vient parce que Dieu nous touche, jusque dans les plus petites parties de nos cellules et de notre système immunitaire, et rend les choses entières à nouveau.

Je crois que parfois Il agit par la médecine, mais d'autres fois Il agit par la prière efficace et fervente des hommes et des femmes justes. (Jacques 5:16)

Avec toute notre connaissance, il est facile de nous gonfler d'orgueil et de croire que nous n'avons besoin de personne. Nous vivons dans un monde foisonnant de connaissances et dans un monde où la sagesse a été reléguée au second plan.

Nous devons choisir la source de notre information avec soin et réaliser que nous ne savons pas tout. Peut‑être que la raison pour laquelle la crainte de l'Éternel est le commencement de la sagesse est qu'elle est la première étape pour mettre de côté notre orgueil et réaliser que nous sommes une petite partie de la Création. Ce n'est qu'alors que nous pouvons humblement écouter, apprendre et recevoir la guérison.

Dirk scanned the sanctuary, trying to be discreet and yet utterly failing as he twisted and turned in his seat. He was intent on locating Brother Silas before the service began. Every Sunday morning, he would crane his neck in search of the hoary head of the fellowship’s oldest member, and every time his mother would cast Dirk that glance that meant, “Sit still and look forward.”

This morning, he didn’t have to even look behind him. Two rows from the front of the auditorium, Dirk spotted Brother Silas’ white hair and his black vest. To Dirk, it was a very special vest. In the pocket of that vest was something very important. In that vest pocket, there were mints. Lifesavers, to be exact. And all a little boy had to do to get one of those mints was to go up to Brother Silas after church service and politely ask to have one. And then, Brother Silas would smile, reach into the inner pocket, draw out a mint, and hand it to the little boy.

That was why Dirk diligently searched the church house to find Brother Silas’ whereabouts - so he would know where to go to get one of those mints. This Sunday was no different, and as soon as the last Amen was said, a swarm of young boys and girls began to cluster around Brother Silas like chickadees at a birdfeeder. Brother Silas genially doled out his mints in turn, all while continuing to chat with the men. When Dirk’s turn came, he dutifully said, “Thank you,” without even thinking what he said.

Dirk didn’t lose any time eating that mint, and before he knew it, the mint was gone and he could go on with his afternoon and with the rest of the week.

That Thursday, the phone rang, and when his mother picked it up, Dirk could tell that it was a recorded message announcing something because his mother only listened instead of holding up her end of the conversation. He didn’t think much of it until later in the evening when he overheard his parents discuss the message.

“What hospital did they say Brother Silas is in? Did they say how long they expect him to stay? Maybe we should make a visit,” Mother said.

“I think it would be worthwhile for us to pay him a visit,” replied Father.

“Will he be in church on Sunday?” interjected Dirk, stopping the travels of his tractor in his concern to hear the answer.

“No, I think it will be quite a while till he’ll feel able to be at church again. He’s very sick, Dirk,” Father said. Neither his father nor his mother expected the response that this answer caused. Dirk started crying, and at first, they were touched that he would be so compassionate about Brother Silas. And then Dirk started fussing.

“But what about my mint? If Brother Silas isn’t at church, I won’t get my mint! He just has to be at church!” He would have gone on and on in this way if his parents had let him.

“Why Dirk Phillips, first of all, we do not go to church services so that you can get a mint. We go to church services to worship God. Furthermore, you should be concerned about Brother Silas, not about whether you will get a mint or not. How would you like it if your friends were only concerned about something you gave them, without considering how you are doing?” “I’m sorry. I didn’t think about it like that,” Dirk sniveled, using his sleeve as a handkerchief.

“Can you think of anyone in the Bible who complained when they didn’t get what they wanted?” Mother inquired. No one came to Dirk’s mind, although he was sure that there were plenty of examples in the Bible. “The Israelites, Dirk. They often complained and it did not please God,” she prompted.

Father then asked Dirk to read through Numbers 11 and copy down the sentences that showed ungratefulness and how God felt about it. His parents then assured Dirk that they would look into visiting Brother Silas. They suggested planning to pick up a bag of mints on their way, just for Brother Silas.

When the day came to visit Brother Silas, Father took his son into the store to select a bag of mints. “Did you ever stop to think how many times Brother Silas has to do this to keep his pockets well lined with mints for all you children?” he asked Dirk, whose eyes grew wide at this little revelation.

“No, I never did. But he probably had to buy a whole bag every week! There’s a lot of us children at church.”

It was a full month before Brother Silas felt well enough to attend church services again. When he did, Dirk’s eyes lit up at the sight. At the close of the service, Dirk hung back for a while before approaching him. To be honest, he felt a little shy. But as he watched the other children receive their mints and he saw the unmistakable twinkle in Brother Silas’ eyes as he doled them out, Dirk grew more confident. He, too, joined the throng.

“I’m glad you’re feeling better, Brother Silas. I missed seeing you,” Dirk confided as he looked up into the face of the kindly gentleman.

“I am, too! It is very nice to be back. I quite missed being here,” replied Brother Silas, placing his hand gently on Dirk’s shoulder as they spoke. He then reached into his vest pocket and pulled out a mint. A Lifesaver, to be exact. And this time, when Dirk gave his thanks, it was with the feeling of gratitude and not just the words of it.

Dirk het die heiligdom geskandeer, probeer om diskreet te wees en tog heeltemal gefaal terwyl hy in sy sitplek gedraai en gedraai het. Hy was daarop gemik om Broer Silas te vind voordat die eredienst begin het. Elke Sondagoggend sou hy sy nek rek om die grys kop van die gemeente se oudste lid te soek, en elke keer sou sy moeder vir Dirk daardie kyk gee wat beteken het: “Sit stil en kyk vorentoe.”

Vandag het hy nie eens agter hom hoef te kyk nie. Twee rye voor in die saal het Dirk Broer Silas se wit hare en sy swart baadjie raakgesien. Vir Dirk was dit ’n baie spesiale baadjie. In die sak van daardie baadjie was iets baie belangrik. In daardie baadjiesak was pepermuntjies. Lifesavers, om presies te wees. En al wat ’n seuntjie moes doen om een van daardie pepermuntjies te kry, was om na die eredienst by Broer Silas op te gaan en beleefd te vra of hy een kon kry. En toe sou Broer Silas glimlag, in die binnesak grawe, ’n pepermuntjie uittrek en dit aan die seuntjie oorhandig.

Dit is waarom Dirk ywerig die kerkgebou deursoek het om uit te vind waar Broer Silas was—sodat hy sou weet waarheen om te gaan om een van daardie pepermuntjies te kry. Hierdie Sondag was geen uitsondering nie, en sodra die laaste Amen gesê is, het ’n trop jong seuntjies en dogtertjies om Broer Silas begin saamdrom soos voëltjies by ’n voersilo. Broer Silas het sy pepermuntjies vriendelik een-vir-een uitgedeel, en het terselfdertyd voortgegaan om met die mans te gesels. Toe dit Dirk se beurt was, het hy pligsgetrou gesê: “Dankie,” sonder om eers te dink oor wat hy gesê het.

Dirk het geen tyd verloor om daardie pepermuntjie te eet nie, en voor hy dit geweet het, was die pepermuntjie weg en kon hy met sy middag voortgaan en met die res van die week.

Daardie Donderdag het die telefoon gelui, en toe sy moeder dit opneem, kon Dirk sien dat dit ’n opgeneemde boodskap was wat iets aangekondig het, omdat sy moeder net geluister het in plaas daarvan om haar deel van die gesprek te voer. Hy het nie baie daaraan gedink nie totdat later daardie aand toe hy oorhoor sy ouers die boodskap bespreek het.

“Watter hospitaal het hulle gesê is Broer Silas in? Het hulle gesê hoe lank hulle verwag hy sal bly? Miskien moet ons hom gaan besoek,” het Ma gesê.

“Ek dink dit sal vir ons sinvol wees om hom te gaan besoek,” het Pa geantwoord.

“Sal hy Sondag by die kerk wees?” het Dirk ingegrap en die reis van sy trok gestop omdat hy die antwoord wil hoor.

“Nee, ek dink dit sal ’n rukkie wees voordat hy weer in staat sal wees om by die kerk te wees. Hy is baie siek, Dirk,” het Pa gesê. Nie sy pa of sy ma het die reaksie verwag wat hierdie antwoord veroorsaak het nie. Dirk het begin huil, en aanvanklik was hulle geroer dat hy so medegevoel sou hê oor Broer Silas. En toe het Dirk begin kerm.

“Maar wat van my pepermunt? As Broer Silas nie by die kerk is nie, sal ek nie my pepermunt kry nie! Hy moet net by die kerk wees!” Hy sou so aangegaan het as sy ouers hom laat sou hê.

“Waarom Dirk Phillips, in die eerste plek gaan ons nie na kerkdienste sodat jy ’n pepermunt kan kry nie. Ons gaan na kerkdienste om God te aanbid. Verder behoort jy bekommerd te wees oor Broer Silas, nie oor of jy ’n pepermunt kry of nie. Hoe sou jy daarvan hou as jou vriende net omgee oor iets wat jy hulle gegee het, sonder om te oorweeg hoe dit met jou gaan?” “Ek’s jammer. Ek het nie so gedink nie,” het Dirk gesniffel en sy mou as ’n sakdoek gebruik.

“Kan jy aan enigiemand in die Bybel dink wat gekla het toe hulle nie gekry het wat hulle wou hê nie?” het Ma gevra. Niemand het by Dirk op die oomblik opgeklink nie, alhoewel hy seker was dat daar talle voorbeelde in die Bybel was. “Die Israeliete, Dirk. Hulle het dikwels gekla en dit het nie God behaag nie,” het sy aangestoot.

Pa het toe vir Dirk gevra om Numeri 11 deur te lees en die sinne neer te skryf wat ondankbaarheid en hoe God daaroor gevoel het, getoon het. Sy ouers het Dirk toe verseker dat hulle sal kyk na ’n besoek aan Broer Silas. Hulle het voorgestel om op pad ’n sak pepermuntjies te koop, net vir Broer Silas.

Toe die dag aangebreek het om Broer Silas te besoek, het Pa sy seun in die winkel geneem om ’n sak pepermuntjies te kies. “Het jy al ooit stilgestaan en gedink hoeveel keer Broer Silas dit moet doen om sy sakke mooi vol pepermuntjies te hou vir julle kinders?” het hy vir Dirk gevra, wie se oë groot geword het oor hierdie klein onthulling.

“Nee, ek het nooit daaraan gedink nie. Maar hy moes waarskynlik elke week ’n hele sak koop! Daar is baie van ons kinders by die kerk.”

Dit was ’n volle maand voordat Broer Silas weer goed genoeg gevoel het om kerkbyeenkomste by te woon. Toe hy dit doen, het Dirk se oë by die gesig opgelaat. Aan die einde van die diens het Dirk vir ’n rukkie agtergebly voordat hy na hom toe gestap het. Om eerlik te wees, het hy ’n bietjie skaam gevoel. Maar terwyl hy die ander kinders sien hul pepermuntjies ontvang en die onmiskenbare glinster in Broer Silas se oë sien terwyl hy dit uitdeel, het Dirk meer selfvertroue gekry. Hy het ook by die skare aangesluit.

“Ek is bly jy voel beter, Broer Silas. Ek het jou gemis om jou te sien,” het Dirk toevertrou terwyl hy in die gesig van die vriendelike heer opkyk.

“Ek ook! Dit is baie lekker om terug te wees. Ek het dit regtig gemis om hier te wees,” het Broer Silas geantwoord en sy hand saggies op Dirk se skouer gesit terwyl hulle gesels het. Hy het toe in sy baadjiesak ingegrawe en ’n pepermuntjie uittrek. ’n Lifesaver, om presies te wees. En hierdie keer, toe Dirk sy dank uitspreek, was dit met die gevoel van dankbaarheid en nie net die woorde daarvan nie.

City of God, how broad and far
outspread thy walls sublime!

of every age and clime:

one King omnipotent.

How purely hath thy speech come down
from man's primaeval youth!
How grandly hath thine empire grown
of freedom, love, and truth!

with never-fainting ray!

to meet the dawning day!

in vain the drifting sands:
unharmed upon the eternal Rock
the eternal city stands.

'Tis winter now; the fallen snow
has left the heavens all coldly clear;
through leafless boughs, the sharp winds blow,
and all the earth lies dead and drear.

And yet God's love is not withdrawn;
his life within the keen air breathes;
his beauty paints the crimson dawn,
and clothes each branch with glittering wreaths.

And though abroad the sharp winds blow,
and skies are chill, and frosts are keen,
home closer draws her circle now,
and warmer glows her light within.

O God, you give the winter's cold,
as well as summer's joyous rays,
you warmly in your love enfold,
and keep us through life's wintry days.

Dirk scanned the sanctuary, trying to be discreet and yet utterly failing as he twisted and turned in his seat. He was intent on locating Brother Silas before the service began. Every Sunday morning, he would crane his neck in search of the hoary head of the fellowship’s oldest member, and every time his mother would cast Dirk that glance that meant, “Sit still and look forward.”

This morning, he didn’t have to even look behind him. Two rows from the front of the auditorium, Dirk spotted Brother Silas’ white hair and his black vest. To Dirk, it was a very special vest. In the pocket of that vest was something very important. In that vest pocket, there were mints. Lifesavers, to be exact. And all a little boy had to do to get one of those mints was to go up to Brother Silas after church service and politely ask to have one. And then, Brother Silas would smile, reach into the inner pocket, draw out a mint, and hand it to the little boy.

That was why Dirk diligently searched the church house to find Brother Silas’ whereabouts - so he would know where to go to get one of those mints. This Sunday was no different, and as soon as the last Amen was said, a swarm of young boys and girls began to cluster around Brother Silas like chickadees at a birdfeeder. Brother Silas genially doled out his mints in turn, all while continuing to chat with the men. When Dirk’s turn came, he dutifully said, “Thank you,” without even thinking what he said.

Dirk didn’t lose any time eating that mint, and before he knew it, the mint was gone and he could go on with his afternoon and with the rest of the week.

That Thursday, the phone rang, and when his mother picked it up, Dirk could tell that it was a recorded message announcing something because his mother only listened instead of holding up her end of the conversation. He didn’t think much of it until later in the evening when he overheard his parents discuss the message.

“What hospital did they say Brother Silas is in? Did they say how long they expect him to stay? Maybe we should make a visit,” Mother said.

“I think it would be worthwhile for us to pay him a visit,” replied Father.

“Will he be in church on Sunday?” interjected Dirk, stopping the travels of his tractor in his concern to hear the answer.

“No, I think it will be quite a while till he’ll feel able to be at church again. He’s very sick, Dirk,” Father said. Neither his father nor his mother expected the response that this answer caused. Dirk started crying, and at first, they were touched that he would be so compassionate about Brother Silas. And then Dirk started fussing.

“But what about my mint? If Brother Silas isn’t at church, I won’t get my mint! He just has to be at church!” He would have gone on and on in this way if his parents had let him.

“Why Dirk Phillips, first of all, we do not go to church services so that you can get a mint. We go to church services to worship God. Furthermore, you should be concerned about Brother Silas, not about whether you will get a mint or not. How would you like it if your friends were only concerned about something you gave them, without considering how you are doing?” “I’m sorry. I didn’t think about it like that,” Dirk sniveled, using his sleeve as a handkerchief.

“Can you think of anyone in the Bible who complained when they didn’t get what they wanted?” Mother inquired. No one came to Dirk’s mind, although he was sure that there were plenty of examples in the Bible. “The Israelites, Dirk. They often complained and it did not please God,” she prompted.

Father then asked Dirk to read through Numbers 11 and copy down the sentences that showed ungratefulness and how God felt about it. His parents then assured Dirk that they would look into visiting Brother Silas. They suggested planning to pick up a bag of mints on their way, just for Brother Silas.

When the day came to visit Brother Silas, Father took his son into the store to select a bag of mints. “Did you ever stop to think how many times Brother Silas has to do this to keep his pockets well lined with mints for all you children?” he asked Dirk, whose eyes grew wide at this little revelation.

“No, I never did. But he probably had to buy a whole bag every week! There’s a lot of us children at church.”

It was a full month before Brother Silas felt well enough to attend church services again. When he did, Dirk’s eyes lit up at the sight. At the close of the service, Dirk hung back for a while before approaching him. To be honest, he felt a little shy. But as he watched the other children receive their mints and he saw the unmistakable twinkle in Brother Silas’ eyes as he doled them out, Dirk grew more confident. He, too, joined the throng.

“I’m glad you’re feeling better, Brother Silas. I missed seeing you,” Dirk confided as he looked up into the face of the kindly gentleman.

“I am, too! It is very nice to be back. I quite missed being here,” replied Brother Silas, placing his hand gently on Dirk’s shoulder as they spoke. He then reached into his vest pocket and pulled out a mint. A Lifesaver, to be exact. And this time, when Dirk gave his thanks, it was with the feeling of gratitude and not just the words of it.
